questions.question: Expand the following expressions using the expand command in Maple: (i) (x + y)³ (ii) cos(x + y) + sin(x − y) (iii) (2a − b)² + (a + 3b)² (iv) eˣ(x + y) − eˣ(x − y) (v) (x + 2)(x − 3) (vi) sqrt(x + y)
questions.answer:
(i) x³ + 3x²y + 3xy² + y³
(ii) cos(x)cos(y) − sin(x)sin(y) + sin(x)cos(y) − cos(x)sin(y)
(iii) 5a² + 2ab + 10b²
(iv) 2eˣy
(v) x² − x − 6
(vi) √(x + y) — unchanged
questions.explanation: expand distributes products/powers and applies sum formulae: binomial theorem in (i); addition formulae cos(x+y) and sin(x−y) in (ii); (iii) (4a²−4ab+b²)+(a²+6ab+9b²); (iv) eˣ[(x+y)−(x−y)] = 2yeˣ; (vi) a sum under a radical has no expansion rule, so Maple returns it as is.

questions.question: Use the factor command in Maple to factorize: (i) x³ − 8 (ii) x⁴ − y⁴ (iii) x² − 4 (iv) 3x³ + 12x² − 15x (v) 2x² + 6xy + 4y² (vi) x² + 4x + 4
questions.explanation: factor reverses expansion over the rationals: (i) difference of cubes a³−b³; (ii) difference of squares applied twice; (iv) take 3x common then split x²+4x−5; (v) take 2 common then split x²+3xy+2y²; (vi) perfect square trinomial.

questions.question: Simplify using the simplify command in Maple: (i) (x²+2x+1)/(x+1) (ii) (x³−x²−x+1)/(x²+1) (iii) sin(x)² + cos(x)² (iv) (3x²+2x−1)/(x²+1)
questions.explanation: (i) numerator = (x+1)², one factor cancels; (ii) numerator = x²(x−1)−(x−1) = (x−1)(x²−1) = (x−1)²(x+1), nothing cancels with x²+1; (iii) Pythagorean identity; (iv) numerator (3x−1)(x+1) shares no factor with x²+1.

questions.question: Evaluate the numerical value of sin(π/6) using the evalf command in Maple.
questions.explanation: sin(Pi/6) stays exact (= 1/2) symbolically; evalf forces floating-point evaluation, giving 0.5.

questions.question: Find the inverse of the matrix A := Matrix(2, [1, 2, 3, 4]) using the Matrix Inverse command in Maple. (Run with(LinearAlgebra): first.)
questions.explanation: A = [[1,2],[3,4]]; det A = 1·4 − 2·3 = −2; A¹ = (1/det)·[[4,−2],[−3,1]]. Command: MatrixInverse(A).

questions.question: Find the transpose of the matrix B := Matrix(2, 3, [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]) using the Transpose command in Maple. (Run with(LinearAlgebra): first.)
questions.explanation: B is 2×3 = [[1,2,3],[4,5,6]]; Transpose swaps rows and columns giving a 3×2 matrix. Command: Transpose(B).

questions.question: Perform matrix multiplication for matrices A := Matrix(2, [1, 2, 3, 4]) and B := Matrix(2, [5, 6, 7, 8]) using the command in Maple. (Run with(LinearAlgebra): first.)
questions.explanation: Row-by-column products: (1,1)=1·5+2·7=19; (1,2)=1·6+2·8=22; (2,1)=3·5+4·7=43; (2,2)=3·6+4·8=50. Command: A.B

questions.question: Plot the functions f(x) = x² and g(x) = 2x − 1 on the same graph in the range [−5, 5].
questions.answer: Maple command: plot([x^2, 2*x-1], x = -5..5); — a parabola through the origin together with a straight line of slope 2, tangent to it at (1, 1). See the generated graph in the solution notes.
questions.explanation: plot accepts a list of expressions to draw several curves in one window; x² = 2x−1 ⇒ (x−1)² = 0, so the line touches the parabola only at x = 1.

questions.question: Generate a graph that includes the functions h(x) = sin(x) and k(x) = cos(x) in the interval [0, 2π].
questions.answer: Maple command: plot([sin(x), cos(x)], x = 0..2*Pi); — two unit-amplitude waves phase-shifted by π/2: sin starts at 0 and cos starts at 1; they cross at x = π/4 and x = 5π/4.
questions.explanation: Both curves have amplitude 1 and period 2π; cos(x) = sin(x + π/2), which is the visible horizontal shift between the two waves.

questions.question: Plot the parametric curves x(t) = cos(2t) and y(t) = sin(3t) for t in the range [−2π, 2π].
questions.answer: Maple command: plot([cos(2*t), sin(3*t), t = -2*Pi..2*Pi]); — a closed Lissajous figure inside the square [−1,1]×[−1,1].
questions.explanation: The third list entry makes Maple plot parametrically (x(t), y(t)); frequency ratio 2:3 with periods dividing 4π makes the curve close on itself.

questions.question: Identify the domain and range of the functions through the following graphs (figure below): (i) parabola y = x² with vertex at the origin, opening upward  (ii) straight line y = x through the origin  (iii) curve y = √x starting at the origin  (iv) curve y = 1/x² (two branches above the x-axis)  (v) curve y = 1/x (branches in the first and third quadrants).
questions.answer:
(i) Domain = ℝ; Range = {y ∈ ℝ : y ≥ 0}
(ii) Domain = ℝ; Range = ℝ
(iii) Domain = {x ∈ ℝ : x ≥ 0}; Range = {y ∈ ℝ : y ≥ 0}
(iv) Domain = {x ∈ ℝ : x ≠ 0}; Range = {y ∈ ℝ : y > 0}
(v) Domain = {x ∈ ℝ : x ≠ 0}; Range = {y ∈ ℝ : y ≠ 0}
questions.explanation: Domain = horizontal extent of the curve, range = vertical extent: (i) the parabola spans all x and its lowest point is y = 0; (ii) the line covers the whole plane; (iii) √x exists only for x ≥ 0 and starts at y = 0; (iv) a gap at x = 0 and both branches lie strictly above the x-axis; (v) a gap at x = 0 and y = 0 is never attained.

questions.question: If f(x) = 5x + 2 and g(x) = 2x² − 3, then find: (i) fog  (ii) gof  (iii) fof  (iv) gog
questions.explanation: Substitute the inner function into the outer one: (i) 5(2x²−3)+2; (ii) 2(5x+2)²−3 = 2(25x²+20x+4)−3; (iii) 5(5x+2)+2; (iv) 2(2x²−3)²−3 = 2(4x⁴−12x²+9)−3.

questions.question: If f(x) = 2x and g(x) = x + 1, then find fog(x) for x = −5.
questions.explanation: (fog)(x) = f(g(x)) = 2(x + 1) = 2x + 2; at x = −5: 2(−5) + 2 = −8.

questions.question: If f(x) = x + 3 and g(x) = x², then find gof(x) for x = 1.
If c(x) = cos x and p(x) = x³ + 1, then find poc(x).
questions.explanation: (poc)(x) = p(c(x)) = (cos x)³ + 1 = cos³x + 1.

questions.question: If f(x) = x + 2 and g(x) = 3x − 2, then find (fog)⁻¹ and (gof)⁻¹, and show that (gof)⁻¹ = f⁻¹og⁻¹.
questions.explanation: fog(x) = (3x−2)+2 = 3x and gof(x) = 3(x+2)−2 = 3x+4; invert each by solving y = … for x. The inverse of a composition reverses the order of the factors, which the f⁻¹og⁻¹ computation confirms.

questions.question: If h(x) = x − 3 and k(x) = 2x + 5, then verify: (i) hok ≠ koh  (ii) (hok)⁻¹ = k⁻¹oh⁻¹  (iii) (koh)⁻¹ = h⁻¹ok⁻¹
questions.answer:
(i) hok = 2x + 2 while koh = 2x − 1 ⇒ hok ≠ koh
(ii) (hok)⁻¹ = (x − 2)/2 = k⁻¹(h⁻¹(x)) — verified
(iii) (koh)⁻¹ = (x + 1)/2 = h⁻¹(k⁻¹(x)) — verified
questions.explanation: hok(x) = (2x+5)−3 = 2x+2 and koh(x) = 2(x−3)+5 = 2x−1, so the two orders differ. With h⁻¹(x) = x+3 and k⁻¹(x) = (x−5)/2: k⁻¹oh⁻¹ = ((x+3)−5)/2 = (x−2)/2 and h⁻¹ok⁻¹ = (x−5)/2+3 = (x+1)/2, matching the inverses obtained directly from hok and koh.

questions.question: Which of the following are algebraic, exponential, logarithmic, trigonometric, inverse trigonometric, hyperbolic and inverse hyperbolic functions: (i) y = x² + 5x + 6  (ii) f(x) = tan⁻¹x  (iii) y = 2^(x+1)  (iv) y = log₅(x + 2)  (v) f(x) = 3sin x  (vi) y = a^(sin x)  (vii) f(x) = (x² + 5x + 7)/(x + 9)  (viii) f(x) = sin x / sec x  (ix) y = logₙ sin x  (x) f(x) = cosec⁻¹√(x² − 1)  (xi) f(x) = tan(sin x)  (xii) y = x/(x + 3)  (xiii) f(x) = sinh x  (xiv) y = ln cosh x  (xv) y = tanh⁻¹x  (xvi) y = cos⁻¹(ln x)
questions.answer:
(i) algebraic
(ii) inverse trigonometric
(iii) exponential
(iv) logarithmic
(v) trigonometric
(vi) exponential
(vii) algebraic
(viii) trigonometric
(ix) logarithmic
(x) inverse trigonometric
(xi) trigonometric
(xii) algebraic
(xiii) hyperbolic
(xiv) logarithmic
(xv) inverse hyperbolic
(xvi) inverse trigonometric
questions.explanation: Classify by the dominant operation: polynomials and ratios of polynomials are algebraic; a variable exponent with constant base is exponential ((iii), (vi)); a log of an expression is logarithmic ((iv), (ix), (xiv)); sin/cos/tan/sec compositions are trigonometric ((v), (viii), (xi)); tan⁻¹, cosec⁻¹, cos⁻¹ are inverse trigonometric ((ii), (x), (xvi)); sinh is hyperbolic ((xiii)); tanh⁻¹ is inverse hyperbolic ((xv)).

questions.question: Identify whether y is the explicit or implicit function of the independent variable x: (i) xy² + 5xy + 7 = 0  (ii) y = 3x² − 3x + 5  (iii) yx² + y²x = 3 − 5y  (iv) x² + xy² = 2 + 3xy  (v) y = (x + 3)/(x² + 5)  (vi) x/y = 3x³y − 5
questions.answer:
(i) implicit function
(ii) explicit function
(iii) implicit function
(iv) implicit function
(v) explicit function
(vi) implicit function
questions.explanation: y is explicit only when the equation is already solved for y in terms of x alone ((ii), (v)); wherever y remains mixed with x or un-isolated ((i), (iii), (iv), (vi)) the function is implicit.

questions.question: Draw the graph of the following functions: (i) f(x) = e^(3x)  (ii) f(x) = 3log₁₀x  (iii) y = √(36 − x²)  (iv) x²/16 + y²/25 = 1
questions.answer: See the four plotted curves in the figure: (i) exponential through (0, 1) hugging y = 0 on the left; (ii) log curve for x > 0 crossing the x-axis at 1; (iii) upper half of the circle centre O radius 6; (iv) ellipse with semi-axes 4 (x) and 5 (y).
questions.explanation: (iii) squaring gives x² + y² = 36 with y ≥ 0 — a semicircle; (iv) is the standard ellipse x²/4² + y²/5² = 1. MAPLE: plot(exp(3*x), x=-1..1.2); plot(3*log10(x), x=0..9); plot(sqrt(36-x^2), x=-6..6); implicitplot(x^2/16+y^2/25=1, ...).

questions.question: Draw the graph of the parametric equations of function x = at², y = 2at, when a = 4 and −5 ≤ t ≤ 5.
questions.answer: A right-opening parabola y² = 16x from (100, −40) through the vertex (0, 0) to (100, 40) — see figure.
questions.explanation: With a = 4: x = 4t², y = 8t; eliminating t (t = y/8) gives x = y²/16, i.e. y² = 16x. MAPLE: plot([4*t^2, 8*t, t = -5..5]);

questions.question: Draw the graph of the parametric equations of function x = a sec θ, y = b tan θ, when a = 3, b = 4 and −π ≤ θ ≤ π.
questions.answer: The hyperbola x²/9 − y²/16 = 1: two branches opening left/right with vertices (±3, 0) and asymptotes y = ±(4/3)x — see figure.
questions.explanation: sec²θ − tan²θ = 1 turns the parametrisation into (x/3)² − (y/4)² = 1. θ ∈ (−π/2, π/2) traces the right branch, the remaining intervals the left branch. MAPLE: plot([3*sec(t), 4*tan(t), t = -Pi..Pi], discont = true);

questions.question: Draw the graph of f(x) = x² for x ≤ 1 and f(x) = 2x for x > 1.
questions.answer: Parabola y = x² up to the closed point (1, 1), then the line y = 2x starting from the open point (1, 2) — a jump of 1 at x = 1; see figure.
questions.explanation: Each piece is drawn on its own interval; at x = 1 the first piece gives 1 (included) while the second piece would give 2 (excluded), so the curve breaks there. MAPLE: plot(piecewise(x <= 1, x^2, 2*x), x = -3..4);

questions.question: Solve the following: (i) [2, ∞) ∪ (3, 5)  (ii) [−1, 1] − (2, ∞)  (iii) (5, ∞) ∩ (−3, 6)  (iv) [3, 5] − (3, 5)  (v) [1, 10] ∩ [3, 11]  (vi) (−∞, 5) − (−∞, 3)
questions.explanation: Union keeps all points of either set, intersection the common points, and A − B deletes B from A: (i) (3,5) lies inside [2,∞); (ii) (2,∞) is disjoint from [−1,1]; (iv) only the endpoints survive; (vi) 3 itself is not removed. (The key prints open brackets in (i), (ii), (v) — those endpoints do belong.)

questions.question: Find the nth term and limit of the following sequences: (i) 1, 1/2, 1/4, 1/8, …  (ii) 1·2/3·4, 3·4/5·6, 5·6/7·8, …
questions.explanation: (i) each term halves, a geometric sequence with ratio 1/2 → 0; (ii) numerator is the pair-product (2n−1)(2n), denominator the next pair (2n+1)(2n+2); leading terms 4n²/4n² → 1.

questions.question: Find the limit of the following sequences whose nth terms are: (i) aₙ = (1+5n)/(7n)  (ii) aₙ = (3n−1)(n⁴−n) / [(n²+5)(n³−7)]  (iii) aₙ = (n+1)! / [n! − (n+1)!]
questions.explanation: (i) divide by n: (1/n+5)/7 → 5/7; (ii) ratio of leading terms 3n⁵/n⁵ = 3; (iii) n! − (n+1)! = n!(1−(n+1)) so aₙ = (n+1)/(−n) → −1.

questions.question: Find the limit of the function y = 5x/(x + 1) for x → ∞.
questions.explanation: Divide top and bottom by x: y = 5/(1 + 1/x) → 5/(1+0) = 5.

questions.question: Evaluate by using theorems on limits: (i) lim<sub>x→2</sub> (x⁵ + x² + x + 1)  (ii) lim<sub>x→5</sub> ((1+x)/x²)  (iii) lim<sub>x→1</sub> [(2x³ + 3x²)(x + 1)]  (iv) lim<sub>x→5</sub> {(x + 1) − (x² + 2x + 3)}
questions.explanation: Polynomials are continuous, so substitute: (i) 32+4+2+1; (ii) 6/25 (quotient theorem, denominator ≠ 0); (iii) (2+3)(2) by the product theorem; (iv) 6 − 38 by the difference theorem.

questions.question: Evaluate the limits: (i) lim<sub>x→1</sub> (x²+4)³  (ii) lim<sub>x→0</sub> 4/(x−4)  (iii) lim<sub>x→∞</sub> 5/(5x+10)  (iv) lim<sub>x→7</sub> (x²−49)/(x−7)  (v) lim<sub>x→0</sub> (√(x+3)−√3)/x  (vi) lim<sub>x→7</sub> (x−7)/(√x−√7)  (vii) lim<sub>x→0</sub> (1+x/3)^(5/x)  (viii) lim<sub>x→0</sub> (1+ax)^(a/x)  (ix) lim<sub>x→∞</sub> (1+p/x)^(px)  (x) lim<sub>x→∞</sub> (1−pq/x)^(x/p)  (xi) lim<sub>x→0</sub> (17^x−1)/x  (xii) lim<sub>h→0</sub> [(1+2h)^n−1]/(5h)  (xiii) lim<sub>x→0</sub> (2^x−4^x−8^x−1)/(x+2)  (xiv) lim<sub>x→0</sub> [(1+7x)/(1−9x)]^(1/x)  (xv) lim<sub>x→0</sub> (a^x−b^x)/x  (xvi) lim<sub>x→0</sub> (e^(−2x)−e^(−11x))/x  (xvii) lim<sub>x→0</sub> (3e^(−5x)−5e^(−2x)+2)/x  (xviii) lim<sub>x→0</sub> (1+3tan x)^(cot x)  (xix) lim<sub>x→2</sub> (x⁴−16)/(x³−8)  (xx) lim<sub>x→∞</sub> (2x−x²)/(3x²−4x+1)
questions.answer:
(i) 125
(ii) −1
(iii) 0
(iv) 14
(v) 1/(2√3)
(vi) 2√7
(vii) e^(5/3)
(viii) e^(a²)
(ix) e^(p²)
(x) e^(−q)
(xi) ln 17
(xii) 2n/5
(xiii) −1
(xiv) e^16
(xv) ln(a/b)
(xvi) 9
(xvii) −5
(xviii) e³
(xix) 8/3
(xx) −1/3
questions.explanation: Substitute where continuous ((i)–(iii), (xiii)); factor or rationalise the 0/0 forms ((iv) x+7; (v) conjugate gives 1/(√(x+3)+√3); (vi) √x+√7); use (1+u)^(1/u) → e for (vii)–(x), (xiv), (xviii); (a^x−1)/x → ln a for (xi), (xv), (xvi), (xvii); binomial expansion for (xii); factor (x−2) in (xix). (xx): leading terms −x²/3x² = −1/3 — the book key misprints −3.

questions.question: Evaluate the limits: (i) lim<sub>x→0</sub> a sin(ax)/x  (ii) lim<sub>x→0</sub> sin(√a·x)/(x/√a)  (iii) lim<sub>x→0</sub> (3cos x + 2tan x)³  (iv) lim<sub>x→0</sub> (3sin x − x³)/(2x)  (v) lim<sub>x→0</sub> sin(px)/sin(qx)  (vi) lim<sub>x→0</sub> (2π−x)sec(π−x)/(π/2)  (vii) lim<sub>x→0</sub> sin(x°)/x  (viii) lim<sub>x→0</sub> (1−cos mx)/(1−cos nx)  (ix) lim<sub>x→0</sub> (sin 3x sin 5x)/(7x²)
questions.explanation: Use sin(kx)/x → k and (1−cos kx)/x² → k²/2: (i) a·a; (ii) (√a·x)(√a/x); (iii) substitute (3·1+0)³; (iv) (3/2)(sin x/x) − x²/2; (v) px/qx; (vi) substitute: (2π)(sec π)(2/π) = −4; (vii) x° = (π/180)x rad; (viii) (m²x²/2)/(n²x²/2); (ix) (3·5)/7.

questions.question: Evaluate the limits: (i) lim<sub>x→0</sub> sin²(x/2)/(4x²)  (ii) lim<sub>x→∞</sub> x sin(1/x)  (iii) lim<sub>x→∞</sub> [√(x²+x+1) − x]  (iv) lim<sub>x→0</sub> (1−cos³x)/sin²x  (v) lim<sub>x→0</sub> (a^x+a^(−x)−2)/x²  (vi) lim<sub>x→0</sub> (6^x−3^x−2^x+1)/x²  (vii) lim<sub>x→3</sub> [x/(x+2) − 3/5]/(x−3)  (viii) lim<sub>y→4</sub> (y^(5/2)−16y^(1/2))/(y−4)  (ix) lim<sub>x→1</sub> (1/√x − 1)/(1−x)  (x) lim<sub>x→π</sub> (√(5+cos x)−2)/(π−x)  (xi) lim<sub>x→1</sub> x^(1/(x−1))  (xii) lim<sub>x→1</sub> (x²−√x)/(√x−1)  (xiii) lim<sub>x→π/4</sub> (√2−cos x−sin x)/(4x−π)²  (xiv) lim<sub>x→e</sub> (ln x−1)/(x−e)  (xv) lim<sub>x→2</sub> (x+1)sin(x−2)/(x²−4)
questions.explanation: (i) (x/2)²/4x²; (ii) h = 1/x gives sin h/h; (iii) conjugate gives (x+1)/(√(x²+x+1)+x); (iv) (1−cos x)(1+cos x+cos²x)/sin²x; (v) (a^(x/2)−a^(−x/2))²/x²; (vi) (2^x−1)(3^x−1)/x²; (vii) numerator = 2(x−3)/[5(x+2)]; (viii) √y(y+4); (ix) 1/[√x(1+√x)]; (x) numerator and its slope vanish at π; (xi) (1+h)^(1/h); (xii) u = √x gives u(u²+u+1); (xiii) x = π/4+h gives √2(1−cos h)/16h²; (xiv) slope of ln x at e; (xv) (x+1)/(x+2) · sin(x−2)/(x−2).

questions.question: Evaluate the following limits: (i) lim<sub>x→2⁺</sub> (x−2)/|x−2|  (ii) lim<sub>x→1⁻</sub> (x²+2x−3)/|x−1|  (iii) lim<sub>x→2</sub> (x²+4x−12)/|x−2|
questions.explanation: |x−a| = (x−a) on the right of a and −(x−a) on the left: (i) ratio 1; (ii) (x−1)(x+3)/[−(x−1)] = −(x+3) → −4; (iii) (x−2)(x+6)/|x−2| gives +8 from the right and −8 from the left, so the two-sided limit fails.

questions.question: Determine whether lim<sub>x→1</sub> f(x), lim<sub>x→2</sub> f(x), lim<sub>x→3</sub> f(x) and lim<sub>x→4</sub> f(x) exist when f(x) = 2x+1 (0 ≤ x < 2), x−7 (2 ≤ x < 4), x (4 ≤ x ≤ 6).
questions.answer: lim<sub>x→1</sub> f = 3 (exists); lim<sub>x→2</sub> f does not exist; lim<sub>x→3</sub> f = −4 (exists); lim<sub>x→4</sub> f does not exist
questions.explanation: At 1 and 3 the point lies inside a single piece (values 3 and −4); at 2 the one-sided limits are 5 and −5, and at 4 they are −3 and 4, so those limits do not exist.

questions.question: Test the continuity and discontinuity of: (i) f(x) = sin(x² + πx) + 7x² + x at x = 0  (ii) f(x) = (2 − cos 3x − cos 4x)/x at x = 0  (iii) f(x) = 7+3x (x < 1), 1−5x (x ≥ 1) at x = 1
questions.explanation: (i) f(0) = 0 = lim f; (ii) the limit exists (≈12.5x → 0) but f(0) is undefined (0/0 form), so f is discontinuous at 0; (iii) left limit 10 ≠ right limit and value −4 — a jump.

questions.question: Determine whether the following functions are continuous at x = 2: (i) f(x) = (x²−4)/(x−2)  (ii) g(x) = (x²−4)/(x−2) for x ≠ 2, 3 for x = 2  (iii) h(x) = (x²−4)/(x−2) for x ≠ 2, 4 for x = 2
questions.explanation: (x²−4)/(x−2) = x+2 for x ≠ 2, so the limit at 2 is 4 in every case: (i) f(2) undefined; (ii) g(2) = 3 ≠ 4; (iii) h(2) = 4 = lim — only (iii) satisfies lim = value.

questions.question: Suppose f(x) = −x⁴ + 3 for x ≤ 2 and x² + 9 for x > 2. Is f continuous everywhere?
questions.answer: Continuous everywhere except at x = 2 (left/value −13 vs right 13 — a jump).
questions.explanation: Both pieces are polynomials, hence continuous on their intervals; at x = 2 the one-sided values −16+3 = −13 and 4+9 = 13 disagree, so continuity fails only there.

questions.question: Find the value of k if f(x) = sin(kx)/x for x ≠ 0 and 2 for x = 0 is continuous at x = 0.
questions.explanation: lim<sub>x→0</sub> sin(kx)/x = k must equal f(0) = 2.

questions.question: Find the value of k if f(x) = kx − 9 (x < 5), 9x − k (x > 5), 36 (x = 5) is continuous at x = 5.
questions.explanation: Left limit 5k−9 = 36 and right limit 45−k = 36 both give k = 9, so the three values agree.

questions.question: Find the values of m and n so that f is continuous at x = 3: (i) f(x) = mx (x < 3), n (x = 3), −2x+9 (x > 3)  (ii) f(x) = mx (x < 3), x² (x ≥ 3)
questions.explanation: (i) left 3m, right −6+9 = 3, value n ⇒ 3m = 3, n = 3; (ii) left 3m must equal right 9 ⇒ m = 3.

questions.question: If f(x) = [√(2x+5) − √(x+7)]/(x−2) for x ≠ 2 and k for x = 2, find k so that f is continuous at x = 2.
questions.explanation: Rationalising: numerator becomes (2x+5)−(x+7) = x−2, cancelling the denominator, so f(x) = 1/[√(2x+5)+√(x+7)] → 1/(3+3) = 1/6; continuity needs f(2) = k = 1/6.

questions.question: Choose the correct answer: (i) f(x) = x is called  (ii) the set {x | x ∈ ℜ} as an interval  (iii) [3,5] − (3,5)  (iv) R = {(x,y) | x,y ∈ ℜ and y = 5}  (v) f(x) = x/|x|, x ≠ 0  (vi) f(x) = 4ˣ ⇒ f(x+1) − f(x)  (vii) limit of aₙ = 1/2ₙ  (viii) lim<sub>x→0</sub> sin(ax)/x  (ix) lim<sub>x→3</sub> (x²−9)/(x−3)  (x) f : [−1,4] → ℜ, f(x) = x², f(−3)  (xi) lim<sub>h→0</sub> sin(π/2+h)  (xii) lim<sub>x→0</sub> e^(−1/x)  (xiii) lim<sub>x→c</sub> f(x) exists iff  (xiv) lim<sub>n→∞</sub> (1+1/n)^(−7n)  (xv) limit of 1, π⁻¹, π⁻², …  (xvi) which represents a parametric function  (xvii) g(x) = 3x+2, g(f(x)) = x ⇒ f(2)  (xviii) k making x/tan 3x (x ≠ 0), k (x = 0) continuous  (xix) lim<sub>x→0</sub> (1−x)^(1/x)  (xx) sech⁻¹x equals

questions.question: If h(x) = √(x²+3) and k(x) = x² − 2, find: (i) hok(x)  (ii) koh  (iii) hoh  (iv) kok
questions.explanation: Substitute the inner function: (i) √((x²−2)²+3); (ii) (√(x²+3))²−2; (iii) √((√(x²+3))²+3); (iv) (x²−2)²−2.

questions.question: If f(x) = x + 3 and g(x) = x², find gof(x) for x = 1.
f(x) = (x+1)/3 and g(x) = 3x + 5 are given; verify that (i) (fog)⁻¹ = g⁻¹of⁻¹  (ii) (gof)⁻¹ = f⁻¹og⁻¹
questions.answer:
(i) fog = x+2 ⇒ (fog)⁻¹ = x−2 = g⁻¹(f⁻¹(x)) — verified
(ii) gof = x+6 ⇒ (gof)⁻¹ = x−6 = f⁻¹(g⁻¹(x)) — verified
questions.explanation: f⁻¹(x) = 3x−1 and g⁻¹(x) = (x−5)/3; then g⁻¹of⁻¹ = (3x−1−5)/3 = x−2 and f⁻¹og⁻¹ = 3(x−5)/3−1 = x−6, matching the direct inverses of fog = x+2 and gof = x+6.

questions.question: Recognize as explicit or implicit functions and express the implicit ones explicitly where possible: (i) x³ + 2xy = 5x² − 3y  (ii) 3y = 5x² − 3x  (iii) x²y + xy = 5y − 3  (iv) 2x²y − xy = 5 + 3xy
questions.answer:
(i) implicit; y = (5x² − x³)/(2x+3)
(ii) explicit; y = (5x² − 3x)/3
(iii) implicit; y = −3/(x² + x − 5)
(iv) implicit; y = 5/[2x(x − 2)]
questions.explanation: Collect the y terms and divide: (i) y(2x+3) = 5x²−x³; (iii) y(x²+x−5) = −3; (iv) y(2x²−4x) = 5. (ii) is already solved for y. (The key misprints (iv) as 5/[2x(x−1)].)

questions.question: Show that the parametric equations x = a sec θ, y = b tan θ represent the equation x²/a² − y²/b² = 1.
questions.answer: x/a = sec θ and y/b = tan θ; since sec²θ − tan²θ = 1, (x/a)² − (y/b)² = 1, i.e. x²/a² − y²/b² = 1 — shown.
questions.explanation: Dividing each parametric equation by its constant isolates sec θ and tan θ, and the Pythagorean-type identity sec² − tan² = 1 eliminates θ.

questions.question: Draw and explain the graph of: (i) f(x) = e^(5x)  (ii) y = √(4 − x²)  (iii) x²/9 + y²/16 = 1
questions.answer: (i) exponential through (0,1), flat on the left, steep rise on the right; (ii) upper semicircle of radius 2; (iii) ellipse with semi-axes 3 (x) and 4 (y) — see figure.
questions.explanation: (ii) squaring gives x²+y² = 4 with y ≥ 0; (iii) is the standard ellipse x²/3² + y²/4² = 1.

questions.question: Draw the graph of the parametric equations x = at², y = 2at when a = 6 and −5 ≤ t ≤ 5.
questions.answer: Right-opening parabola y² = 24x from (150, −60) through (0,0) to (150, 60) — see figure.
questions.explanation: x = 6t², y = 12t ⇒ t = y/12 ⇒ x = y²/24, i.e. y² = 24x.

questions.question: Draw the graph of the parametric equations x = a sec θ, y = b tan θ when a = 4, b = 3 and −π ≤ θ ≤ π.
questions.answer: Hyperbola x²/16 − y²/9 = 1: branches opening left/right, vertices (±4, 0), asymptotes y = ±(3/4)x — see figure.
questions.explanation: sec²θ − tan²θ = 1 gives (x/4)² − (y/3)² = 1; the two θ-intervals around ±π/2 trace the left branch, the middle one the right branch.

questions.question: Solve the following: (i) [1, ∞) ∪ (2, 3)  (ii) [−1, 1] ∩ (2, ∞)  (iii) (4, ∞) ∩ (−3, 3)  (iv) [2, 3] − (2, 3)  (v) [1, 9] ∩ [3, 12]  (vi) (−∞, 7) − (−∞, 2)
questions.explanation: (i) (2,3) lies inside [1,∞); (ii) and (iii) the intervals do not overlap — empty set (the key misprints (iii) as (4,3)); (iv) removing the open middle leaves the endpoints (key misprints [2,3]); (v) common part 3..9; (vi) 2 itself is not removed.

questions.question: Find the limit of the sequence 1, 1/4, 1/16, 1/64, …
Find the limit of aₙ = −1 + (1/5)ⁿ.
questions.explanation: (1/5)ⁿ → 0, leaving −1.

questions.question: Find the limit of the function y = 1/x³ for x → ∞.
questions.explanation: The denominator grows without bound while the numerator stays 1.

questions.question: Evaluate: (i) lim<sub>x→3</sub> (x³ + x⁴ + x + 5)  (ii) lim<sub>x→7</sub> (1+x)/x₇  (iii) lim<sub>x→1</sub> [(2x⁴ + 3x³)(x + 3)]  (iv) lim<sub>x→3</sub> [(x+3) − (x³ + 5x + 5)]  (v) lim<sub>x→π/4</sub> (cosec²x − 2)/(cot x − 1)  (vi) lim<sub>x→π</sub> sin(π−x)/[π(π−x)]  (vii) lim<sub>x→0</sub> (1+2x)^(5/x)  (viii) lim<sub>x→0</sub> (3^(2x) − 1)/sin x
questions.explanation: (i)–(iv) substitute (polynomials are continuous); (v) cosec²x−2 = cot²x−1 = (cot x−1)(cot x+1); (vi) sin u/u → 1 with u = π−x; (vii) (1+u)^(1/u) → e with u = 2x, exponent 5/x = (1/u)·10; (viii) [(3^(2x)−1)/(2x)]·[2x/sin x] → ln 3 · 2.

questions.question: Determine whether the following are continuous at x = 3: (i) f(x) = (x²−9)/(x−3)  (ii) g(x) = (x²−9)/(x−3) for x ≠ 3, 5 for x = 3  (iii) h(x) = (x²−9)/(x−3) for x ≠ 3, 6 for x = 3
questions.explanation: For x ≠ 3 the expression equals x+3, so the limit at 3 is 6: (i) f(3) undefined; (ii) g(3) = 5 ≠ 6; (iii) h(3) = 6 = lim.

questions.question: If f(x) = 3x (x ≤ −2), x² − 1 (−2 < x < 2), 3 (x ≥ 2), discuss the continuity or discontinuity at x = 2 and x = −2.
questions.answer: Continuous at x = 2; discontinuous at x = −2.
questions.explanation: At 2: left limit x²−1 → 3 equals right limit and value 3; at −2: left limit and value 3(−2) = −6 but right limit x²−1 → 3 — a jump.

questions.question: Find the average rate of change of the function between the given values: (i) f(x) = x² + 4, a = 2, b = 2.3  (ii) f(x) = x³ − 4, a = 2, b = 2.3  (iii) f(x) = x³ − 8, a = 3, b = 2.5

Find the average rate of change: (i) the area of a circle A = πx² when the radius changes from a = 3 to b = 3.1 cm  (ii) the volume of a sphere V = (4/3)πx³ when the radius changes from a = 2 to b = 1.9 cm
The annual profit p of a small business is given by p(t) = 3t² + t + 1, where t ≥ 0 measures the years since 1995. Find the average rate of change of profit between t = 3 and t = 3.5.

A ball is thrown straight up with an initial velocity of 80 feet/second; its height after t seconds is h(t) = −16t² + 80t feet. Find the average velocity during the interval: (a) t = 2 to t = 2.1 s  (b) t = 2 to t = 2.01 s

Find by definition (ab-initio) the derivatives of: (i) f(x) = 2x  (ii) f(x) = 1 − √x  (iii) f(x) = 1/√x  (iv) f(x) = 3 − x²  (v) f(x) = x(x+1)  (vi) f(x) = x² − 3  (vii) f(x) = x³ + 5  (viii) f(x) = 4x² − 3x  (ix) f(x) = 1/(x+2)  (x) f(x) = 3/(2x+5)
questions.explanation: Using f′(x) = lim<sub>δx→0</sub> [f(x+δx) − f(x)]/δx: expand, cancel, and take the limit. E.g. (ix): [1/(x+δx+2) − 1/(x+2)]/δx = −1/[(x+δx+2)(x+2)] → −1/(x+2)². Roots are handled by rationalizing (multiply by the conjugate); fractions by combining over a common denominator. All ten results match the Answers key (printed p. 412).

questions.question: Find f′(x) using the definition of derivative: (i) f(x) = ³√(2x+1)  (ii) f(x) = (2x−1)^(−1/2)  (iii) f(x) = (6x+7)^(5/2)  (iv) f(x) = (3x−5)^(−3/2)
questions.explanation: First-principles limits with algebraic identities: (i) a³ − b³ = (a−b)(a²+ab+b²) on cube roots; (ii)/(iv) rationalization and a³−b³ on square roots; (iii) split u^(5/2) as u²√u and add-subtract a common term. Chain-rule checks: (5/2)(6x+7)^(3/2)·6 = 15(6x+7)^(3/2); (−3/2)(3x−5)^(−5/2)·3 = −9/[2(3x−5)^(5/2)]. All four match the key.

questions.question: Differentiate the following w.r.t. x: (i) 5x⁵  (ii) (7/9)x⁹  (iii) −25x^(−3/5)  (iv) 124√x  (v) (1/22)x²²  (vi) x^(−100)  (vii) 15³√x  (viii) 16·⁴√(x^(3/4))  (ix) −4/x^(3/4)  (x) 3/³√(x²)
questions.explanation: Power rule d/dx xₙ = n·x^(ₙ−¹) on each term after rewriting roots as fractional powers; e.g. (viii) 16·⁴√(x^(3/4)) = 16x^(3/16) → 3x^(−13/4).

questions.question: Differentiate the following w.r.t. x: (i) x⁵/(a²+b²) + x²/(a²−b²)  (ii) 2x + (1/2)x⁶  (iii) ³√(x²) + √x  (iv) (1/21)x²¹ + (1/22)x²²  (v) −(5/4)x^(−4/5) + (2/3)x^(−3/2)
questions.explanation: Term-by-term power rule; a and b are constants so 1/(a²+b²) etc. are constant coefficients.

questions.question: Differentiate the following w.r.t. x: (i) 2ax³ − x²/b + 6  (ii) x³ − (3/7)x^(7/3)  (iii) 5x^(3/5) − (1/7)x^(7/3)  (iv) x¹⁰ − 10x¹⁵  (v) 3³√(x²) − 4·⁴√x
questions.explanation: Power rule with constant parameters a, b; roots converted to fractional exponents first.

questions.question: Differentiate the following polynomial functions w.r.t. x: (i) p(x) = x³ − 3x² + 2x + 1  (ii) p(x) = x⁴ − 3x² + 2x − 3  (iii) p(x) = x⁶ − x⁴ + x³ + x  (iv) p(x) = 9x⁹ + 7x⁷ + (1/5)x⁵ − (1/4)x⁴ + x + 1
questions.explanation: Term-by-term power rule on each polynomial.

questions.question: Find the derivative using the product rule: (i) h(x) = (2x−5)(5x+7)  (ii) h(x) = x·√(3x²+4)  (iii) h(x) = ³√(x+1)·⁵√(x²+1)  (iv) h(x) = x²(√x + 1)  (v) h(x) = (x+1)³·x^(−3/2)
questions.explanation: (uv)′ = u′v + uv′. (ii) u′v+uv′ = √(3x²+4) + 3x²/√(3x²+4); (iii) combine over 15(x+1)^(2/3)(x²+1)^(4/5); (v) factor (3/2)x^(−5/2)(x+1)² leaving [2x − (x+1)] = x−1.

questions.question: Find the derivative using the quotient rule: (i) h(x) = (3x+4)/(2x−3)  (ii) h(x) = (x²−1)(x²+1)^(−1)  (iii) h(x) = (x²−x+1)/(x²+x−1)  (iv) h(x) = 2x⁴/(b²−x²)  (v) h(x) = (√x+1)/(√x−1)
questions.explanation: (u/v)′ = (u′v − uv′)/v². (iii) numerator simplifies to 2x²−4x; (v) the √x terms cancel leaving −2/(2√x) in the numerator.

questions.question: Find the derivatives using the chain rule: (i) y = (x⁴+5x²+6)^(3/2)  (ii) y = ((x−1)/(x+1))^(3/4)  (iii) y = √((2+x)/(3+x))  (iv) y = (x+√(x²−1))ₙ  (v) y = ³√((x³+1)/(x³−1))
questions.explanation: Outer-power rule times inner derivative; e.g. (ii) inner derivative is 2/(x+1)² and the (−1/4) power flips the fraction.

questions.question: Differentiate x³/(1+x³) w.r.t. x³.
questions.explanation: With t = x³ the expression is t/(1+t), whose derivative is 1/(1+t)².

questions.question: If y = f(x) is given implicitly, find dy/dx: (i) y − xy − sin y = 0  (ii) y³ − 3y + 2x = 0  (iii) x² + y² + 4x + 6y − 12 = 0  (iv) sin(xy) + sec x = 2  (v) x√(1+y) + y√(1+x) = 0  (vi) y(x²+1) = x(y²+1)
questions.answer:
(i) y/(1 − x − cos y)
(ii) 2/[3(1−y²)]
(iii) −(x+2)/(y+3)
(iv) −[y cos(xy) + sec x tan x]/[x cos(xy)]
(v) −√((1+y)/(1+x))·[y + 2√((1+x)(1+y))]/[x + 2√((1+x)(1+y))]
(vi) (y²+1−2xy)/(x²+1−2xy)
questions.explanation: Differentiate both sides treating y as y(x), collect y′ terms and solve; (v) multiply through by 2√(1+y)√(1+x) before isolating y′.

questions.question: If u²/a² + v²/b² = 1 (a, b non-zero constants), find du/dv and dv/du.
questions.explanation: Differentiate w.r.t. v: (2u/a²)(du/dv) + 2v/b² = 0; the other derivative is its reciprocal.

questions.question: Find the slope of the tangent to the curve 3x² − 7y² + 14y − 27 = 0 at the point (−3, 0).
questions.explanation: 6x − 14yy′ + 14y′ = 0; at (−3,0): −18 + 14y′ = 0 ⇒ y′ = 9/7.

questions.question: Differentiate by the first-principle method: (i) sin 4x  (ii) cos²2x  (iii) sec √x  (iv) √(tan x)  (v) csc 3x  (vi) cot 2x
questions.answer:
(i) 4cos 4x
(ii) −2 sin 4x
(iii) sec√x tan√x/(2√x)
(iv) sec²x/(2√(tan x))
(v) −3 csc 3x cot 3x
(vi) −2 csc²2x
questions.explanation: lim<sub>δx→0</sub>[f(x+δx)−f(x)]/δx with sum-to-product / conjugate tricks; (ii) −4 sin2x cos2x collapses to −2 sin4x.

questions.question: Using differentiation rules, differentiate w.r.t. their involved variables: (i) f(x) = (x+2)sin x  (ii) f(θ) = tan²θ·sec³θ  (iii) f(t) = sin²3t·cos³t  (iv) f(x) = √(sin2x/cos x)  (v) f(θ) = (tanθ−1)/secθ  (vi) f(x) = sin x² + sin²x
questions.answer:
(i) sin x + (x+2)cos x
(ii) sec³θ tanθ(2sec²θ + 3tan²θ)
(iii) 3cos²t(sin6t cos t − sin²3t sin t)
(iv) cos x/√(2 sin x)
(v) sinθ + cosθ
(vi) 2x cos x² + sin 2x
questions.explanation: Product/quotient rules; (iv) simplifies first: sin2x/cos x = 2 sin x; (v) simplifies to sinθ − cosθ.

questions.question: Differentiate (1+tan²x)/(1−tan²x) w.r.t. tan²x.
questions.explanation: With t = tan²x: d/dt[(1+t)/(1−t)] = [(1−t)+(1+t)]/(1−t)² = 2/(1−t)².

questions.question: Find dy/dx: (i) y = sin⁻¹√((1−cos x)/2)  (ii) y = cot⁻¹√((1+cos x)/(1−cos x))  (iii) y = tan⁻¹(sin2x/(1+cos2x))  (iv) y = x + cos⁻¹x·√(1−x²)  (v) y = x tan⁻¹x/(1+x²)  (vi) y = tan⁻¹[(√(1+x)−√(1−x))/(√(1+x)+√(1−x))]
questions.explanation: Half-angle simplifications: (i) sin⁻¹(sin x/2) = x/2; (ii) cot⁻¹(cot x/2) = x/2; (iii) tan⁻¹(tan x) = x; (vi) x = cosθ reduces the argument to tan(π/4 − θ/2).

questions.question: If y = tan(2 tan⁻¹(x/2)), prove that dy/dx = 4(1+y²)/(4+x²).
questions.explanation: With t = tan⁻¹(x/2): dy/dt = 2sec²2t = 2(1+y²) and dt/dx = 2/(4+x²); multiply.

questions.question: If y/x = tan⁻¹(x/y), show that dy/dx = y/x.
questions.explanation: Differentiating both sides gives (xy′−y)/x² = (y−xy′)/(x²+y²); factoring (xy′−y) forces it to zero, so xy′ = y.

questions.question: Given that tan y(1+tan x) = 1 − tan x, show that dy/dx = −1.
questions.explanation: tan y = (1−tan x)/(1+tan x) = tan(π/4 − x), so y = π/4 − x.

questions.question: If y = tan(a tan⁻¹x), show that (1+x²)dy/dx − a(1+y²) = 0.
questions.explanation: y′ = sec²(a tan⁻¹x)·a/(1+x²) = a(1+y²)/(1+x²).

questions.question: Find dy/dx when: (i) x = a sinθ, y = a cosθ  (ii) x = t + 1/t, y = t + 1  (iii) x = a(1−t²)/(1+t²), y = 2bt/(1+t²)  (iv) x = aθ², y = 2aθ
questions.explanation: Parametric rule dy/dx = (dy/dt)/(dx/dt); (iii) dx/dt = −4at/(1+t²)², dy/dt = 2b(1−t²)/(1+t²)².

questions.question: If y = √(tan x + √(tan x + √(tan x + …))), prove that (2y − 1)dy/dx = sec²x.
questions.explanation: The infinite nesting means y² = tan x + y; differentiating gives 2yy′ = sec²x + y′.

questions.question: Find the derivatives of cos⁻¹x, csc⁻¹x and cot⁻¹x by using the differentiation formula.
questions.answer: d/dx cos⁻¹x = −1/√(1−x²); d/dx csc⁻¹x = −1/(x√(x²−1)); d/dx cot⁻¹x = −1/(1+x²)
questions.explanation: Standard inverse-trigonometric derivative formulas (csc⁻¹ valid for |x| > 1).

questions.question: Differentiate the following w.r.t. x: (i) x² + 2ˣ  (ii) 4ˣ + 5ˣ  (iii) e^(tan x + cot x)  (iv) e^(tan x²)  (v) e^(2 ln(2x+1))  (vi) log₁⁰x  (vii) eˣ/(x²+1)  (viii) x² + 2ˣ + a^(2x)  (ix) (ln x)ˣ  (x) ln(√(e^(3x)+e^(−3x)))  (xi) ln(sin(ln x))  (xii) ln[tan(x/2 + π/4)]
questions.answer:
(i) 2x + 2ˣln2
(ii) 4ˣln4 + 5ˣln5
(iii) (sec²x − csc²x)e^(tan x+cot x)
(iv) 2x sec²(x²)e^(tan x²)
(v) 4(2x+1)
(vi) 1/(x ln10)
(vii) (x−1)²eˣ/(x²+1)²
(viii) 2x + 2ˣln2 + 2a^(2x)ln a (a > 0)
(ix) (ln x)ˣ[1/ln x + ln(ln x)]
(x) (3/2)tanh 3x
(xi) cot(ln x)/x
(xii) sec x
questions.explanation: d/dx aˣ = aˣln a; (v) collapses to (2x+1)²; (ix) take ln y = x ln(ln x); (xii) the derivative reduces to 1/sin(x+π/2).

questions.question: Using logarithmic differentiation find dy/dx if: (i) y = √((x²−1)/(x²+1))  (ii) y = x³√x  (iii) y = xe^(cos x)  (iv) y = e^(−2x)(x²+2x+1)  (v) y = ln(eˣ/(1+eˣ))  (vi) y = √((1+eˣ)/(1−eˣ))
questions.explanation: Take ln of both sides, differentiate, then multiply back by y; (ii) is simply x^(7/2).

questions.question: Find dy/dx if: (i) y = (1−x²)/√(1+x²)  (ii) y = √((1−x)/(1+x))
questions.explanation: Quotient/chain rule; in (i) factor (1+x²)^(−3/2) to combine the two terms.

questions.question: Find dy/dx if: (i) y = x^(sin x)  (ii) y = (sin⁻¹x)^(ln x)  (iii) y = (tan⁻¹x)^(sin x+cos x)  (iv) y = (ln x)^(cos x)  (v) y = xˣ  (vi) y = ln[(√(x²+1)−x)/(√(x²+1)+x)]
questions.answer:
(i) x^(sin x)(sin x/x + cos x ln x)
(ii) (sin⁻¹x)^(ln x)[ln x/(√(1−x²) sin⁻¹x) + ln(sin⁻¹x)/x]
(iii) (tan⁻¹x)^(sin x+cos x)[(sin x+cos x)/((1+x²)tan⁻¹x) + (cos x − sin x)ln(tan⁻¹x)]
(iv) (ln x)^(cos x)[cos x/(x ln x) − sin x ln(ln x)]
(v) xˣ(1 + ln x)
(vi) −2/√(x²+1)
questions.explanation: Variable base and exponent: ln y = (exponent)·ln(base), then product rule. (vi) the fraction equals (√(x²+1)−x)², so y = 2ln(√(x²+1)−x).

questions.question: Find dy/dx when: (i) x^y·yˣ = 1  (ii) ln(xy) = x² + y²  (iii) y = sin⁻¹(cos x) + cos⁻¹(sin x)  (iv) y = x^y  (v) y = cos x·ln(sin⁻¹x)  (vi) xₙ·yₙ = aₙ
questions.answer:
(i) −(y/x)(x ln y + y)/(y ln x + x)
(ii) −(y/x)(2x²−1)/(2y²−1)
(iii) −2
(iv) y²/[x(1 − y ln x)]
(v) cos x/[√(1−x²) sin⁻¹x] − sin x·ln(sin⁻¹x)
(vi) −y/x
questions.explanation: Take logs to linearize products/powers, then differentiate implicitly; (iii) sin⁻¹(cos x) = π/2 − x and cos⁻¹(sin x) = π/2 − x.

questions.question: Differentiate the following w.r.t. x: (i) sinh[ln(x+3)]  (ii) sinh(e^(3x))  (iii) cosh(2x²+3x)  (iv) tanh√x/√(cosh x)  (v) tan(e^(sinh⁻¹x))  (vi) sinh⁻¹x/sech⁻¹x  (vii) cosh x·coth x²  (viii) sinh x·tanh x²  (ix) ln[tanh(x²+2x+1)]
questions.answer:
(i) cosh[ln(x+3)]/(x+3)
(ii) 3e^(3x)cosh(e^(3x))
(iii) (4x+3)sinh(2x²+3x)
(iv) [cosh x·sech²√x − √x·sinh x·tanh√x]/(2√x·cosh^(3/2)x)
(v) e^(sinh⁻¹x)·sec²(e^(sinh⁻¹x))/√(1+x²)
(vi) [x√(1−x²)·sech⁻¹x + √(1+x²)·sinh⁻¹x]/[x√(1−x⁴)(sech⁻¹x)²]
(vii) sinh x·coth x² − 2x·cosh x·csch²x²
(viii) cosh x·tanh x² + 2x·sinh x·sech²x²
(ix) 2(x+1)csch(x²+2x+1)sech(x²+2x+1)
questions.explanation: Chain rule with d/dx sinh u = cosh u·u′ etc.; (vi) uses d/dx sech⁻¹x = −1/(x√(1−x²)). Note: the printed key shows "+" in (iv)'s numerator; the correct sign is − (key misprint).

questions.question: Find dy/dx for: (i) y = x cosh⁻¹x − √(x²−1)  (ii) y = x tanh⁻¹(3x)  (iii) ln(cosh⁻¹x) + sinh⁻¹y = C  (iv) y = ln(1−x²) + 2x tanh⁻¹x  (v) y = tanh⁻¹(tan x³)  (vi) y = x sech⁻¹(√x)
questions.explanation: In (i) and (iv) the algebraic terms cancel exactly; (vi) uses d/dx sech⁻¹(√x) = −1/(2x√(1−x)).

questions.question: Write the MAPLE command diff to differentiate: (i) f(x) = 2x³+3x²+6  (ii) f(x) = sin(2x+3)  (iii) f(x) = (x+1)(x+2)  (iv) f(x) = (x²−3x+2)/(x²−4)
questions.explanation: MAPLE syntax: diff(expression, [variable]); with explicit * for multiplication.

questions.question: Write the MAPLE command > d/dx to differentiate: (i) f(x) = x³+5x²+3x+7  (ii) f(x) = sin x²  (iii) f(x) = (√x+1)/(x²+1)
questions.answer:
(i) > diff(x^3+5*x^2+3*x+7, x);
(ii) > diff(sin(x^2), x);
(iii) > diff((sqrt(x)+1)/(x^2+1), x);
questions.explanation: The > d/dx prompt form takes the expression and the variable x directly.

questions.question: Select the correct options: (i) derivative of 2/x³  (ii) derivative of √x + x√x  (iii) y = (x+1)(x²−2)  (iv) ax²+by² = ab  (v) y = √(tan x − y)  (vi) y = tan⁻¹√x  (vii) derivative of tan x w.r.t. cot x  (viii) f(x) = ax²−3x−5, f′(2) = 9  (ix) derivative of x²e^(2x)  (x) derivative of aˣ if a < 0  (xi) y = tan⁻¹√((1−cos2x)/(1+cos2x))  (xii) d/dx(sinh⁻¹x + cosh⁻¹x)  (xiii) derivative of tanh ax  (xiv) derivative of coth⁻¹(2x)  (xv) f(x) = ln 2x, g inverse of f, g′(x)  (xvi) f(x) = a cos 3x, f′(π/2) = 6
questions.answer:
(i) (d) −6/x⁴
(ii) (a) 1/(2√x) + (3/2)√x
(iii) (b) 3x²+2x−2
(iv) (c) −ax/(by)
(v) (d) sec²x/(2y+1)
(vi) (d) 1/[2(√x+x√x)]
(vii) (b) −tan²x
(viii) (b) 3
(ix) (c) 2e^(2x)(x²+x)
(x) (d) does not exist
(xi) (a) 1
(xii) (c) 1/√(x²+1) + 1/√(x²−1)
(xiii) (c) a sech²ax
(xiv) (b) 2/(1−4x²)
(xv) (d) eˣ/2
(xvi) (c) 2
questions.explanation: Each option verified by direct differentiation; (v) and (xi) use y² = tan x − y and the half-angle identity respectively; (xv) the inverse of ln 2x is eˣ/2.

questions.question: Find the derivative of √(cos x) and sec√x by first principle.
questions.explanation: Rationalize / use sec A − sec B = sec A sec B(cos B − cos A) with sum-to-product, then take lim<sub>δx→0</sub>.

questions.question: If y = (sin x)^(ln x), find dy/dx.
questions.answer: (sin x)^(ln x)[ln(sin x)/x + cot x·ln x]
questions.explanation: ln y = ln x·ln(sin x); differentiate and multiply back by y.

questions.question: Find dy/dx if ax² + 2hxy + by² = 0.
questions.explanation: Implicit differentiation: 2ax + 2h(y + xy′) + 2byy′ = 0.

questions.question: Let f(x) = cot⁻¹(2x/(1−x²)); find f′(x) and f′(−√3).
questions.explanation: With x = tanθ the argument is tan 2θ, so f = π/2 − 2θ per branch and f′ = −2/(1+x²). Note: the printed key's second value π/6 is f(−√3), not f′(−√3) (key misprint).

questions.question: x = 4(t − sin t) and y = 4(1 + cos t); find dy/dx.
questions.explanation: (dy/dt)/(dx/dt) = −sin t/(1−cos t) = −cot(t/2) by half-angle identities.

questions.question: Differentiate w.r.t. x: (i) (x²+x⁻¹)/(x²−x⁻¹)  (ii) (3x−2)/√(x²+1)
questions.explanation: (i) multiply top and bottom by x to get (x³+1)/(x³−1); (ii) quotient rule then combine over (x²+1)^(3/2).

questions.question: If y = x⁴ + 2x², show that dy/dx = 4x√(y+1).
questions.explanation: y+1 = (x²+1)², so √(y+1) = x²+1 and 4x(x²+1) = 4x³+4x = y′.

questions.question: If y = √(sin x + √(sin x + √(sin x + …))), show that (2y − 1)y′ = cos x.
questions.explanation: Infinite nesting gives y² = sin x + y; differentiate: 2yy′ = cos x + y′.

questions.question: Differentiate w.r.t. x: (i) cosh(cos⁻¹√x)  (ii) tanh⁻¹(cos 2x)
questions.explanation: (i) chain rule with d/dx cos⁻¹√x = −1/(2√x√(1−x)); (ii) (−2 sin 2x)/(1−cos²2x) = −2/sin 2x.

questions.question: Calculate the first, second and third order derivatives of y = cos²x.
questions.explanation: Write y = (1+cos 2x)/2 first; each differentiation then doubles the coefficient.

questions.question: Find the 2nd order derivative of f(x) = cos x/(1+sin x).
questions.explanation: f′ simplifies to −1/(1+sin x) because −sin x(1+sin x) − cos²x = −(1+sin x).

questions.question: Find the fourth order derivatives: (i) h(t) = 3t⁷ − 6t⁴ + 8t³ − 12t + 18  (ii) f(x) = ³√x − 1/(8x²) − √x
questions.explanation: Differentiate four times term by term; in (ii) keep fractional/negative powers until the end.

questions.question: Determine the fourth order derivative: (i) r(t) = 3t² + 8√t  (ii) y = cos x  (iii) f(y) = sin 3y + e^(−2y) + ln(7y)
questions.explanation: (ii) the fourth derivative of cos x cycles back to cos x; (iii) ln(7y) contributes −6/y⁴.

questions.question: If x² + y² = 10, find y″.
questions.explanation: y′ = −x/y, then differentiate the quotient and substitute back.

questions.question: Find d²y/dx² if: (i) 2y² + 6x² = 76  (ii) x³ + y³ = 1
questions.explanation: Implicit differentiation twice; in (ii) y′ = −x²/y² and the numerator collapses using the original equation.

questions.question: Find d²y/dx² if: (i) x = −5t³ − 7 and y = 3t² + 16  (ii) x = cosθ and y = sinθ
questions.explanation: Parametric second derivative: d²y/dx² = [d/dt(dy/dx)]/(dx/dt).

questions.question: The derivative of r(t) is r′(t) = 6t + 4t^(−1/2) + eˬ; find r″(t), r″′(t) and r⁴(t).
questions.explanation: Differentiate the given first derivative three more times.

questions.question: If x² + y² = 25, find d²y/dx² at the point (4, 3).
questions.explanation: y″ = −(x²+y²)/y³ = −25/y³; at y = 3 this is −25/27.

questions.question: Write MAPLE commands to find higher order derivatives: (i) f(x) = x³+3x²+6x+8 (third)  (ii) f(x) = cos√(2x+3) (second)  (iii) f(x) = e^(x²+5x+3) (third)  (iv) f(x) = ln√(3x+2) (second)  (v) f(x) = e^(sin x) (third)
questions.answer:
(i) > diff(x^3+3*x^2+6*x+8, x$3);
(ii) > diff(cos(sqrt(2*x+3)), x$2);
(iii) > diff(exp(x^2+5*x+3), x$3);
(iv) > diff(ln(sqrt(3*x+2)), x$2);
(v) > diff(exp(sin(x)), x$3);
questions.explanation: MAPLE's x$n syntax repeats differentiation n times. The book skips Q10–11 and the key lists this item as 10.

questions.question: Obtain the first three terms of the Maclaurin's series for: (i) cos x  (ii) eˣ  (iii) ln(1+x)  (iv) sin²x  (v) e^(sin x)  (vi) xe^(−x)  (vii) 1/(1+x)
questions.answer:
(i) 1 − x²/2! + x⁴/4!
(ii) 1 + x + x²/2!
(iii) x − x²/2 + x³/3
(iv) x² − x⁴/3 + 2x⁶/45
(v) 1 + x + x²/2!
(vi) x − x² + x³/2
(vii) 1 − x + x²
questions.explanation: Evaluate f and its derivatives at 0; (iv) uses sin²x = (1−cos 2x)/2.

questions.question: Find the first four terms of the Taylor's series: (i) ln x centered at a = 1  (ii) 1/x centered at a = 1  (iii) sin x centered at a = π/4  (iv) cos x centered at a = π/2
questions.explanation: Taylor coefficients fₙ(a)/n!; in (iv) the even-order terms vanish at π/2.

questions.question: Does the Maclaurin's series of f(x) = 1/x, g(x) = cosec x and h(x) = √x exist? If not, why? Give appropriate justification.
questions.answer: No — none of the three has a Maclaurin series.
questions.explanation: f and g are not defined at x = 0, and for all three the derivatives of all orders fail to exist at 0 (h′(x) = 1/(2√x) → ∞ as x → 0⁺).

questions.question: Write MAPLE commands to find the Taylor expression: (i) eˣ at x = 1 upto 10 terms  (ii) sin x at x = π upto 10 terms  (iii) cos x at x = π upto 10 terms  (iv) ln(1+x) at x = 0 upto 10 terms  (v) 1/x at x = 1 upto 5 terms  (vi) 1/x at x = 2 upto 5 terms
questions.answer:
(i) > taylor(exp(x), x = 1, 10)
(ii) > taylor(sin(x), x = π, 10)
(iii) > taylor(cos(x), x = π, 10)
(iv) > taylor(ln(1+x), x = 0, 10)
(v) > taylor(1/x, x = 1, 5)
(vi) > taylor(1/x, x = 2, 5)
questions.explanation: taylor(expression, x = a, n) expands about a with n terms.

questions.question: Determine the slope of the tangent to the curve y = x³ at the point (3/2, 27/8).
questions.explanation: y′ = 3x² evaluated at x = 3/2.

questions.question: Find the slope of the tangents to the curve x² + y² = 25 at the points on it whose x-coordinate is 2.
questions.explanation: y = ±√21 and y′ = −x/y.

questions.question: Find the equation of the tangent and the equation of the normal to the curve y = x + 1/x at the point where x = 2.
questions.explanation: Point (2, 5/2), slope 3/4; normal slope −4/3.

questions.question: Given two curves y = x² and y = (x−3)². Find the angle between them.
questions.explanation: They meet at (3/2, 9/4) with slopes 3 and −3; tanθ = |(m₁−m₂)/(1+m₁m₂)| = 3/4.

questions.question: Prove that the tangent lines to the curve y² = 4ax at the points where x = a are at right angles to each other.
questions.explanation: y′ = 2a/y and at x = a, y = ±2a.

questions.question: At what points on the curve x² + y² − 2x − 4y + 1 = 0 is the tangent parallel to the y-axis?
questions.explanation: y′ = (1−x)/(y−2) is undefined at y = 2; substituting gives x²−2x−3 = 0.

questions.question: Show that the function f(x) = −x² + 10x + 9 is increasing at x = 4.
questions.answer: Shown: f′(4) = 2 > 0, so f is increasing at x = 4
questions.explanation: f′(x) = −2x + 10.

questions.question: Show that f(x) = tan²x is decreasing at x = 3π/4.
questions.answer: Shown: f′(3π/4) = −4 < 0, so f is decreasing there
questions.explanation: f′(x) = 2 tan x sec²x; tan(3π/4) = −1, sec²(3π/4) = 2.

questions.question: Find the maximum and minimum values, if any, of f : ℜ → ℜ: (i) x²−2x+3  (ii) x³−9x²+15x+3  (iii) −x⁴+2x²  (iv) eˣ sin x  (v) 2eˣ + e^(−x)  (vi) 2x − x²
questions.answer:
(i) minimum at x = 1 (value 2)
(ii) relative maximum f(1) = 10; relative minimum f(5) = −22
(iii) relative minimum f(0) = 0; relative maxima f(±1) = 1
(iv) relative minimum −e^(−π/4)/√2 ≈ −0.322 at x = −π/4; relative maximum e^(3π/4)/√2 ≈ 7.46 at x = 3π/4
(v) relative minimum 2√2 ≈ 2.828 at x = −(ln 2)/2
(vi) relative maximum f(1) = 1
questions.explanation: Second-derivative test at each critical point. Key's printed values for (ii) and (iv) are garbled (see solution file flags); the values above are the verified ones.

questions.question: A rectangular reservoir with a square bottom and open top is to be lined inside with lead. Find the dimensions to hold a³/2 cubic metres so that the lead required is minimum.
questions.answer: Length = a, breadth = a, height = a/2
questions.explanation: S = x² + 2a³/x with x the base side; S′ = 0 gives x = a and then h = a/2.

questions.question: Find a right-angled triangle of maximum area with a hypotenuse of length h.
questions.answer: Isosceles right triangle with legs h/√2; maximum area h²/4
questions.explanation: Maximize A² = x²(h²−x²)/4 over the leg x.

questions.question: A particle moves so that its distance s at time t is given by s = ut + ½at² (u, a fixed). Find its speed and the magnitude of its acceleration at time t.
questions.explanation: v = ds/dt and a = dv/dt.

questions.question: Choose the correct answer: (i) If y = 1/x then y‴(1) = (a) 6 (b) −6 (c) 2 (d) none  (ii) The nth derivative of 2eˣ is (a) 2neˣ (b) 2e^(nx) (c) 2eˣ (d) eˣ/2  (iii) If xy = k² then y″ = (a) 2k²/x (b) −2k²/x³ (c) 3k²/x³ (d) 2k²/x³  (iv) The third derivative of 2ˣ is (a) (ln3)²e^(xln2) (b) (ln2)³e^(xln3) (c) (ln2)³e^(xln2) (d) none  (v) The second derivative of A sin x + B cos x is (a) f(x) (b) −f(x) (c) ±f(x) (d) none  (vi) d²S/dt² gives (a) velocity (b) deceleration (c) acceleration (d) average velocity  (vii) If y = tan⁻¹x then y″(1) = (a) −1/2 (b) 1/4 (c) −1/4 (d) 1/2  (viii) y = x − x³/3! + x⁵/5! − … is the Maclaurin series of (a) sin x (b) cos x (c) eˣ (d) none  (ix) f is decreasing when for x<sub>1</sub> < x<sub>2</sub> (a) f(x<sub>1</sub>) < f(x<sub>2</sub>) (b) f(x<sub>1</sub>) > f(x<sub>2</sub>) (c) ≥ (d) ≤  (x) A point where f′(c) = 0 is called (a) maximum (b) minimum (c) stationary (d) critical
questions.answer:
(i) (b) −6
(ii) (c) 2eˣ
(iii) (d) 2k²/x³
(iv) (c) (ln2)³e^(xln2)
(v) (b) −f(x)
(vi) (c) acceleration
(vii) (a) −1/2
(viii) (a) sin x
(ix) (b) f(x1) > f(x2)
(x) (c) stationary point
questions.explanation: (i) y‴ = −6x^(−4). (iii) y = k²/x. (iv) 2ˣ = e^(x ln2). (vii) y″ = −2x/(1+x²)². All ten match the answers key.

questions.question: Find the second derivative of ln(1 + x²).
questions.explanation: y′ = 2x/(1+x²); quotient rule gives y″ = [2(1+x²) − 4x²]/(1+x²)².

questions.question: If x = 3u² + 1 and y = 3u² + 5u, find d²y/dx².
questions.explanation: dy/dx = (6u+5)/(6u) = 1 + (5/6)u^(−1); differentiate in u and divide by dx/du = 6u.

questions.question: Find the third derivatives: (i) v = x³ − x² + x − 1  (ii) f = 7 sin(x/3) + cos(1 − 2x)  (iii) y = e^(−5x) + 8 ln(2x⁴)
questions.explanation: (iii) 8 ln(2x⁴) = 8 ln 2 + 32 ln x, so y′ = −5e^(−5x) + 32/x.

questions.question: Find the second derivatives: (i) g = sin(2x³ − 9x)  (ii) z = ln(7 − x³)  (iii) q = 2/(6 + 2x − x²)⁴  (iv) h = cos²(7t)  (v) 2x³ + y² = 1 − 4y  (vi) 6y − xy² = 1
questions.answer:
(i) 12x cos(2x³−9x) − (6x²−9)² sin(2x³−9x)
(ii) (−42x − 3x⁴)/(7 − x³)²
(iii) 16(6+2x−x²)^(−5) + 40(2−2x)²(6+2x−x²)^(−6)
(iv) 98 sin²(7t) − 98 cos²(7t)
(v) −6x(y+2)^(−1) − 9x⁴(y+2)^(−3)
(vi) 2y³(6−2xy)^(−2) [2 + xy(6−2xy)^(−1)]
questions.explanation: (v) implicit: y′ = −3x²/(y+2). (vi) implicit: y′ = y²/(6−2xy). (iv) h′ = −7 sin(14t), h″ = −98 cos(14t).

questions.question: If y = cos x, find y′, y″, y‴ and y⁗.
questions.answer: y′ = −sin x; y″ = −cos x; y‴ = sin x; y⁗ = cos x
questions.explanation: Successive differentiation cycles with period 4.

questions.question: If x = 4 sin t and y = 5 cos t, find d²y/dx².
questions.explanation: dy/dx = −(5/4) tan t; divide d/dt of that by dx/dt = 4 cos t.

questions.question: Find the rth derivative of xₙ for r ≤ n.
questions.explanation: Each differentiation drops the exponent by 1 and multiplies by the current exponent; the key's printed form is garbled (see solution file flags).

questions.question: Obtain the Taylor series for f(x) = x⁴ + x − 2 at a = 1.
Obtain the Taylor series for the function (x − 1)eˣ near x = 1.
questions.explanation: f(1) = 0; f′ = xeˣ, f″ = (1+x)eˣ, f‴ = (2+x)eˣ, f⁗ = (3+x)eˣ, evaluated at x = 1 and divided by k!.

questions.question: Find the Maclaurin series for ln(1 + x) and hence find that for ln((1+x)/(1−x)).
questions.answer: ln(1+x) = x − x²/2 + x³/3 − …;  ln((1+x)/(1−x)) = 2(x + x³/3 + x⁵/5 + …) = 2Σ x^(2n−1)/(2n−1)
questions.explanation: Subtract the series of ln(1−x) = −(x + x²/2 + x³/3 + …) from that of ln(1+x); even powers cancel.

questions.question: Find the equation of the tangent line to the curve y = x³ − 3x² + x at the point (2, −2).
questions.explanation: y′ = 3x² − 6x + 1 gives slope 1 at x = 2; point-slope form.

questions.question: At what point on the graph of y = x² is the tangent line parallel to the line 3x − y = 2?
questions.explanation: Slope of the line is 3; set y′ = 2x = 3.

questions.question: Determine the interval on which the function f(x) = x² − 3x + 1 is increasing and decreasing.
questions.explanation: f′(x) = 2x − 3 changes sign at x = 3/2.

questions.question: Find the domain of the following vector functions: (i) r(t) = 2t î − 3t ĵ + (1/t) k̂  (ii) r(t) = sin t î + cos t ĵ + tan t k̂  (iii) r(t) = (1 − t) î + √t ĵ + (1/t²) k̂  (iv) g(t) = cos t î − cot t ĵ + cosec t k̂
questions.explanation: The domain is the intersection of the component domains: (i) 1/t needs t ≠ 0; (ii) tan t fails at odd multiples of π/2; (iii) √t needs t ≥ 0 and 1/t² needs t ≠ 0; (iv) cot t and cosec t fail at nπ.

questions.question: Find the limit of the vector function r(t) = (e^(3t) − 1) î + (√(3+t) − √3)/(3t) ĵ + 1/(9t+1) k̂ at t = 0.
questions.explanation: Component limits: e^(3t)−1 → 0; rationalizing the ĵ component gives 1/(3(√(3+t)+√3)) → 1/(6√3); 1/(9t+1) → 1.

questions.question: If u(t) = t² î − 2 ĵ and v(t) = 2t î − 5 k̂ are vector functions and h = 3t is a scalar function, find: (i) lim<sub>t→0</sub> [u(t) + v(t)]  (ii) lim<sub>t→1</sub> [u(t) · v(t)]  (iii) lim<sub>t→1</sub> [u(t) × v(t)]  (iv) lim<sub>t→5</sub> [h u(t)]
questions.explanation: Evaluate componentwise at the limit point; (iii) (î − 2ĵ) × (2î − 5k̂) = 5ĵ + 4k̂ + 10î. The key prints (i) as −2î − 5k̂ (unit-vector misprint); the verified sum is −2ĵ − 5k̂.

questions.question: Show that the function R(t) = sin²t î + tan t ĵ + (1/t) k̂ is continuous at t = π/4.
questions.answer: Shown: lim<sub>t→π/4</sub> R(t) = ½ î + ĵ + (4/π) k̂ = R(π/4)
questions.explanation: Each component (sin²t, tan t, 1/t) is continuous at π/4, so the limit equals the value.

questions.question: Show that the function r(t) = (2/t) î + t³/(2t³ − 5) ĵ + (1/eˬ) k̂ is continuous as t → ∞.
questions.answer: Shown: lim<sub>t→∞</sub> r(t) = ½ ĵ, a finite vector, so the limit exists
questions.explanation: 2/t → 0; t³/(2t³−5) = 1/(2 − 5/t³) → 1/2; e^(−t) → 0.

questions.question: For what values of t are the following vector functions continuous: (i) r(t) = ln(t+3) î + 1/(t−1) ĵ + (t+2)/(t²−4) k̂  (ii) r(t) = 1/(3t+1) î + (1/t) ĵ
questions.answer:
(i) all t > −3 with t ≠ 1 and t ≠ ±2
(ii) all t ≠ 0 and t ≠ −1/3
questions.explanation: Intersect the component continuity sets: (i) ln(t+3) needs t > −3, 1/(t−1) needs t ≠ 1, (t+2)/(t²−4) needs t ≠ ±2.

questions.question: Find the derivative of the following vector functions: (i) f(t) = ln t² î + e^(2t) ĵ + (2t² + 1) k̂  (ii) f(t) = (t + 1) î + ln(t + 2) ĵ  (iii) f(t) = sec t î + cos t² ĵ + (t² + t + 1) k̂
questions.explanation: Differentiate componentwise; (i) d/dt ln t² = 2t/t² = 2/t; (iii) chain rule on cos t² and sec t.

questions.question: If x(t) = t î + 2t ĵ and y(t) = 2t î + 3t k̂ are vector functions and Ø(t) = 3t is a scalar function, find: (i) d/dt [x − y]  (ii) d/dt [x · y]  (iii) d/dt [x × y]  (iv) d/dt [Ø x]
questions.explanation: (ii) x·y = 2t². (iii) x×y = 6t² î − 3t² ĵ − 4t² k̂. (iv) Øx = 3t² î + 6t² ĵ.

questions.question: A particle moves so that its position as a function of time is r(t) = î + 4t² ĵ + t k̂. Write expressions for its (a) velocity and (b) acceleration as functions of time.
questions.explanation: v = dr/dt and a = dv/dt, componentwise.

questions.question: The path of a particle is given for time t > 0 by x = t² − 3t and y = (2/3)t³. Find the magnitude of velocity and acceleration of the particle at t = 5.
questions.explanation: v = (2t−3, 2t²) → (7, 50); a = (2, 4t) → (2, 20); take magnitudes.

questions.question: A particle moves along the curve x = 2t² and y = 4t. Find the component of velocity and acceleration at t = 2 in the direction of 2 î + ĵ.
questions.explanation: v(2) = (8, 4), a = (4, 0); project on u = (2î+ĵ)/√5. The key's "acceleration component = 4" is |a|, not the component along 2î+ĵ (see solution file flags).

questions.question: Choose the correct answer: (i) domain of r(t) = t³ î + 1/(t−1) ĵ + ln(t−2) k̂ is (a) {t > 2} (b) {t < 2} (c) {t > 0} (d) {t > 1}  (ii) F(t) = cos t î + sin 2t k̂ at t = π is (a) not continuous (b) continuous (c) limit does not exist (d) none  (iii) F(t) = 1/(t−2) î + sin t ĵ is continuous for (a) t ≠ 2 (b) t > 2 (c) t ≤ 2 (d) all t  (iv) u = t² î − e^(2t) ĵ, h(t) = t²+2t−2: lim<sub>t→0</sub> [h u] = (a) −ĵ (b) ĵ (c) 2ĵ (d) −2ĵ  (v) u = t² î − e^(2t) ĵ, v = −2 î − t² k̂: lim<sub>t→0</sub> [u·v] = (a) 0 (b) t⁴ (c) t²−e^(2t) (d) −2t²  (vi) f(t) = t² î − e^(2t) ĵ then f′(t) = (a) 2t î−2e^(2t) ĵ (b) 2t î−e^(2t) ĵ (c) 2t î−2te^(2t) ĵ (d) none  (vii) velocity of r(t) = (1/(2π)) t î + 3 cos t ĵ at t = π/2 is (a) (1/2π)î+3ĵ (b) (1/2π)î (c) (1/2π)î−3ĵ (d) none  (viii) magnitude of velocity of r(t) = 4cos t î + 4sin t ĵ + (3/(2π))t² k̂ at t = π is (a) √5 (b) 5 (c) √(5π) (d) 5π  (ix) magnitude of acceleration of the same r at t = π/2 is (a) √(16π²+9)/π (b) √(16π²+9) (c) √(16π²+9)/π² (d) √(16+9π²)/π  (x) if a = 2 î + 3 ĵ + 5 k̂ then da/dt = (a) 10 (b) √38 (c) 0 (d) none
questions.answer:
(i) (a) {t > 2}
(ii) (b) is continuous
(iii) (a) t ≠ 2
(iv) (c) 2ĵ
(v) (a) 0
(vi) (a) 2t î − 2e^(2t) ĵ
(vii) (c) (1/2π) î − 3 ĵ
(viii) (b) 5
(ix) (a) √(16π²+9)/π
(x) (c) 0
questions.explanation: (iv) h(0)u(0) = (−2)(−ĵ) = 2ĵ. (viii) v(π) = (0,−4,3). (ix) a(π/2) = (0,−4,3/π). (x) a is constant. All ten match the answers key.

questions.question: Find the limit of the vector function r(t) = 2t î + t³ ĵ + k̂ when t → 2.
questions.explanation: Take the limit of each component at t = 2.

questions.question: If u = 5 î − 2t ĵ and v = î − 3t k̂ are vector functions and k = t + 1 is a scalar function, find: (i) lim<sub>t→0</sub> [u − v]  (ii) lim<sub>t→1</sub> [u · v]  (iii) lim<sub>t→1</sub> [u × v]  (iv) lim<sub>t→5</sub> [k u]
Check the continuity of the function G(t) = (t + 8) î + 6/(t−8) ĵ + ln(t + 8) k̂ at t = 0.
questions.answer: Continuous: lim<sub>t→0</sub> G(t) = 8 î − (3/4) ĵ + ln 8 k̂ = G(0)
questions.explanation: Each component is continuous at t = 0 (t = 8 and t = −8 are the only trouble points).

questions.question: For what values of t is the vector function r(t) = √(36 − t²) î + ln(t + 4) ĵ continuous?
questions.explanation: 36 − t² ≥ 0 gives −6 ≤ t ≤ 6; ln(t+4) needs t > −4; intersect.

questions.question: Find f′(t) of the following vector functions: (i) f(t) = e^(t⁴) î + (t³ + 3) ĵ + cosec t² k̂  (ii) f(t) = (1/t) î + e^(2t³) ĵ + sec t³ k̂
questions.answer:
(i) 4t³e^(t⁴) î + 3t² ĵ − 2t cosec t² cot t² k̂
(ii) −(1/t²) î + 6t²e^(2t³) ĵ + 3t² sec t³ tan t³ k̂
questions.explanation: Chain rule on each component. The key prints the î component of (ii) as "ln t" (misprint); d/dt(1/t) = −1/t².

questions.question: A particle moves along the curve x = t³ + 2t, y = 3e^(−2t), z = 2 sin(5t) (distances in cm, time in s). Find the magnitude of the acceleration of the particle at t = 0.
questions.explanation: a = (6t, 12e^(−2t), −50 sin 5t); at t = 0 this is (0, 12, 0).

questions.question: The path of a particle is given for time t > 0 by x = t + 2/t and y = 3t². Find the velocity of the particle when t = 1 and the acceleration at t = 2.

Evaluate by standard formulae: (i) ∫9x⁵ dx  (ii) ∫15/x³ dx  (iii) ∫a/√(bx) dx  (iv) ∫b y^(2/3) dy  (v) ∫(3x²−9x+5) dx  (vi) ∫(2x⁻⁵+3x⁻²) dx  (vii) ∫(x⁵+3x³−5x+6)/x⁴ dx  (viii) ∫(cos x+3 sin x) dx  (ix) ∫(3 sec x−cosec x) dx  (x) ∫(2 tan x−5 sec x) dx  (xi) ∫(9eˣ−3 cos x−5 sin x) dx  (xii) ∫(sec²x+cosec²x) dx
questions.answer:
(i) (3/2)x⁶ + C
(ii) −15/(2x²) + C
(iii) 2a√(x/b) + C
(iv) (3/5)b y^(5/3) + C
(v) x³ − (9/2)x² + 5x + C
(vi) −1/(2x⁴) − 3/x + C
(vii) x²/2 + 3 ln|x| + 5/(2x²) − 2/x³ + C
(viii) sin x − 3 cos x + C
(ix) ln|(sec x+tan x)³/(cosec x−cot x)| + C
(x) ln|sec²x/(sec x+tan x)⁵| + C
(xi) 9eˣ − 3 sin x + 5 cos x + C
(xii) tan x − cot x + C
questions.explanation: Power rule term by term; (ix)–(x) use ∫sec = ln|sec+tan|, ∫cosec = ln|cosec−cot|, ∫tan = ln|sec|.

questions.question: Evaluate: (i) ∫(3x²+9x+3)^½ (6x+9) dx  (ii) ∫√(ax²+2bx+c) (ax+b) dx  (iii) ∫(6x+5)/√(3x²+5x+2) dx  (iv) ∫(x²+4x+3)^(−9) (2x+4) dx  (v) ∫(x−2)(x−3)(x−4) dx  (vi) ∫(2x²−3)² dx  (vii) ∫(x³−3x²+9)^(7/2) (x²−2x) dx  (viii) ∫(x²−5)³ dx  (ix) ∫(cos x+sin x)^(3/2) (cos x−sin x) dx  (x) ∫(tan x+sin x)(sec²x+cos x) dx
questions.answer:
(i) (2/3)(3x²+9x+3)^(3/2) + C
(ii) (1/3)(ax²+2bx+c)^(3/2) + C
(iii) 2√(3x²+5x+2) + C
(iv) −1/(8(x²+4x+3)⁴) + C
(v) x⁴/4 − 3x³ + 13x² − 24x + C
(vi) (4/5)x⁵ − 4x³ + 9x + C
(vii) (2/27)(x³−3x²+9)^(9/2) + C
(viii) x⁷/7 − 3x⁵ + 25x³ − 125x + C
(ix) (2/5)(cos x+sin x)^(5/2) + C
(x) ½(tan x+sin x)² + C
questions.explanation: In (i)–(iv), (vii), (ix), (x) the second factor is (a multiple of) the derivative of the inner function; (v), (vi), (viii) expand first.

questions.question: Evaluate: (i) ∫x/(x²+3) dx  (ii) ∫(sec²x+cos x)/(tan x+sin x) dx  (iii) ∫(5x⁴+4x³−3x²+2x)/(x⁵+x⁴−x³+x²) dx  (iv) ∫(eˣ+1/x)/(eˣ+ln x) dx  (v) ∫(5x²−2x+2)/(5x³−3x²+6x−9) dx  (vi) ∫dx/(x+√x)
questions.answer:
(i) ½ ln|x²+3| + C
(ii) ln|tan x+sin x| + C
(iii) ln|x⁵+x⁴−x³+x²| + C
(iv) ln|eˣ+ln x| + C
(v) (1/3) ln|5x³−3x²+6x−9| + C
(vi) 2 ln|√x+1| + C
questions.explanation: Each is of the form ∫f′/f = ln|f|; in (v) the numerator is one third of the derivative; in (vi) write x+√x = √x(√x+1) and substitute u = √x+1.

questions.question: Evaluate: (i) ∫eˣ(sin x+cos x) dx  (ii) ∫eˣ(sin⁻¹x + 1/√(1−x²)) dx  (iii) ∫eˣ(tan⁻¹x + 1/(1+x²)) dx  (iv) ∫eˣ(sec²x+tan x) dx  (v) ∫eˣ(1/x+ln x) dx
questions.answer:
(i) eˣ sin x + C
(ii) eˣ sin⁻¹x + C
(iii) eˣ tan⁻¹x + C
(iv) eˣ tan x + C
(v) eˣ ln x + C
questions.explanation: Each integrand is eˣ(f + f′), whose integral is eˣf.

questions.question: Evaluate: (i) ∫dx/(x²+9)  (ii) ∫dt/√(4−t²)  (iii) ∫dy/(y√(y²−9))  (iv) ∫dt/(4t²−9)  (v) ∫dx/√(9x²+16)  (vi) ∫dx/√(16x²−9)  (vii) ∫dx/(9−x²)  (viii) ∫dx/(x√(4x²−16))  (ix) ∫√(9−4x²) dx  (x) ∫√(25+9x²) dx  (xi) ∫dy/(9y²+81)  (xii) ∫dx/(4x²−16)
questions.explanation: Standard inverse-trig and logarithmic forms after scaling the variable (u = 2x, 3x or 4x as needed); (ix), (x) use the √(a²−u²) and √(a²+u²) area-type formulae.

questions.question: Evaluate by substitution: (i) ∫3x/√(x²+7) dx  (ii) ∫x^(4/3)(a^(7/3) − x^(7/3))^(5/2) dx  (iii) ∫(1+2x)/√(1−x) dx  (iv) ∫(2x²+4x+5)^(3/2)(x+1) dx  (v) ∫x/√(1−x²) dx  (vi) ∫(x+1)/(x²+2x+5) dx  (vii) ∫x³(9+x²)^(3/2) dx  (viii) ∫(x³−9)^(5/2) x⁵ dx  (ix) ∫x⁹(x⁵+3)^(2/5) dx  (x) ∫(3x²+2x+5)/(x³+x²+5x−1) dx
questions.explanation: In each case the algebraic factor outside is (a multiple of) the derivative of the inner function; in (vii)–(ix) the leftover power of x is also rewritten in u. The key's plus sign in (ii) is a misprint.

questions.question: Evaluate by substitution: (i) ∫(ln x)/x dx  (ii) ∫dx/(x ln x)  (iii) ∫tan x/ln(cos x) dx  (iv) ∫tan(ln x)/x dx  (v) ∫(1+e^(2x))^(−½) e^(2x) dx  (vi) ∫5e^(5 tan x)/cos²x dx  (vii) ∫e^(2x)/(eˣ+e^(−x)) dx  (viii) ∫e^(cosec 2x+1)(cosec 2x cot 2x) dx  (ix) ∫3ˣ dx  (x) ∫e^(sin x+cos x+3)(cos x − sin x) dx
questions.answer:
(i) ½(ln x)² + C
(ii) ln|ln x| + C
(iii) −ln|ln(cos x)| + C
(iv) ln|sec(ln x)| + C
(v) √(1+e^(2x)) + C
(vi) e^(5 tan x) + C
(vii) eˣ − tan⁻¹(eˣ) + C
(viii) −½ e^(cosec 2x+1) + C
(ix) 3ˣ/ln 3 + C
(x) e^(sin x+cos x+3) + C
questions.explanation: (vii) write eˣ+e^(−x) = (e^(2x)+1)/eˣ and substitute u = eˣ: ∫u²/(u²+1) du.

questions.question: Evaluate by substitution: (i) ∫cos⁵2x sin 2x dx  (ii) ∫cot√x/√x dx  (iii) ∫(2+sin 3x)⁶ cos 3x dx  (iv) ∫sin(ax+b) dx  (v) ∫(sin x+cos x)/(sin x−cos x) dx  (vi) ∫e^(2x) sec²(e^(2x)) dx  (vii) ∫cosec 3x cot 3x/(a+b cosec 3x)² dx  (viii) ∫dx/((2 cot x+3) sin²x)  (ix) ∫sec x/(3 sin x+4 cos x) dx  (x) ∫cos(3x−5) dx
questions.answer:
(i) −(1/12)cos⁶2x + C
(ii) 2 ln|sin√x| + C
(iii) (1/21)(2+sin 3x)⁷ + C
(iv) −(1/a)cos(ax+b) + C
(v) ln|sin x−cos x| + C
(vi) ½ tan(e^(2x)) + C
(vii) 1/(3b(a+b cosec 3x)) + C
(viii) −½ ln|2 cot x+3| + C
(ix) (1/3) ln|3 tan x+4| + C
(x) (1/3) sin(3x−5) + C
questions.explanation: (viii) 1/sin²x = cosec²x is −½ d/dx(2 cot x+3). (ix) divide numerator and denominator by cos²x to get ∫sec²x/(3 tan x+4) dx.

questions.question: Evaluate: (i) ∫cos²2y dy  (ii) ∫sin³(3x+5) dx  (iii) ∫cos³x √(sin x) dx  (iv) ∫sin⁴x cos⁵x dx  (v) ∫sin³x/√(cos x) dx  (vi) ∫cos⁵x sin⁷x dx  (vii) ∫sin³x cos³x dx  (viii) ∫sin 2x cos 4x dx  (ix) ∫cos 3x cos 5x dx  (x) ∫sin 3x cos 7x dx  (xi) ∫tan²x dx  (xii) ∫cot⁴x dx  (xiii) ∫tan⁷x dx  (xiv) ∫sec⁴2x dx  (xv) ∫tan⁵3x sec³3x dx  (xvi) ∫cosec⁴3x dx  (xvii) ∫sec⁴x √(tan x) dx  (xviii) ∫cot 2x cosec⁴2x dx  (xix) ∫cosec⁴x/√(cot x) dx  (xx) ∫√(1+cos x) dx
questions.answer:

(ii) −(1/3)cos(3x+5) + (1/9)cos³(3x+5) + C
(iii) (2/3)sin^(3/2)x − (2/7)sin^(7/2)x + C
(iv) sin⁵x/5 − 2sin⁷x/7 + sin⁹x/9 + C
(v) −2√(cos x) + (2/5)cos^(5/2)x + C
(vi) sin⁴x/8 − sin¹⁰x/5 + sin¹²x/12 + C
(vii) sin⁴x/4 − sin⁶x/6 + C
(viii) −(1/12)cos 6x + (1/4)cos 2x + C
(ix) (1/16)sin 8x + (1/4)sin 2x + C
(x) −(1/20)cos 10x + (1/8)cos 4x + C
(xi) tan x − x + C
(xii) −(1/3)cot³x + cot x + x + C
(xiii) tan⁶x/6 − tan⁴x/4 + tan²x/2 + ln|cos x| + C
(xiv) ½ tan 2x + (1/6)tan³2x + C
(xv) (1/21)sec⁷3x − (2/15)sec⁵3x + (1/9)sec³3x + C
(xvi) −(1/3)cot 3x − (1/9)cot³3x + C
(xvii) (2/3)tan^(3/2)x + (2/7)tan^(7/2)x + C
(xviii) −(1/4)cot²2x − (1/8)cot⁴2x + C

questions.question: Evaluate ∫x³dx/√(9−x²).
questions.explanation: u = 9−x², x³dx = (9−u)(−du/2).

questions.question: Evaluate ∫6dx/(9−x²).
questions.explanation: 6 · (1/6) ln|(3+x)/(3−x)|.

questions.question: Evaluate ∫x²√(9−x²) dx.
questions.explanation: x = 3 sin θ gives 81∫sin²θ cos²θ dθ = (81/8)(θ − sin 4θ/4).

questions.question: Evaluate ∫5dx/(25x²+9).
Evaluate ∫dx/(4+x²)^(3/2).
questions.explanation: x = 2 tan θ reduces it to (1/4)∫cos θ dθ.

questions.question: Evaluate ∫dx/√(16+4x²).
questions.explanation: √(16+4x²) = 2√(4+x²).

questions.question: Evaluate ∫x³√(9x²−36) dx.
questions.explanation: 3∫x³√(x²−4) dx with u = x²−4.

questions.question: Evaluate ∫dx/√(a²+x²).
questions.explanation: x = a tan θ.

questions.question: Evaluate ∫dx/(16−x²)^(5/2).
questions.explanation: x = 4 sin θ gives (1/256)∫sec⁴θ dθ = (1/256)(tan θ + tan³θ/3). The key's second numerator "x" is a misprint for x³.

questions.question: Evaluate ∫x⁵dx/√(x²−9).
questions.explanation: u = x²−9, x⁵dx = (u+9)² du/2.

questions.question: Evaluate ∫dx/(x²+4x+5).
Evaluate ∫dx/√(5+4x−x²).
questions.explanation: 5+4x−x² = 9−(x−2)².

questions.question: Evaluate ∫dx/√(9x−x²).
questions.explanation: 9x−x² = 81/4 − (x−9/2)².

questions.question: Evaluate ∫dx/((x+1)√(x²+2x−15)).
questions.explanation: x²+2x−15 = (x+1)²−16; u = x+1.

questions.question: Evaluate ∫dx/((x−4)√(x²−8x−9)).
questions.explanation: x²−8x−9 = (x−4)²−25; u = x−4.

questions.question: Evaluate ∫(2x−5)dx/√(8x−x²).
questions.explanation: Split 2x−5 = −(8−2x) + 3; the remainder uses 8x−x² = 16−(x−4)².

questions.question: Evaluate ∫(x+3)dx/(x²+2x+5).
questions.explanation: x+3 = ½(2x+2) + 2; the remainder uses (x+1)²+4.

questions.question: Evaluate ∫(3x+9)dx/(x²+4x+4).
questions.explanation: u = x+2 turns it into ∫(3/u + 3/u²) du.

questions.question: Evaluate ∫(4x+9)dx/√(2x²+8x−10).
questions.explanation: 4x+9 = (4x+8)+1; the remainder uses 2x²+8x−10 = 2((x+2)²−9).

questions.question: Evaluate ∫(2x−5)dx/√(5+4x−x²).
questions.explanation: 2x−5 = −(4−2x) − 1; the remainder uses 5+4x−x² = 9−(x−2)².

questions.question: Integrate by parts: (i) ∫x²eˣ dx (ii) ∫x³eˣ dx (iii) ∫x cos x dx (iv) ∫ln x dx (v) ∫x² sin x dx (vi) ∫x cosec²x dx (vii) ∫x sec²x dx (viii) ∫(ln x)² dx.
questions.answer: (i) (x²−2x+2)eˣ+C (ii) (x³−3x²+6x−6)eˣ+C (iii) x sin x+cos x+C (iv) x(ln x−1)+C (v) 2(x sin x+cos x)−x² cos x+C (vi) ln|sin x|−x cot x+C (vii) x tan x+ln|cos x|+C (viii) x(ln x)²+2x(1−ln x)+C
questions.explanation: u = the algebraic or logarithmic factor, dv = the rest; (i)–(ii) reduce ∫xⁿeˣdx repeatedly; (viii) ∫(ln x)²dx = x(ln x)² − 2∫ln x dx.

questions.question: Integrate by parts: (i) ∫(x+1) ln(x+1) dx (ii) ∫x ln x dx (iii) ∫x⁻³ ln x dx (iv) ∫x⁻⁴ ln x² dx (v) ∫sin x cos x ln(sin x) dx (vi) ∫(tan x/cos²x) ln(tan x) dx (vii) ∫cot x cosec²x ln(cot x) dx (viii) ∫sec³x tan x ln(sec x) dx (ix) ∫cosec x cot x ln(cosec x) dx (x) ∫(ln x²)/x² dx (xi) ∫sec³x dx (xii) ∫cosec³x dx.
questions.answer: (i) (1/4)(x+1)²(ln(x+1)²−1)+C (ii) (1/4)x²(ln x²−1)+C (iii) −(1/(4x²))(1+ln x²)+C (iv) −(1/(9x³))(ln x⁶+2)+C (v) (1/4)sin²x{ln(sin x)²−1}+C (vi) (1/4)tan²x{ln(tan x)²−1}+C (vii) −(1/4)cot²x{ln(cot x)²−1}+C (viii) (1/9)sec³x{ln(sec x)³−1}+C (ix) cosec x(1−ln|cosec x|)+C (x) −(2/x)(1+ln x)+C (xi) (1/2)sec x tan x+ln√(sec x+tan x)+C (xii) −(1/2)cosec x cot x+ln√(cosec x−cot x)+C
questions.explanation: u = the logarithmic factor throughout, e.g. (iv) 2∫x⁻⁴ ln x dx = 2[−(ln x)/(3x³) − 1/(9x³)]; (xi)–(xii) reduction: 2I = sec x tan x + ln|sec x+tan x|, and the cosec analogue.

questions.question: Integrate by parts: (i) ∫3x cos 3x dx (ii) ∫x² sin x dx (iii) ∫(x/cot²x) dx (iv) ∫x sec²x dx (v) ∫(5x/sin²2x) dx (vi) ∫cos √x dx (vii) ∫e²ˣ sin 2x dx (viii) ∫e⁻ˣ cos 2x dx (ix) ∫cos(ln x) dx (x) ∫eʰˣ sin bx dx.
questions.answer: (i) x sin 3x+(1/3)cos 3x+C (ii) (2−x²)cos x+2x sin x+C (iii) x tan x−ln|sec x|−x²/2+C (iv) x tan x+ln|cos x|+C (v) (5/4)[−2x cot 2x+ln|sin 2x|]+C (vi) 2√x sin√x+2 cos√x+C (vii) (1/4)e²ˣ(sin 2x−cos 2x)+C (viii) (1/5)e⁻ˣ(2 sin 2x−cos 2x)+C (ix) (1/2)x[sin(ln x)+cos(ln x)]+C (x) eʰˣ(a sin bx−b cos bx)/(a²+b²)+C
questions.explanation: (iii) x/cot²x = x tan²x = x(sec²x−1); (v) 5∫x cosec²2x dx; (vi) t = √x gives 2∫t cos t dt; (vii)–(x) ∫eʰˣ sin bx dx = eʰˣ(a sin bx − b cos bx)/(a²+b²) and the cosine analogue; (ix) pair I with ∫sin(ln x)dx.

questions.question: Integrate by parts: (i) ∫sin⁻¹3x dx (ii) ∫x⁴ tan⁻¹x dx (iii) ∫tan⁻¹(2x) dx (iv) ∫x cos⁻¹x dx (v) ∫3x² sin⁻¹(3x) dx (vi) ∫2x sec⁻¹x dx (vii) ∫6x cosec⁻¹(2x) dx (viii) ∫x² cot⁻¹x dx.
questions.explanation: u = the inverse-trigonometric factor; the leftover integrals use x⁵/(1+x²) = x³−x+x/(1+x²), x²/√(1−x²), x/√(x²−1), x/√(4x²−1) and x³/(1+x²) = x−x/(1+x²).

questions.question: Integrate by parts: (i) ∫√(9−x²) dx (ii) ∫√(16+4x²) dx (iii) ∫√(x²−25) dx.
questions.explanation: Standard radical results obtained by one integration by parts; (ii) √(16+4x²) = 2√(4+x²).

questions.question: Evaluate by partial fractions ∫(5x−2)dx/((x−3)(x+7)).
Evaluate by partial fractions ∫(7x−25)dx/((x−3)(x−4)).
questions.explanation: A = 4 at x = 3, B = 3 at x = 4.

questions.question: Evaluate by partial fractions ∫dx/(a²−x²).
Evaluate by partial fractions ∫dx/(x²−a²).
questions.explanation: 1/(x²−a²) = (1/(2a))[1/(x−a) − 1/(x+a)].

questions.question: Evaluate by partial fractions ∫(x²+2x+3)dx/(x³−x).
questions.explanation: x³−x = x(x−1)(x+1); A = −3, B = 3, C = 1.

questions.question: Evaluate by partial fractions ∫5dx/(x²−2x−15).
questions.explanation: x²−2x−15 = (x−5)(x+3); A = 5/8, B = −5/8.

questions.question: Evaluate by partial fractions ∫(2x+7)dx/((x−1)(x−5)(x+3)).
questions.explanation: Cover-up: A = −9/16, B = 17/32, C = 1/32. The key's −19/16 on ln(x−1) is a misprint: only −9/16 makes the residues sum to zero.

questions.question: Evaluate by partial fractions ∫(5x+6)dx/((x+3)(x−2)²).
questions.explanation: A = −9/25, B = 9/25, C = 16/5; ∫C/(x−2)²dx = −C/(x−2).

questions.question: Evaluate by partial fractions ∫(7x²−2x+5)dx/((x−6)(x−3)³).
questions.explanation: u = x−3: numerator 7u²+40u+62 over u³(u−3); expand 1/(u−3) to read off the coefficients.

questions.question: Evaluate by partial fractions ∫(2x+1)dx/((x−3)(x²+1)).
questions.explanation: A = 7/10, Bx+C = −(7/10)x − 1/10; the linear part gives −(7/20)ln(x²+1) − (1/10)tan⁻¹x.

questions.question: Evaluate by partial fractions ∫sec²x dx/((1+tan x)(2+tan x)).
questions.explanation: t = tan x, dt = sec²x dx; 1/((1+t)(2+t)) = 1/(1+t) − 1/(2+t).

questions.question: Evaluate by partial fractions ∫cosec²x dx/(cot x(2+cot x)).
questions.explanation: u = cot x, du = −cosec²x dx; (1/2)ln|(2+cot x)/cot x| = (1/2)ln|1+2 tan x|.

questions.question: Evaluate by partial fractions ∫(3x+7)dx/((2x−1)(x−4)²).
Evaluate by partial fractions ∫(7x−4)dx/((x−3)(x²+2)).
Evaluate by partial fractions ∫(2x²+5x+1)dx/(x²+5x+6).
Evaluate by partial fractions ∫(x³+3x+1)dx/(x²+5x−14).
questions.explanation: Division gives x − 5 + (42x−69)/((x−2)(x+7)); A = 5/3, B = 121/3.

questions.question: Evaluate the definite integrals: (i) ∫₀²(4x³+3x²+5)dx (ii) ∫⁻₁²(x²+1)²dx (iii) ∫₁²(θ+√θ)³dθ (iv) ∫₁³(y+1/√y)²dy (v) ∫₀⁴dx/(√(2+x)+√x).
questions.explanation: Direct antiderivatives; (v) rationalize: (1/2)∫(√(2+x)−√x)dx.

questions.question: Evaluate the definite integrals: (i) ∫₁⁴x(x²+9)^(3/2)dx (ii) ∫₂⁵x dx/(7x²+2) (iii) ∫₀³(2x+3)dx/√(2x²+6x+5) (iv) ∫₁²(x³+2x)^(−1/2)(3x²+2)dx (v) ∫₀^(π/2)cos³x dx (vi) ∫_(π²/4)^(π²/36) sin√x/√x dx (vii) ∫₀^(π/4)√(tan x)sec²x dx (viii) ∫₀²e⁵ˣ⁻²dx (ix) ∫₀^(π/3)cos³3x sin²3x dx (x) ∫₀^(π/3)tan²x sec⁴x dx.
questions.explanation: Substitutions u = x²+9, 7x²+2, 2x²+6x+5, x³+2x, t = tan x, t = √x; (ix) the integrand is odd about t = π/2 after t = 3x. The key's eⁱ⁶ in (viii) is a misprint for eⁱ⁰.

questions.question: Compute by basic properties: (i) ∫₂²(x⁴+2x+3)^(5/2)(2x³+1)dx (ii) ∫⁻₅₀^⁵⁰(10x⁹−8x⁷+6x⁵−4x³+2x)dx (iii) ∫_(−π/2)^(π/2)sin⁹x cos⁶x dx (iv) ∫_−π^πsec⁸x tan x dx (v) ∫_(−π/2)^(π/2)sin²x cos²x dx (vi) ∫_(−π/4)^(π/4)tan²x dx (vii) ∫⁻₂₂(x⁴+2x²)dx.
questions.explanation: (i) equal limits; (ii)–(iv) odd integrands on symmetric intervals; (v)–(vii) even, double the half integral.

questions.question: Given that d/dx(x/√(1+x²)) = 1/(1+x²)^(3/2), evaluate ∫₀³dx/(1+x²)^(3/2).
questions.explanation: The given derivative is the antiderivative: [x/√(1+x²)]₀³.

questions.question: Given that d/dx[F(x)] = (2+x²)/(1+x²), evaluate F(√3)−F(1); if F(1) = π, find F(x).
Given ∫⁻₂³f(x)dx = 4 and ∫₅³f(x)dx = 7, evaluate: (i) ∫₃⁻²f(x)dx (ii) ∫⁻₂³f(y)dy (iii) ∫₃⁵f(y)dy (iv) ∫₂²f(x)dx (v) ∫⁻₂⁵f(x)dx (vi) ∫₅⁻²f(y)dy.
questions.explanation: Reversing limits changes sign; the dummy variable is irrelevant; ∫⁻₂⁵ = ∫⁻₂³ + ∫₃⁵.

questions.question: Evaluate by trigonometric substitution: (i) ∫₀²dx/√(16−x²) (ii) ∫⁻₁¹dx/(4−x²) (iii) ∫₃^(2√3)x³dx/√(x²+4) (iv) ∫₀^√3x²√(3−x²)dx.
questions.explanation: (i) x = 4 sin θ; (ii) partial fractions or x = 2 sin θ; (iii) u = x²+4 gives [( √(x²+4)/3)(x²−8)]₃^(2√3) — the key's 10 2/3 is the value with lower limit 0; (iv) x = √3 sin θ gives 9∫₀^(π/2)sin²θcos²θdθ.

questions.question: Compute by integration by parts: (i) ∫₅⁹xe⁴ˣdx (ii) ∫₁⁴x²ln x dx (iii) ∫_(π/6)^(π/2)x sin 2x dx (iv) ∫₀¹tan⁻¹x dx.
questions.explanation: (i) uv with u = x; (ii) u = ln x; (iii) u = x, dv = sin 2x dx; (iv) u = tan⁻¹x leaves ∫x/(1+x²)dx.

questions.question: Find the area above the x-axis under y = 3x²+2 between x = 1 and x = 2.
Find the area above the x-axis under y = 1/√(4−x²) between x = 1/2 and x = √3/2.
Find the area above the x-axis under y = ln x between x = 1 and x = 3.
questions.explanation: [x ln x − x]₁³.

questions.question: Find the area above the x-axis under y = x sin x between x = π/3 and x = π/2.
questions.explanation: [sin x − x cos x] = 1 − (√3/2 − π/6).

questions.question: Find the area above the x-axis under y = 1/(9+x²) between x = −√3 and x = √3.
questions.explanation: (1/3)[tan⁻¹(x/3)]; even integrand gives (2/3)tan⁻¹(1/√3).

questions.question: Find the area above the x-axis under y = 4x³+3x²+2x+1 between x = 0 and x = 2.
Find the area above the x-axis under y = 3 sec²x between x = π/6 and x = π/3.
questions.explanation: 3[tan x] = 3(√3 − 1/√3).

questions.question: Find the area above the x-axis under y = 6 sin²x between x = 0 and x = π/3.
questions.explanation: 6 sin²x = 3(1−cos 2x); 3[x − (sin 2x)/2]₀^(π/3).

questions.question: Find the area above the x-axis under y = 5e⁵ˣ between x = −2 and x = 3.
Find the area above the x-axis under y = cos⁴x between x = 0 and x = π/2.
Find the area above the x-axis under y = 4/sin²x between x = π/6 and x = π/4.
questions.explanation: 4∫cosec²x dx = 4[−cot x].

questions.question: Find the area above the x-axis under x²+y² = 36 between x = −1 and x = 1.
Find the area above the x-axis under x²/4+y²/9 = 1 between x = −1 and x = 1.
questions.explanation: y = (3/2)√(4−x²); 3[(x/2)√(4−x²)+2 sin⁻¹(x/2)]₀¹ doubled by symmetry.

questions.question: Find the area above the x-axis under y² = 2x+5 between x = 1 and x = 2.
Find the area above the x-axis under y² = tan⁴x between x = π/6 and x = π/4.
questions.explanation: y = tan²x = sec²x−1; [tan x − x].

questions.question: Write MAPLE commands to find the integration of: (i) f(x) = e²ˣ (ii) f(x) = sin x (iii) f(x) = cos 2x (iv) f(x) = ln(1+x) (v) f(x) = 1/x.
questions.answer: (i) > int(e²ˣ, x = 1..5) (ii) > int(sin(x), x = 0..4π) (iii) > int(cos(2x), x = 0..π/2) (iv) > int(ln(1+x), x = 0..3) (v) > int(1/x, x = 2..5)
questions.explanation: MAPLE's int command with the ranges as printed in the key.

questions.question: Choose the correct option: (i) ∫fⁿ(x)f′(x)dx, n ≠ −1 (ii) same with n = −1 (iii) ∫xⁿdx, n = −1 (iv) ∫sin x cos x dx (v) ∫x²ln e^(x²)dx (vi) ∫e^(ln x³)dx (vii) ∫(1+tan²x)dx (viii) ∫2eˣ/(1+eˣ)dx (ix) ∫e^(x+3 ln x)/x³dx (x) ∫ln(eˣ·e^(sin x))dx (xi) ∫[1/(x√(x²−1))]/cosec⁻¹x dx (xii) F antiderivative of f: ∫₀ʲf(x)dx (xiii) ∫⁻₅₀^⁵⁰(x³+x)dx (xiv) ∫_(−π/2)^(π/2)sin⁹x cosⁱⁱx dx (xv) ∫_(−π/2)^(π/2)sinⁱ⁰x cosⁱⁱx dx (xvi) area under y = ln e^(x²) from −1 to 1 (xvii) ∫₀ʲf(x)dx equals (xviii) ∫₂²(x³+3x²−5x^(−1/2))dx (xix) ∫⁻²²(x⁵−x³+x)⁵(5x⁴−3x²+1)dx (xx) ∫dx/(a²+x²).
questions.answer:
(i) (d) f^(n+1)(x)/(n+1)+c
(ii) (c) ln|f(x)|+c
(iii) (d) ln x+c
(iv) (d) −(1/4)cos 2x+c
(v) (b) x⁵/5+c
(vi) (c) x⁴/4+c
(vii) (a) tan x+c
(viii) (b) ln(1+eˣ)²+c
(ix) (b) eˣ+c
(x) (c) x²/2−cos x+c
(xi) (a) ln(cosec⁻¹x)⁻¹+c
(xii) (b) F(b)−F(a)
(xiii) (a) 0
(xiv) (c) 0
(xv) (d) 2∫₀^(π/2)sinⁱ⁰x cosⁱⁱx dx
(xvi) (a) 2/3
(xvii) (c) −∫ʲ₀f(x)dx
(xviii) (a) 0
(xix) (b) 0
(xx) (c) (1/a)tan⁻¹(x/a)+c
questions.explanation: (viii) the key prints (a) but d/dx ln(1+eˣ) = eˣ/(1+eˣ), half the integrand, so (b) is correct; (xix) u = x⁵−x³+x is odd with u(±2) = ±26, so [u⁶/6] vanishes. All others match the key letters.

questions.question: Evaluate: (i) ∫(5x²−3x+1)/(x²(x+1))dx (ii) ∫dx/(sin x cos x) (iii) ∫e³ˣ/(1+e⁶ˣ)dx (iv) ∫(ln x)⁷/x dx (v) ∫5cos x dx/(6+sin x−sin²x) (vi) ∫x sec²x dx (vii) ∫dθ/(cot θ−tan θ) (viii) ∫x/(1+√x)dx (ix) ∫(3+3tan²x)/(1+9tan²x)dx (x) ∫cot⁻¹2x dx (xi) ∫(1−√x)/(1+√x)dx (xii) ∫sin⁵x√(cos x)dx.
questions.answer:
(i) ln|(x+1)⁹/x⁴|−1/x+c
(ii) ln|tan x|+c
(iii) (1/3)tan⁻¹(e³ˣ)+c
(iv) (ln x)⁸/8+c
(v) ln|(sin x+2)/(sin x−3)|+c
(vi) x tan x+ln|cos x|+c
(vii) (1/4)ln|sec 2θ|+c
(viii) (2/3)x^(3/2)−x+2√x−2 ln(√x+1)+c
(ix) tan⁻¹(3 tan x)+c
(x) x cot⁻¹2x+(1/2)ln(1+4x²)+c
(xi) 4√x−x−ln(√x+1)⁴+c
(xii) −(2/3)cos^(3/2)x+(4/7)cos^(7/2)x−(2/11)cos^(11/2)x+C
questions.explanation: Flags vs key: (i) the key's ln|x⁻³(x²+1)^(3/2)|−1/x+4tan⁻¹x is the antiderivative of the (x²+1) variant, not the printed x²(x+1); (vii) cot θ−tan θ = 2cot 2θ so the argument is 2θ, the key omits it; (viii) the log term is −2ln(√x+1), the key doubles it; (x) the log term is (1/2)ln(1+4x²), the key's exponent 1/4 halves it. (ii)–(vi), (ix), (xi), (xii) match the key.

questions.question: Find the distance between the following pairs of points: (i) A(−1, 3) and B(5, −5)  (ii) C(−1, 0) and D(0, −1)  (iii) E(1, −1) and F(2, 7)  (iv) G(−1, −4) and H(5, −4)
questions.explanation: Distance formula on each pair: (i) √(36+64)=10; (ii) √(1+1)=√2; (iii) √(1+64)=√65; (iv) √(36+0)=6. All match the key.

questions.question: Find the point on the y-axis which is 5√2 units away from (5, 2).
questions.explanation: P(0, y): 25+(y−2)²=50 → (y−2)²=25 → y=7 or −3. Matches the key.

questions.question: Find the point on the x-axis which is √41 units away from (−7, 5).
questions.explanation: P(x, 0): (x+7)²+25=41 → (x+7)²=16 → x=−3 or −11. Matches the key.

questions.question: If ABC is a triangle whose vertices are A(−3, 3), B(2, 6) and C(3, 0), give the most specific name for triangle ABC.
questions.explanation: |AB|=√34, |BC|=√37, |CA|=√45; all three sides differ. Matches the key.

questions.question: If the point P(2, 1) lies on the line segment joining the points A(4, 2) and B(8, 4), then show that |AP| = ½|AB|.
questions.explanation: |AP|=√(4+1)=√5; |AB|=√(16+4)=2√5; ½|AB|=√5=|AP|.

questions.question: Find the coordinates of the midpoint of following points: (i) M(−4, 2) and N(−4, −2)  (ii) P(−1, −4) and Q(5, −4)  (iii) S(1, −2) and T(2, −4)  (iv) X(6, 2) and Y(−2, −7)
questions.explanation: Average the two endpoints. Flag: the key prints (ii) as (2, 0), but the midpoint of (−1,−4) and (5,−4) is (2,−4) — key misprint; (i), (iii), (iv) match the key.

questions.question: Find the point which divides the line segment joining (4, −1) and (4, 3) in the ratio 3:1 internally.
questions.explanation: x=(3·4+1·4)/4=4; y=(3·3+1·(−1))/4=2. Matches the key.

questions.question: The points P(−2, 2), Q(2, −1) and R(−1, 4) are the mid-points of the sides of the triangle. Find the vertices.
questions.explanation: Each vertex = sum of two midpoints minus the third: P+Q−R=(1,−3), P+R−Q=(−5,7), Q+R−P=(3,1). Matches the key.

questions.question: Z(4, 5) and X(7, −1) are two given points and the point Y divides the line-segment ZX externally in the ratio 4:3. Find the coordinates of Y.
questions.explanation: External section: ((4·7−3·4)/(4−3), (4·(−1)−3·5)/(4−3))=(16, −19). Matches the key.

questions.question: If a point P(k, 7) divides the line segment joining A(8, 9) and B(1, 2) in a ratio k₁:k₂, then find ratio k₁:k₂. Also find the value of k.
