questions.question: Evaluate ∫dx/((x+1)√(x²+2x−15)).
questions.explanation: x²+2x−15 = (x+1)²−16; u = x+1.

questions.question: Evaluate ∫dx/((x−4)√(x²−8x−9)).
questions.explanation: x²−8x−9 = (x−4)²−25; u = x−4.

questions.question: Evaluate ∫(2x−5)dx/√(8x−x²).
questions.explanation: Split 2x−5 = −(8−2x) + 3; the remainder uses 8x−x² = 16−(x−4)².

questions.question: Evaluate ∫(x+3)dx/(x²+2x+5).
questions.explanation: x+3 = ½(2x+2) + 2; the remainder uses (x+1)²+4.

questions.question: Evaluate ∫(3x+9)dx/(x²+4x+4).
questions.explanation: u = x+2 turns it into ∫(3/u + 3/u²) du.

questions.question: Evaluate ∫(4x+9)dx/√(2x²+8x−10).
questions.explanation: 4x+9 = (4x+8)+1; the remainder uses 2x²+8x−10 = 2((x+2)²−9).

questions.question: Evaluate ∫(2x−5)dx/√(5+4x−x²).
questions.explanation: 2x−5 = −(4−2x) − 1; the remainder uses 5+4x−x² = 9−(x−2)².

questions.question: Integrate by parts: (i) ∫x²eˣ dx (ii) ∫x³eˣ dx (iii) ∫x cos x dx (iv) ∫ln x dx (v) ∫x² sin x dx (vi) ∫x cosec²x dx (vii) ∫x sec²x dx (viii) ∫(ln x)² dx.
questions.answer: (i) (x²−2x+2)eˣ+C (ii) (x³−3x²+6x−6)eˣ+C (iii) x sin x+cos x+C (iv) x(ln x−1)+C (v) 2(x sin x+cos x)−x² cos x+C (vi) ln|sin x|−x cot x+C (vii) x tan x+ln|cos x|+C (viii) x(ln x)²+2x(1−ln x)+C
questions.explanation: u = the algebraic or logarithmic factor, dv = the rest; (i)–(ii) reduce ∫xⁿeˣdx repeatedly; (viii) ∫(ln x)²dx = x(ln x)² − 2∫ln x dx.

questions.question: Integrate by parts: (i) ∫(x+1) ln(x+1) dx (ii) ∫x ln x dx (iii) ∫x⁻³ ln x dx (iv) ∫x⁻⁴ ln x² dx (v) ∫sin x cos x ln(sin x) dx (vi) ∫(tan x/cos²x) ln(tan x) dx (vii) ∫cot x cosec²x ln(cot x) dx (viii) ∫sec³x tan x ln(sec x) dx (ix) ∫cosec x cot x ln(cosec x) dx (x) ∫(ln x²)/x² dx (xi) ∫sec³x dx (xii) ∫cosec³x dx.
questions.answer: (i) (1/4)(x+1)²(ln(x+1)²−1)+C (ii) (1/4)x²(ln x²−1)+C (iii) −(1/(4x²))(1+ln x²)+C (iv) −(1/(9x³))(ln x⁶+2)+C (v) (1/4)sin²x{ln(sin x)²−1}+C (vi) (1/4)tan²x{ln(tan x)²−1}+C (vii) −(1/4)cot²x{ln(cot x)²−1}+C (viii) (1/9)sec³x{ln(sec x)³−1}+C (ix) cosec x(1−ln|cosec x|)+C (x) −(2/x)(1+ln x)+C (xi) (1/2)sec x tan x+ln√(sec x+tan x)+C (xii) −(1/2)cosec x cot x+ln√(cosec x−cot x)+C
questions.explanation: u = the logarithmic factor throughout, e.g. (iv) 2∫x⁻⁴ ln x dx = 2[−(ln x)/(3x³) − 1/(9x³)]; (xi)–(xii) reduction: 2I = sec x tan x + ln|sec x+tan x|, and the cosec analogue.

questions.question: Integrate by parts: (i) ∫3x cos 3x dx (ii) ∫x² sin x dx (iii) ∫(x/cot²x) dx (iv) ∫x sec²x dx (v) ∫(5x/sin²2x) dx (vi) ∫cos √x dx (vii) ∫e²ˣ sin 2x dx (viii) ∫e⁻ˣ cos 2x dx (ix) ∫cos(ln x) dx (x) ∫eʰˣ sin bx dx.
questions.answer: (i) x sin 3x+(1/3)cos 3x+C (ii) (2−x²)cos x+2x sin x+C (iii) x tan x−ln|sec x|−x²/2+C (iv) x tan x+ln|cos x|+C (v) (5/4)[−2x cot 2x+ln|sin 2x|]+C (vi) 2√x sin√x+2 cos√x+C (vii) (1/4)e²ˣ(sin 2x−cos 2x)+C (viii) (1/5)e⁻ˣ(2 sin 2x−cos 2x)+C (ix) (1/2)x[sin(ln x)+cos(ln x)]+C (x) eʰˣ(a sin bx−b cos bx)/(a²+b²)+C
questions.explanation: (iii) x/cot²x = x tan²x = x(sec²x−1); (v) 5∫x cosec²2x dx; (vi) t = √x gives 2∫t cos t dt; (vii)–(x) ∫eʰˣ sin bx dx = eʰˣ(a sin bx − b cos bx)/(a²+b²) and the cosine analogue; (ix) pair I with ∫sin(ln x)dx.

questions.question: Integrate by parts: (i) ∫sin⁻¹3x dx (ii) ∫x⁴ tan⁻¹x dx (iii) ∫tan⁻¹(2x) dx (iv) ∫x cos⁻¹x dx (v) ∫3x² sin⁻¹(3x) dx (vi) ∫2x sec⁻¹x dx (vii) ∫6x cosec⁻¹(2x) dx (viii) ∫x² cot⁻¹x dx.
questions.explanation: u = the inverse-trigonometric factor; the leftover integrals use x⁵/(1+x²) = x³−x+x/(1+x²), x²/√(1−x²), x/√(x²−1), x/√(4x²−1) and x³/(1+x²) = x−x/(1+x²).

questions.question: Integrate by parts: (i) ∫√(9−x²) dx (ii) ∫√(16+4x²) dx (iii) ∫√(x²−25) dx.
questions.explanation: Standard radical results obtained by one integration by parts; (ii) √(16+4x²) = 2√(4+x²).

questions.question: Evaluate by partial fractions ∫(5x−2)dx/((x−3)(x+7)).
Evaluate by partial fractions ∫(7x−25)dx/((x−3)(x−4)).
questions.explanation: A = 4 at x = 3, B = 3 at x = 4.

questions.question: Evaluate by partial fractions ∫dx/(a²−x²).
Evaluate by partial fractions ∫dx/(x²−a²).
questions.explanation: 1/(x²−a²) = (1/(2a))[1/(x−a) − 1/(x+a)].

questions.question: Evaluate by partial fractions ∫(x²+2x+3)dx/(x³−x).
questions.explanation: x³−x = x(x−1)(x+1); A = −3, B = 3, C = 1.

questions.question: Evaluate by partial fractions ∫5dx/(x²−2x−15).
questions.explanation: x²−2x−15 = (x−5)(x+3); A = 5/8, B = −5/8.

questions.question: Evaluate by partial fractions ∫(2x+7)dx/((x−1)(x−5)(x+3)).
questions.explanation: Cover-up: A = −9/16, B = 17/32, C = 1/32. The key's −19/16 on ln(x−1) is a misprint: only −9/16 makes the residues sum to zero.

questions.question: Evaluate by partial fractions ∫(5x+6)dx/((x+3)(x−2)²).
questions.explanation: A = −9/25, B = 9/25, C = 16/5; ∫C/(x−2)²dx = −C/(x−2).

questions.question: Evaluate by partial fractions ∫(7x²−2x+5)dx/((x−6)(x−3)³).
questions.explanation: u = x−3: numerator 7u²+40u+62 over u³(u−3); expand 1/(u−3) to read off the coefficients.

questions.question: Evaluate by partial fractions ∫(2x+1)dx/((x−3)(x²+1)).
questions.explanation: A = 7/10, Bx+C = −(7/10)x − 1/10; the linear part gives −(7/20)ln(x²+1) − (1/10)tan⁻¹x.

questions.question: Evaluate by partial fractions ∫sec²x dx/((1+tan x)(2+tan x)).
questions.explanation: t = tan x, dt = sec²x dx; 1/((1+t)(2+t)) = 1/(1+t) − 1/(2+t).

questions.question: Evaluate by partial fractions ∫cosec²x dx/(cot x(2+cot x)).
questions.explanation: u = cot x, du = −cosec²x dx; (1/2)ln|(2+cot x)/cot x| = (1/2)ln|1+2 tan x|.

questions.question: Evaluate by partial fractions ∫(3x+7)dx/((2x−1)(x−4)²).
Evaluate by partial fractions ∫(7x−4)dx/((x−3)(x²+2)).
Evaluate by partial fractions ∫(2x²+5x+1)dx/(x²+5x+6).
Evaluate by partial fractions ∫(x³+3x+1)dx/(x²+5x−14).
questions.explanation: Division gives x − 5 + (42x−69)/((x−2)(x+7)); A = 5/3, B = 121/3.

questions.question: Evaluate the definite integrals: (i) ∫₀²(4x³+3x²+5)dx (ii) ∫⁻₁²(x²+1)²dx (iii) ∫₁²(θ+√θ)³dθ (iv) ∫₁³(y+1/√y)²dy (v) ∫₀⁴dx/(√(2+x)+√x).
questions.explanation: Direct antiderivatives; (v) rationalize: (1/2)∫(√(2+x)−√x)dx.

questions.question: Evaluate the definite integrals: (i) ∫₁⁴x(x²+9)^(3/2)dx (ii) ∫₂⁵x dx/(7x²+2) (iii) ∫₀³(2x+3)dx/√(2x²+6x+5) (iv) ∫₁²(x³+2x)^(−1/2)(3x²+2)dx (v) ∫₀^(π/2)cos³x dx (vi) ∫_(π²/4)^(π²/36) sin√x/√x dx (vii) ∫₀^(π/4)√(tan x)sec²x dx (viii) ∫₀²e⁵ˣ⁻²dx (ix) ∫₀^(π/3)cos³3x sin²3x dx (x) ∫₀^(π/3)tan²x sec⁴x dx.
questions.explanation: Substitutions u = x²+9, 7x²+2, 2x²+6x+5, x³+2x, t = tan x, t = √x; (ix) the integrand is odd about t = π/2 after t = 3x. The key's eⁱ⁶ in (viii) is a misprint for eⁱ⁰.

questions.question: Compute by basic properties: (i) ∫₂²(x⁴+2x+3)^(5/2)(2x³+1)dx (ii) ∫⁻₅₀^⁵⁰(10x⁹−8x⁷+6x⁵−4x³+2x)dx (iii) ∫_(−π/2)^(π/2)sin⁹x cos⁶x dx (iv) ∫_−π^πsec⁸x tan x dx (v) ∫_(−π/2)^(π/2)sin²x cos²x dx (vi) ∫_(−π/4)^(π/4)tan²x dx (vii) ∫⁻₂₂(x⁴+2x²)dx.
questions.explanation: (i) equal limits; (ii)–(iv) odd integrands on symmetric intervals; (v)–(vii) even, double the half integral.

questions.question: Given that d/dx(x/√(1+x²)) = 1/(1+x²)^(3/2), evaluate ∫₀³dx/(1+x²)^(3/2).
questions.explanation: The given derivative is the antiderivative: [x/√(1+x²)]₀³.

questions.question: Given that d/dx[F(x)] = (2+x²)/(1+x²), evaluate F(√3)−F(1); if F(1) = π, find F(x).
Given ∫⁻₂³f(x)dx = 4 and ∫₅³f(x)dx = 7, evaluate: (i) ∫₃⁻²f(x)dx (ii) ∫⁻₂³f(y)dy (iii) ∫₃⁵f(y)dy (iv) ∫₂²f(x)dx (v) ∫⁻₂⁵f(x)dx (vi) ∫₅⁻²f(y)dy.
questions.explanation: Reversing limits changes sign; the dummy variable is irrelevant; ∫⁻₂⁵ = ∫⁻₂³ + ∫₃⁵.

questions.question: Evaluate by trigonometric substitution: (i) ∫₀²dx/√(16−x²) (ii) ∫⁻₁¹dx/(4−x²) (iii) ∫₃^(2√3)x³dx/√(x²+4) (iv) ∫₀^√3x²√(3−x²)dx.
questions.explanation: (i) x = 4 sin θ; (ii) partial fractions or x = 2 sin θ; (iii) u = x²+4 gives [( √(x²+4)/3)(x²−8)]₃^(2√3) — the key's 10 2/3 is the value with lower limit 0; (iv) x = √3 sin θ gives 9∫₀^(π/2)sin²θcos²θdθ.

questions.question: Compute by integration by parts: (i) ∫₅⁹xe⁴ˣdx (ii) ∫₁⁴x²ln x dx (iii) ∫_(π/6)^(π/2)x sin 2x dx (iv) ∫₀¹tan⁻¹x dx.
questions.explanation: (i) uv with u = x; (ii) u = ln x; (iii) u = x, dv = sin 2x dx; (iv) u = tan⁻¹x leaves ∫x/(1+x²)dx.

questions.question: Find the area above the x-axis under y = 3x²+2 between x = 1 and x = 2.
Find the area above the x-axis under y = 1/√(4−x²) between x = 1/2 and x = √3/2.
Find the area above the x-axis under y = ln x between x = 1 and x = 3.
questions.explanation: [x ln x − x]₁³.

questions.question: Find the area above the x-axis under y = x sin x between x = π/3 and x = π/2.
questions.explanation: [sin x − x cos x] = 1 − (√3/2 − π/6).

questions.question: Find the area above the x-axis under y = 1/(9+x²) between x = −√3 and x = √3.
questions.explanation: (1/3)[tan⁻¹(x/3)]; even integrand gives (2/3)tan⁻¹(1/√3).

questions.question: Find the area above the x-axis under y = 4x³+3x²+2x+1 between x = 0 and x = 2.
Find the area above the x-axis under y = 3 sec²x between x = π/6 and x = π/3.
questions.explanation: 3[tan x] = 3(√3 − 1/√3).

questions.question: Find the area above the x-axis under y = 6 sin²x between x = 0 and x = π/3.
questions.explanation: 6 sin²x = 3(1−cos 2x); 3[x − (sin 2x)/2]₀^(π/3).

questions.question: Find the area above the x-axis under y = 5e⁵ˣ between x = −2 and x = 3.
Find the area above the x-axis under y = cos⁴x between x = 0 and x = π/2.
Find the area above the x-axis under y = 4/sin²x between x = π/6 and x = π/4.
questions.explanation: 4∫cosec²x dx = 4[−cot x].

questions.question: Find the area above the x-axis under x²+y² = 36 between x = −1 and x = 1.
Find the area above the x-axis under x²/4+y²/9 = 1 between x = −1 and x = 1.
questions.explanation: y = (3/2)√(4−x²); 3[(x/2)√(4−x²)+2 sin⁻¹(x/2)]₀¹ doubled by symmetry.

questions.question: Find the area above the x-axis under y² = 2x+5 between x = 1 and x = 2.
Find the area above the x-axis under y² = tan⁴x between x = π/6 and x = π/4.
questions.explanation: y = tan²x = sec²x−1; [tan x − x].

questions.question: Write MAPLE commands to find the integration of: (i) f(x) = e²ˣ (ii) f(x) = sin x (iii) f(x) = cos 2x (iv) f(x) = ln(1+x) (v) f(x) = 1/x.
questions.answer: (i) > int(e²ˣ, x = 1..5) (ii) > int(sin(x), x = 0..4π) (iii) > int(cos(2x), x = 0..π/2) (iv) > int(ln(1+x), x = 0..3) (v) > int(1/x, x = 2..5)
questions.explanation: MAPLE's int command with the ranges as printed in the key.

questions.question: Choose the correct option: (i) ∫fⁿ(x)f′(x)dx, n ≠ −1 (ii) same with n = −1 (iii) ∫xⁿdx, n = −1 (iv) ∫sin x cos x dx (v) ∫x²ln e^(x²)dx (vi) ∫e^(ln x³)dx (vii) ∫(1+tan²x)dx (viii) ∫2eˣ/(1+eˣ)dx (ix) ∫e^(x+3 ln x)/x³dx (x) ∫ln(eˣ·e^(sin x))dx (xi) ∫[1/(x√(x²−1))]/cosec⁻¹x dx (xii) F antiderivative of f: ∫₀ʲf(x)dx (xiii) ∫⁻₅₀^⁵⁰(x³+x)dx (xiv) ∫_(−π/2)^(π/2)sin⁹x cosⁱⁱx dx (xv) ∫_(−π/2)^(π/2)sinⁱ⁰x cosⁱⁱx dx (xvi) area under y = ln e^(x²) from −1 to 1 (xvii) ∫₀ʲf(x)dx equals (xviii) ∫₂²(x³+3x²−5x^(−1/2))dx (xix) ∫⁻²²(x⁵−x³+x)⁵(5x⁴−3x²+1)dx (xx) ∫dx/(a²+x²).
questions.answer:
(i) (d) f^(n+1)(x)/(n+1)+c
(ii) (c) ln|f(x)|+c
(iii) (d) ln x+c
(iv) (d) −(1/4)cos 2x+c
(v) (b) x⁵/5+c
(vi) (c) x⁴/4+c
(vii) (a) tan x+c
(viii) (b) ln(1+eˣ)²+c
(ix) (b) eˣ+c
(x) (c) x²/2−cos x+c
(xi) (a) ln(cosec⁻¹x)⁻¹+c
(xii) (b) F(b)−F(a)
(xiii) (a) 0
(xiv) (c) 0
(xv) (d) 2∫₀^(π/2)sinⁱ⁰x cosⁱⁱx dx
(xvi) (a) 2/3
(xvii) (c) −∫ʲ₀f(x)dx
(xviii) (a) 0
(xix) (b) 0
(xx) (c) (1/a)tan⁻¹(x/a)+c
questions.explanation: (viii) the key prints (a) but d/dx ln(1+eˣ) = eˣ/(1+eˣ), half the integrand, so (b) is correct; (xix) u = x⁵−x³+x is odd with u(±2) = ±26, so [u⁶/6] vanishes. All others match the key letters.

questions.question: Evaluate: (i) ∫(5x²−3x+1)/(x²(x+1))dx (ii) ∫dx/(sin x cos x) (iii) ∫e³ˣ/(1+e⁶ˣ)dx (iv) ∫(ln x)⁷/x dx (v) ∫5cos x dx/(6+sin x−sin²x) (vi) ∫x sec²x dx (vii) ∫dθ/(cot θ−tan θ) (viii) ∫x/(1+√x)dx (ix) ∫(3+3tan²x)/(1+9tan²x)dx (x) ∫cot⁻¹2x dx (xi) ∫(1−√x)/(1+√x)dx (xii) ∫sin⁵x√(cos x)dx.
questions.answer:
(i) ln|(x+1)⁹/x⁴|−1/x+c
(ii) ln|tan x|+c
(iii) (1/3)tan⁻¹(e³ˣ)+c
(iv) (ln x)⁸/8+c
(v) ln|(sin x+2)/(sin x−3)|+c
(vi) x tan x+ln|cos x|+c
(vii) (1/4)ln|sec 2θ|+c
(viii) (2/3)x^(3/2)−x+2√x−2 ln(√x+1)+c
(ix) tan⁻¹(3 tan x)+c
(x) x cot⁻¹2x+(1/2)ln(1+4x²)+c
(xi) 4√x−x−ln(√x+1)⁴+c
(xii) −(2/3)cos^(3/2)x+(4/7)cos^(7/2)x−(2/11)cos^(11/2)x+C
questions.explanation: Flags vs key: (i) the key's ln|x⁻³(x²+1)^(3/2)|−1/x+4tan⁻¹x is the antiderivative of the (x²+1) variant, not the printed x²(x+1); (vii) cot θ−tan θ = 2cot 2θ so the argument is 2θ, the key omits it; (viii) the log term is −2ln(√x+1), the key doubles it; (x) the log term is (1/2)ln(1+4x²), the key's exponent 1/4 halves it. (ii)–(vi), (ix), (xi), (xii) match the key.

questions.question: Find the distance between the following pairs of points: (i) A(−1, 3) and B(5, −5)  (ii) C(−1, 0) and D(0, −1)  (iii) E(1, −1) and F(2, 7)  (iv) G(−1, −4) and H(5, −4)
questions.explanation: Distance formula on each pair: (i) √(36+64)=10; (ii) √(1+1)=√2; (iii) √(1+64)=√65; (iv) √(36+0)=6. All match the key.

questions.question: Find the point on the y-axis which is 5√2 units away from (5, 2).
questions.explanation: P(0, y): 25+(y−2)²=50 → (y−2)²=25 → y=7 or −3. Matches the key.

questions.question: Find the point on the x-axis which is √41 units away from (−7, 5).
questions.explanation: P(x, 0): (x+7)²+25=41 → (x+7)²=16 → x=−3 or −11. Matches the key.

questions.question: If ABC is a triangle whose vertices are A(−3, 3), B(2, 6) and C(3, 0), give the most specific name for triangle ABC.
questions.explanation: |AB|=√34, |BC|=√37, |CA|=√45; all three sides differ. Matches the key.

questions.question: If the point P(2, 1) lies on the line segment joining the points A(4, 2) and B(8, 4), then show that |AP| = ½|AB|.
questions.explanation: |AP|=√(4+1)=√5; |AB|=√(16+4)=2√5; ½|AB|=√5=|AP|.

questions.question: Find the coordinates of the midpoint of following points: (i) M(−4, 2) and N(−4, −2)  (ii) P(−1, −4) and Q(5, −4)  (iii) S(1, −2) and T(2, −4)  (iv) X(6, 2) and Y(−2, −7)
questions.explanation: Average the two endpoints. Flag: the key prints (ii) as (2, 0), but the midpoint of (−1,−4) and (5,−4) is (2,−4) — key misprint; (i), (iii), (iv) match the key.

questions.question: Find the point which divides the line segment joining (4, −1) and (4, 3) in the ratio 3:1 internally.
questions.explanation: x=(3·4+1·4)/4=4; y=(3·3+1·(−1))/4=2. Matches the key.

questions.question: The points P(−2, 2), Q(2, −1) and R(−1, 4) are the mid-points of the sides of the triangle. Find the vertices.
questions.explanation: Each vertex = sum of two midpoints minus the third: P+Q−R=(1,−3), P+R−Q=(−5,7), Q+R−P=(3,1). Matches the key.

questions.question: Z(4, 5) and X(7, −1) are two given points and the point Y divides the line-segment ZX externally in the ratio 4:3. Find the coordinates of Y.
questions.explanation: External section: ((4·7−3·4)/(4−3), (4·(−1)−3·5)/(4−3))=(16, −19). Matches the key.

questions.question: If a point P(k, 7) divides the line segment joining A(8, 9) and B(1, 2) in a ratio k₁:k₂, then find ratio k₁:k₂. Also find the value of k.
A(2, 7) and B(−4, −8) are coordinates of the line segment AB. There are two points that trisect the segment AB. Find the points of trisection.
questions.explanation: Section formula in ratios 1:2 and 2:1: ((−4+4)/3, (−8+14)/3)=(0,2); ((−8+2)/3, (−16+7)/3)=(−2,−3). Matches the key.

questions.question: The vertices P, Q and R of a triangle are (2, 1), (5, 2) and (3, 4) respectively. Find the coordinates of the circum-centre and also the radius of the circum-circle of the triangle.
questions.explanation: |CP|=|CQ| gives 3h+k=12; |CQ|=|CR| gives k=h−1; solving h=13/4, k=9/4; radius=|CP|=√(25/16+25/16)=5√2/4. Matches the key.

questions.question: AB is divided into 20 equal parts by P₁, P₂, P₃, ..., P₁₉. If A and B are (2, 3) and (10, 11) respectively, find the coordinates of P₁₃.
questions.explanation: P₁₃ divides AB in ratio 13:7: ((13·10+7·2)/20, (13·11+7·3)/20)=(144/20, 164/20). Matches the key.

questions.question: If A, B and C are three collinear points and the coordinates of A and B are (3, 4) and (7, 7) respectively, find the coordinates of C if |AC| = 10 units.
questions.explanation: Unit vector along AB = (4/5, 3/5); C = A + 10(4/5, 3/5) = (11, 10). The key lists only this point; (−5, −2) on the opposite ray also satisfies |AC|=10.

questions.question: Find the coordinates of the incentre of triangle whose angular points are respectively: (i) L(2, 8), M(8, 2) and N(9, 9)  (ii) P(−36, 7), Q(20, 7) and R(0, −8)
questions.explanation: Incentre = side-weighted average of vertices. (i) sides 5√2, 5√2, 6√2 → (104/16, 104/16); (ii) sides 25, 39, 56 → (−120/120, 0/120). Matches the key.

questions.question: The line segment joining P(−8, 10) and Q(6, −4) is cut by x and y axes at A and B respectively. Find the ratios in which A and B divide PQ.
questions.explanation: x-axis: y=0 → 4m=10n → m:n=5:2; y-axis: x=0 → 6m=8n → m:n=4:3. Matches the key.

questions.question: Find the coordinates of the centroid of a triangle whose angular points are: (i) A(1, 3), (2, 7) and (5, 6)  (ii) P(−2, 5), Q(−7, 1) and R(−8, −4)
questions.explanation: Centroid = average of the three vertices. Matches the key.

questions.question: A straight line passes through the points (7, 9) and (−1, 1). Find a point in the line whose ordinate is 4.
questions.explanation: Slope = 8/8 = 1; line y = x+2; ordinate 4 → x = 2. Matches the key.

questions.question: Find the slope of the line passing through given pair of points: (i) A(3, 7) and B(2, 9)  (ii) C(5, −2) and D(3, 6)  (iii) E(5, 3) and F(−2, 3)  (iv) G(0, 0) and H(a, b)
questions.explanation: m=(y₂−y₁)/(x₂−x₁): (i) 2/(−1); (ii) 8/(−2); (iii) 0/(−7); (iv) b/a. All match the key.

questions.question: Find the slope of the perpendicular line when the given line passes through the following pair of points: (i) A(2, 1) and B(4, 5)  (ii) C(−1, 0) and D(3, 5)  (iii) E(2, 1) and F(−3, 1)  (iv) G(−1, 2) and H(−1, −5)
questions.explanation: Perpendicular slope = −1/m. (i) m=2; (ii) m=5/4; (iii) m=0 so perpendicular is vertical (undefined); (iv) m undefined (vertical) so perpendicular slope 0. All match the key.

questions.question: In each of the following the slope of the line is given. What is the slope of a line (a) parallel (b) perpendicular, to it?  (i) 2/3  (ii) −7/2  (iii) −1  (iv) 4
questions.explanation: Parallel keeps m; perpendicular takes −1/m. All match the key.

questions.question: Are the lines l₁ and l₂ passing through the given pairs of points parallel, perpendicular or neither? (i) l₁: (1, 2), (3, 1) and l₂: (0, −1), (2, 0)  (ii) l₁: (0, 3), (3, 1) and l₂: (−1, 4), (−7, −5)  (iii) l₁: (2, −1), (5, −7) and l₂: (0, 0), (−1, 2)  (iv) l₁: (1, 0), (2, 0) and l₂: (5, −5), (−10, −5)
questions.explanation: (i) m₁=−1/2, m₂=1/2: neither equal nor m₁m₂=−1; (ii) m₁=−2/3, m₂=3/2: product −1; (iii) both −2; (iv) both 0. All match the key.

questions.question: The line through (6, −4) and (−3, 2) is parallel to the line through (2, 1) and (0, y). Find y.
questions.explanation: m₁=6/(−9)=−2/3; (y−1)/(−2)=−2/3 → y−1=4/3. Matches the key.

questions.question: The line through (2, 5) and (−3, −2) is perpendicular to the line through (4, −1) and (x, 3). Find x.
questions.explanation: m₁=7/5; m₂=4/(x−4); (7/5)(4/(x−4))=−1 → x−4=−28/5. Matches the key.

questions.question: Using slopes prove that (−1, 4), (−3, −6) and (3, −2) are the vertices of right triangle.
questions.answer: m(BC)·m(CA) = −1, right angle at C — proved
questions.explanation: m(AB)=5, m(BC)=2/3, m(CA)=−3/2; (2/3)(−3/2)=−1 so BC ⊥ CA. Proof question, no key entry.

questions.question: Using slopes, find the fourth vertex of a parallelogram if (0, −1), (4, −3) and (12, 3) are its three consecutive vertices.
questions.explanation: Diagonals bisect: D = A+C−B = (8, 5); slope check m(AB)=m(DC)=−1/2, m(BC)=m(AD)=3/4. Matches the key.

questions.question: Find the equations of the straight lines parallel to the coordinate axes and passing through the point (3, −4).
questions.answer: y = −4 (parallel to x-axis); x = 3 (parallel to y-axis)
questions.explanation: A horizontal line keeps the y-coordinate, a vertical line keeps the x-coordinate. Matches the key.

questions.question: Find the equations of the straight lines parallel to the coordinate axes and passing through the point (5, 2).
questions.explanation: Horizontal line y = 2; vertical line x = 5. Matches the key.

questions.question: Write the equation of the straight lines parallel to x-axis which is at a distance of 5 units from above the x-axis.
questions.explanation: Horizontal line 5 units above the x-axis. Matches the key.

questions.question: Find the equation of a line parallel to y-axis which is at a distance of 6 units on its left.
questions.explanation: Vertical line 6 units left of the y-axis. Flag: the key prints x = −5, which matches a distance of 5 units, not the printed 6 — key misprint.

questions.question: Find the equations of the straight line determined by each of the following set of conditions: (i) through (5, −2) with slope 4  (ii) through (−1, −4) with slope −2/3  (iii) through (−1/4, 3/4) with slope 2/5  (iv) through (0, b) with slope m  (v) through (7, −3) and (−4, 1)  (vi) through (5, −5) and (−3, 1)  (vii) through (at₁², 2at₁) and (at₂², 2at₂)  (viii) y-intercept 3, slope 2  (ix) y-intercept −2, slope −2/3  (x) y-intercept −5, slope 1/2  (xi) y-intercept 0, slope 0  (xii) x-intercept 4, y-intercept 3  (xiii) x-intercept −2, y-intercept 5  (xiv) x-intercept −5, y-intercept −1  (xv) perpendicular from origin p = 3 making angle α = 60° with x-axis  (xvi) p = 3/2, α = 150°
questions.answer:
(i) 4x−y−22=0
(ii) 2x+3y+14=0
(iii) 8x−20y+17=0
(iv) mx−y+b=0
(v) 4x+11y+5=0
(vi) 3x+4y+5=0
(vii) 2x−(t₁+t₂)y+2at₁t₂=0
(viii) y=2x+3
(ix) y=(−2/3)x−2
(x) y=(1/2)x−5
(xi) y=0
(xii) 3x+4y=12
(xiii) 5x−2y=−10
(xiv) x+5y=−5
(xv) x+√3y=6
(xvi) √3x−y=−3
questions.explanation: Point-slope for (i)–(vii) [(vii) slope = 2/(t₁+t₂)]; slope-intercept for (viii)–(xi); two-intercept for (xii)–(xiv); normal form xcosα+ysinα=p for (xv)–(xvi). All sixteen match the key.

questions.question: Reduce the equation 3x + 4y − 12 = 0 to the (i) slope-intercept form (ii) two-intercept form (iii) normal or perpendicular form.
questions.explanation: (i) solve for y; (ii) divide by 12; (iii) divide by √(9+16)=5. All match the key.

questions.question: Find the equations of the sides of the triangle whose vertices are (1, 4), (2, −3) and (−1, −2).
questions.explanation: Two-point form on each pair; slopes −7, −1/3, 3. All match the key.

questions.question: Find the equation of the perpendicular bisector of the segment joining (−1, 2) and (9, 12).
questions.explanation: Midpoint (4, 7); segment slope 1 so bisector slope −1. Matches the key.

questions.question: The x-intercept of a line is the reciprocal of its y-intercept and line passes through (2, −1). Find its equation.
questions.explanation: With y-intercept c: cx + y/c = 1; through (2,−1): 2c²−c−1=0 → c=1 or −1/2. Both match the key.

questions.question: Find the equation of the line which passes through (−2, −4) and the sum of its intercepts equal to 3.
questions.explanation: a+b=3 with −2/a−4/b=1 → a²−5a−6=0 → a=−1 or 6. Both match the key.

questions.question: Find the equation of the line which passes through (5, 6) and the y-intercept is twice that of the x-intercept.
questions.explanation: x/a + y/(2a) = 1 → 2x+y=2a; through (5,6): a=8. Matches the key.

questions.question: Find an equation of the line through (11, −5) and parallel to a line having slope 3/2.
questions.explanation: y+5 = (3/2)(x−11). Matches the key.

questions.question: Find an equation of the line through (−4, −6) and perpendicular to the line having slope −3/2.
questions.explanation: Perpendicular slope 2/3: y+6 = (2/3)(x+4). Matches the key.

questions.question: Determine whether each of the specified points is above or below the given straight line: (i) 3x + 11y − 44 = 0, (10, 1), (−4, 6) and (5, 3)  (ii) 10x − 12y + 17 = 0, (−20, −15), (5, 5) and (100, 84)  (iii) 29x − 17y + 31 = 0, (0, 2), (−3, −3) and (20, 30)
questions.answer:
(i) (10, 1) below; (−4, 6) above; (5, 3) above
(ii) (−20, −15) above; (5, 5) below; (100, 84) below
(iii) (0, 2) above; (−3, −3) above; (20, 30) below
questions.explanation: Compare y of the point with y on the line at the same x, e.g. (i) line y=4−(3/11)x gives 14/11 at x=10, so (10,1) is below. All nine match the key.

questions.question: In each of the following, find the perpendicular distance from the point to the line: (i) 15x − 8y − 5 = 0, (2, 1)  (ii) 3x − 4y + 5 = 0, (4, −3)  (iii) 3x + 4y + 10 = 0, (3, −2)  (iv) 2x − 7y + 1 = 0, (7, 4)  (v) 5x + 12y − 16 = 0, (3, −1)
questions.explanation: d = |ax₁+by₁+c|/√(a²+b²). All five match the key.

questions.question: Find the distance between the parallel lines: (i) 5x − 12y + 10 = 0, 5x − 12y − 16 = 0  (ii) x + y − 2 = 0, 2x + 2y − 1 = 0  (iii) 4x − 3y + 12 = 0, 4x − 3y − 12 = 0
questions.explanation: d = |c₁−c₂|/√(a²+b²) after equalising coefficients; (ii) halve the second equation first. All three match the key.

questions.question: What is the angle between two lines when they intersect at origin and one of the line passes through (2, 3) and the other line passes through (−3, 6)?
questions.explanation: m₁=3/2, m₂=−2; tanθ=|(−7/2)/(−2)|=7/4. Matches the key.

questions.question: Find the angle between the following two lines. l₁: 4x − 3y = 8 and l₂: 2x + 5y = 4.
questions.explanation: m₁=4/3, m₂=−2/5; tanθ=(26/15)/(7/15)=26/7. Flag: the key prints 3.69, but the exact ratio is 26/7≈3.7143 (the key rounded the slopes first).

questions.question: Find the acute angle between l₁: y = 3x + 1 and l₂: y = −4x + 3.
questions.explanation: tanθ=|(3+4)/(1−12)|=7/11. Matches the key.

questions.question: Find the angle between two lines, one of which is the x-axis and the other line is x − y + 4 = 0.
questions.explanation: Slopes 0 and 1 give tanθ=1. Matches the key.

questions.question: Find the angle between the lines 2x − 3y + 7 = 0 and 7x + 4y − 9 = 0.
Find the equation of line through point (3, 2) and making angle 45° with the line x − 2y = 3.
questions.explanation: Given slope 1/2; |(m−1/2)/(1+m/2)|=1 gives m=3 or −1/3. Both match the key.

questions.question: Determine the measure of the acute angle between the straight-line x − y + 4 = 0 and the straight line passing through the points (3, −2) and (−2, 4).
Find the equation of family of lines that pass through the point of intersection of 2x + 3y − 8 = 0 and x − y + 1 = 0. Also find the point of intersection.
questions.answer: a(2x + 3y − 8) + b(x − y + 1) = 0; point of intersection (1, 2)
questions.explanation: Family through the common point; solving the pair gives x=1, y=2. The key prints the family only.

questions.question: Find the equation of a line through the intersection of the lines: (i) 2x + 3y + 1 = 0, 3x − 4y = 5 and passing through (2, 1)  (ii) x − 4y = 3, x + 2y = 9 and passing through the origin  (iii) 3x + 2y = 8, 5x − 11y + 1 = 0 and parallel to 6x + 13y = 25  (iv) 2x − 3y + 4 = 0, 3x + 3y − 5 = 0 and parallel to y-axis  (v) 5x − 6y = 1, 3x + 2y + 5 = 0 and perpendicular to 5y − 3x = 11  (vi) 3x − 4y + 1 = 0, 5x + y − 1 = 0 and cutting off equal intercepts from the axes  (vii) 43x + 29y + 43 = 0, 23x + 8y + 6 = 0 and having y-intercept −2  (viii) 2x + 7y − 8 = 0, 3x + 2y + 5 = 0 and making an angle of 45° with the line 2x + 3y − 7 = 0
questions.explanation: Family L₁+kL₂=0 with k from the condition: (i) k=8/3; (ii) k=−1/3; (iii) k=−27/131; (iv) k=1; (v) k=45; (vi) k=−7/4; (vii) k=−3/2; (viii) k=−1. Flag: (viii) the second 45° case (k=−33/7) gives 5x+y+13=0, also valid but not in the key. The eight key answers match.

questions.question: Find the angles of the triangle with the given vertices (1, 2), (3, 4) and (2, 5).
questions.explanation: Side slopes 1, −1, 3: slopes 1 and −1 are perpendicular (90°); tan of the others 1/2 and 2. Matches the key.

questions.question: What are the angles of the triangle with vertices A(3, 2), B(4, 5) and C(−1, −1)?
questions.explanation: Side slopes AB=3, BC=6/5, CA=3/4; at B tan=9/23, at C tan=9/38; at A the interior angle is obtuse, 180°−34.70°. Matches the key.

questions.question: Find the angles of triangle where the slopes of its sides are 3, 1/2, −2.
questions.explanation: (1/2)(−2)=−1 gives the right angle; the other two pairs give tanθ=1. Matches the key.

questions.question: If A(2, 5), B(3, 7) and C(0, 8) are the vertices of a triangle then find the (i) equation of median through A (ii) equation of altitude through B (iii) equation of right bisector of side AC.
questions.explanation: (i) midpoint of BC (3/2, 15/2), slope −5; (ii) slope AC=−3/2 so altitude slope 2/3 through B; (iii) midpoint of AC (1, 13/2), slope 2/3. All match the key.

questions.question: Show that the following lines are concurrent. Also find their point of concurrency: (i) x − y = 6, 4y + 22 = 3x and 6x + 5y + 8 = 0  (ii) x/a + y/b = 1, x/b + y/a = 1 and y = x  (iii) 5x + y + 11 = 0, x + 7y + 9 = 0 and 2x + y + 5 = 0
questions.explanation: Intersect the first two lines and verify the third passes through the point; in (ii) subtracting the first two gives x=y, the third line. All match the key.

questions.question: If A(−1, 5), B(2, 3) and C(7, 6) are the vertices of triangle, then show right bisectors, medians and altitudes of the triangle are concurrent.
questions.answer: Medians at centroid (8/3, 14/3); right bisectors at circumcentre (105/38, 281/38); altitudes at orthocentre (47/19, −15/19) — each family concurrent, shown
questions.explanation: Each family's third line is verified to pass through the intersection of the first two. Proof question, no key entry.

questions.question: Find the area of the triangle whose vertices are: (i) (11, −12), (6, 2) and (−5, 10)  (ii) (3, 1), (−2, 5) and (−4, −5)  (iii) (−5, −2), (4, −6) and (1, 7)  (iv) (−a, b + c), (a, b − c) and (a, −c)  (v) (a cos θ₁, b sin θ₁), (a cos θ₂, b sin θ₂) and (a cos θ₃, b sin θ₃)
questions.answer:
(i) 57 square units
(ii) 29 square units
(iii) 52.5 square units
(iv) ab square units
(v) ½ab{sin(θ₁−θ₂) + sin(θ₂−θ₃) + sin(θ₃−θ₁)}
questions.explanation: Area = ½|x₁(y₂−y₃)+x₂(y₃−y₁)+x₃(y₁−y₂)|; (v) the bracket telescopes into the sine differences. Flag: the key mislabels the (iv) answer as (vi). All match the key.

questions.question: Find the area of a quadrilateral whose consecutive vertices are: (i) (3, −3), (7, 5), (1, 2) and (−3, 4)  (ii) (2, 3), (−1, 2), (−3, 2) and (3, −3)
questions.explanation: Shoelace formula: (i) sum 52; (ii) sum 29; halve each. Both match the key.

questions.question: Prove, by the method of the area of a triangle, that the following points are collinear: (i) (2, 3), (5, 0) and (4, 1)  (ii) (2, 1), (4, −1) and (1, 2)  (iii) (−1, −1), (5, 7) and (8, 11)
questions.answer: Each triangle area = 0, so each triple is collinear — proved
questions.explanation: (i) ½|−2−10+12|=0; (ii) ½|−6+4+2|=0; (iii) ½|4+60−64|=0. Proof question, no key entries.

questions.question: Find the area of triangle formed by the lines: (i) y = 0, y = 2x and y = 6x + 5  (ii) y − x = 0, y + x = 0 and x − c = 0  (iii) y = 2x + 3, 2y + 3x = 3 and x + y + 2 = 0
questions.answer:
(i) 25/24 square units
(ii) c² square units
(iii) 338/21 square units
questions.explanation: Vertices from pairwise intersections: (i) (0,0), (−5/6,0), (−5/4,−5/2); (ii) (0,0), (c,c), (c,−c); (iii) (−3/7,15/7), (−5/3,−1/3), (7,−9). All match the key.

questions.question: Separate the pair of lines represented by the given equations and state their nature: (i) x² − 5xy + 6y² = 0  (ii) 4x² − xy − 5y² = 0  (iii) 9x² − 6xy + y² = 0  (iv) 10x² − 3xy − y² = 0  (v) 7x² − 3xy + 5y² = 0
questions.answer:
(i) x − 3y = 0, x − 2y = 0; two real distinct lines
(ii) 4x − 5y = 0, x + y = 0; two real distinct lines
(iii) 3x − y = 0 twice; coincident real lines
(iv) 2x − y = 0, 5x + y = 0; two real distinct lines
(v) h² − ab = 9/4 − 35 < 0; two imaginary lines (only the origin is real)
questions.explanation: Factor each quadratic in y/x. (v) does not factor over the reals: y = [(3 ± √(−131))/10]x. Matches the key (the book misnumbers the parts (i),(ii),(ii),(iii),(v); they are renumbered (i)–(v) here in printed order, and the key follows the book’s misnumbering).

questions.question: Find the combined equation of the pair of lines through the origin perpendicular to the given pair: (i) 2x² − 5xy + y² = 0  (ii) 6x² − 13xy + 6y² = 0
questions.explanation: The pair perpendicular to ax² + 2hxy + by² = 0 is bx² − 2hxy + ay² = 0. Both match the key.

questions.question: Trace (separate) the pair of lines represented by: (i) x² − 3xy + 2y² = 0  (ii) x² − 6xy + 9y² = 0  (iii) 6x² − xy − y² = 0  (iv) 8x² − 3xy − y² = 0
questions.answer:
(i) y = x and y = x/2
(ii) coincident line y = x/3
(iii) y = 2x and y = −3x
(iv) y = [(−3 + √41)/2]x and y = [(−3 − √41)/2]x
questions.explanation: (i)–(iii) factor directly; (iv) needs the quadratic t² + 3t − 8 = 0 for t = y/x, giving real distinct lines through the origin. Trace question, no key entries.

questions.question: Find the angle between the pair of lines represented by: (i) x² − 5xy + 6y² = 0  (ii) 3x² + 7xy + 2y² = 0  (iii) x² + 2xy − 3y² = 0  (iv) x² + xy − 2y² = 0
questions.explanation: tan θ = 2√(h² − ab)/(a + b). (i) a=1, h=−5/2, b=6 → tan θ = 1/7; (ii) → 1; (iii) → −2 (obtuse); (iv) → −3 (obtuse). All match the key.

questions.question: If one of the gradients of the lines represented by ax² + 2hxy + by² = 0 is twice the other, show that 8h² = 9ab.
questions.answer: Proof: let the gradients be m and 2m. Then m + 2m = −2h/b → m = −2h/(3b), and m·2m = a/b → 2m² = a/b. Substituting: 2·4h²/(9b²) = a/b → 8h² = 9ab. (Shown)
questions.explanation: Uses sum and product of roots of bt² + 2ht + a = 0 where t is the gradient. Proof question, no key entry.

questions.question: Select the correct option: (i) The slope of the line that passes through (−3, −4) and (7, 6) is (a) 0  (b) undefined  (c) −1  (d) 1.  (ii) A line with a slope of 1/2 and a y-intercept 7 is (a) 2y = x − 7  (b) y = (1/2)x + 7  (c) y = (1/2)x − 7  (d) x − 2y = 14.  (iii) Two lines are said to be parallel if and only if their slopes are  (a) equal  (b) unequal  (c) does not exist  (d) negative reciprocals of each other.  (iv) Two lines l₁ and l₂ are said to be perpendicular if and only if  (a) m₁m₂ = −1  (b) m₁m₂ = 1  (c) m₁ = −m₂  (d) m₁ = 1/m₂.  (v) The slope of a line that is perpendicular to a vertical line is  (a) 0  (b) 1  (c) 90°  (d) undefined.  (vi) The slope of the line which makes an angle 45° with the line 3x − y = −5 is  (a) 2  (b) 1/2  (c) 1/2, −2  (d) −2.  (vii) The point on the line 2x − 3y = 5 which is equidistant from (1, 2) and (3, 4) is  (a) (−2, 2)  (b) (4, 1)  (c) (1, −1)  (d) (4, 6).  (viii) In a plane three or more points are said to be collinear if  (a) they lie on a circle  (b) they form a closed loop together  (c) they lie on a straight line  (d) they do not make any defined shape.  (ix) If the line coincides with the x-axis then its equation is  (a) y = b  (b) −b  (c) y = 0  (d) ∞.  (x) The general equation of line also known as standard equation of line is  (a) ax + by + c = 0  (b) y = ax + c  (c) y − y₁ = m(x − x₁)  (d) x/a + y/b = 1
questions.explanation: (i) (6+4)/(7+3) = 1. (ii) y = (1/2)x + 7 is option (b) itself. (vi) |(m−3)/(1+3m)| = 1 → m = 1/2 or −2; the key misprints this as (b), but the complete option is (c). (vii) intersection of 2x − 3y = 5 with the bisector x + y = 5 gives (4, 1).

questions.question: Find the value(s) of a if the distance between the points (5, −2) and (1, a) is 5 units.
questions.explanation: 16 + (a + 2)² = 25 → (a + 2)² = 9 → a + 2 = ±3. Matches the key.

questions.question: M(3, 8) is the midpoint of AB where A is (−2, 3). Find B.
questions.explanation: B = (2·3 − (−2), 2·8 − 3) = (8, 13). Matches the key.

questions.question: Find the centre of the circle whose diameter has endpoints (2, −3) and (−6, 5).
questions.explanation: The centre is the midpoint of a diameter: ((2−6)/2, (−3+5)/2) = (−2, 1). Matches the key.

questions.question: Find the point that divides the segment joining P(−1, 7) and Q(4, −3) in the ratio 2:3.
questions.explanation: Section formula: ((2·4 + 3·(−1))/5, (2·(−3) + 3·7)/5) = (1, 3). Matches the key.

questions.question: Find the points of trisection of the segment joining A(−6, 11) and B(10, −3).
questions.explanation: P = A + (1/3)(B − A) = (−2/3, 19/3); Q = A + (2/3)(B − A) = (14/3, 5/3). Matches the key.

questions.question: Two vertices of a triangle are (1, 4) and (3, 1) and its centroid is the origin. Find the third vertex.
questions.explanation: (1 + 3 + x)/3 = 0 and (4 + 1 + y)/3 = 0 → x = −4, y = −5. Matches the key.

questions.question: Find the slope of a line perpendicular to the line −2y = −8x + 9.
questions.explanation: The given line is y = 4x − 9/2, slope 4; the perpendicular slope is −1/4. Matches the key.

questions.question: Write the equation of the line in two-intercept form having x-intercept (6, 0) and y-intercept (0, 5).
questions.explanation: Two-intercept form x/a + y/b = 1 with a = 6, b = 5. Matches the key.

questions.question: Find the slope and y-intercept of each line: (a) y = 12x − 6  (b) y = 5 − 2x  (c) 4x − y + 13 = 0  (d) y = 4x
questions.answer:
(a) slope 12, y-intercept −6
(b) slope −2, y-intercept 5
(c) slope 4, y-intercept 13
(d) slope 4, y-intercept 0
questions.explanation: Read off the slope-intercept form y = mx + c; (c) rewrites as y = 4x + 13. All match the key.

questions.question: Find the x- and y-intercepts of the line 4x + 8y + 2 = 0.
questions.explanation: Set y = 0: x = −2/4 = −1/2. Set x = 0: y = −2/8 = −1/4. Matches the key.

questions.question: Find k so that the line through (3, k) and (2, 7) is parallel to the line through (−1, 4) and (0, 6).
questions.explanation: Second slope = (6−4)/(0−(−1)) = 2; parallel lines have equal slopes, so (k − 7)/(3 − 2) = 2 → k = 9. Matches the key.

questions.question: Determine whether each pair of lines is parallel, perpendicular, or neither: (a) y = 2x + 7, y = 7x − 2  (b) x = 1, x = 5  (c) x = −3, y = −3
questions.explanation: (a) slopes 2 and 7: neither equal nor negative reciprocals. (b) both vertical. (c) one vertical, one horizontal. All match the key.

questions.question: Find k so that the lines y = 3x − 1, 2y = x + 3 and 3y = kx + 4 are concurrent.
questions.explanation: The first two meet at (1, 2); substituting in the third: 6 = k + 4 → k = 2. Matches the key.

questions.question: For the lines ax − 2y − 1 = 0 and 6x − 4y − b = 0, find the values of a and b when the lines are (i) parallel  (ii) perpendicular  (iii) coincident  (iv) have no common point.
questions.answer:
(i) a = 3, b ≠ 2
(ii) a = −4/3, any b
(iii) a = 3, b = 2
(iv) a = 3, b ≠ 2
questions.explanation: Slopes a/2 and 3/2; intercepts −1/2 and −b/4. Perpendicular: (a/2)(3/2) = −1 → a = −4/3. Coincident: a = 3 and b/4 = 1/2 → b = 2. Flag: the key interchanges the labels of (ii) and (iii) relative to the question; the mapping above is the correct one.

questions.question: Find the equation of the line through the intersection of x + 2y − 5 = 0 and 3x − 2y + 1 = 0 that is (i) parallel to 4x + 3y − 5 = 0  (ii) perpendicular to 2x − 3y + 7 = 0.
questions.explanation: Intersection point: adding the equations gives 4x = 4, x = 1, y = 2, i.e. (1, 2). (i) slope −4/3: y − 2 = −4/3(x − 1). (ii) perpendicular slope −3/2: y − 2 = −3/2(x − 1). Both match the key.

questions.question: Find the distance of the point from the line: (i) (2, 1) from 15x − 8y − 5 = 0  (ii) (7, 4) from 2x − 7y + 1 = 0
questions.explanation: d = |ax₁ + by₁ + c|/√(a² + b²). (i) |30 − 8 − 5|/17 = 1; the key prints the signed value −1 with “point below the line”. (ii) |14 − 28 + 1|/√53 = 13/√53. Matches the key otherwise.

questions.question: Describe the condition under which a plane cuts a right circular cone to produce: (i) circle  (ii) parabola  (iii) ellipse  (iv) hyperbola  (v) a degenerate conic
questions.answer:
(i) plane perpendicular to the axis
(ii) plane parallel to exactly one generator
(iii) plane cuts all generators of one nappe but is not perpendicular to the axis
(iv) plane parallel to the axis (cuts both nappes)
(v) plane passes through the vertex
questions.explanation: With semi-vertical angle α and plane-axis angle β: circle β = 90°; parabola β = α; ellipse α < β < 90°; hyperbola 0 ≤ β < α; through the vertex the section degenerates to a point, a line, or a pair of lines. Descriptive question, no key entry.

questions.question: Find the equation of the circle if: (i) centre is at origin and radius 5√2 units  (ii) centre is (−5, 7) and radius 6 units  (iii) (2, −3) and (−4, 7) are the ends of its diameter  (iv) centre is at origin and contains a point (5, 6)  (v) centre is at (2, 3) and contains the point (5, 7)  (vi) centre is at (p, q) and radius of √(p² + q²) units
questions.answer:
(i) x² + y² = 50
(ii) x² + y² + 10x − 14y + 38 = 0
(iii) x² + y² + 2x − 4y − 29 = 0
(iv) x² + y² = 61
(v) x² + y² − 4x − 6y − 12 = 0
(vi) x² + y² − 2px − 2qy = 0
questions.explanation: Use (x − h)² + (y − k)² = r². (iii) centre = midpoint (−1, 2), r = ½√136 = √34. (iv) r² = 25 + 36 = 61. (v) r² = 9 + 16 = 25. All match the key.

questions.question: Find the centre and radius of each of the following circles and draw them: (i) x² + y² − 25 = 0  (ii) (x + 3)² + (y − 5)² = 49  (iii) x² + y² − 6x + 8y + 10 = 0  (iv) x² + y² − 8x + 9 = 0  (v) 5x² + 5y² + 20x − 15y + 10 = 0
questions.answer:
(i) centre (0, 0), radius 5
(ii) centre (−3, 5), radius 7
(iii) centre (3, −4), radius √15
(iv) centre (4, 0), radius √7
(v) centre (−2, 3/2), radius √17/2
questions.explanation: Centre (−g, −f), r = √(g² + f² − c) after making the squared coefficients 1; (v) divide by 5 first: x² + y² + 4x − 3y + 2 = 0. Sketch: a circle at each centre with the stated radius. All match the key.

questions.question: Find the value of k if the radius of the circle 2x² + 2y² − 8x + 4y + 3k = 0 is 10 units.
questions.explanation: Divide by 2: x² + y² − 4x + 2y + 3k/2 = 0; r² = 4 + 1 − 3k/2 = 100 → 3k/2 = −95. Matches the key.

questions.question: Find the equation of the circle passing through (−3, −4) and concentric with the circle x² + y² − 6x + 8y − 24 = 0. Also identify the outer circle.
questions.answer: x² + y² − 6x + 8y − 11 = 0; the given circle is the outer circle
questions.explanation: Both circles share centre (3, −4). Required radius² = (−3 − 3)² + (−4 + 4)² = 36 (r = 6); the given circle has r = √49 = 7 > 6, so it is the outer one. Matches the key.

questions.question: Show that the equations x = a cos θ and y = a sin θ represent a circle with centre at the origin and radius equal to a.
questions.answer: x² + y² = a²cos²θ + a²sin²θ = a², the circle centred at (0, 0) with radius a. (Shown)
questions.explanation: Squaring and adding eliminates θ via cos² + sin² = 1. Proof question, no key entry.

questions.question: Prove that the equation of a circle (i) through the origin has no constant term  (ii) with centre on the x-axis has no term in y  (iii) with centre on the y-axis has no term in x  (iv) with centre at the origin has no term in x and y both.
questions.answer:
(i) substituting (0, 0) in x² + y² + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0 gives c = 0
(ii) centre on x-axis → f = 0, so the 2fy term vanishes
(iii) centre on y-axis → g = 0, so the 2gx term vanishes
(iv) centre at origin → g = f = 0, both linear terms vanish. (Proved)
questions.explanation: Centre is (−g, −f); each geometric condition forces the matching coefficient to zero. Proof question, no key entry.

questions.question: Find the equation of the circle through the given points: (i) (0, 0), (0, 3), (−4, 0)  (ii) (0, 10), (−10, 0), (8, 6)  (iii) (0, 3), (2, −1), (1, 0)  (iv) (7, −3), (−7, 5), (11, 5)  (v) (1, 1), (2, −1), (3, −2)
questions.answer:
(i) x² + y² + 4x − 3y = 0
(ii) x² + y² = 100
(iii) x² + y² − 10x − 6y + 9 = 0
(iv) x² + y² − 4x − 9y − 57 = 0
(v) x² + y² − 13x − 5y + 16 = 0
questions.explanation: Substitute each point into x² + y² + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0 and solve the three linear equations; e.g. (iv) gives g = −2, f = −9/2, c = −57 and (v) gives g = −13/2, f = −5/2, c = 16. All match the key.

questions.question: Find the equation of the circle through the points (1, 2), (2, 3) and having centre on (i) the x-axis  (ii) the y-axis.
questions.explanation: (i) centre on x-axis → f = 0; the two points give g = −4, c = 3. (ii) g = 0 gives f = −4, c = 11. Both match the key.

questions.question: Find the equation of the circle through the points (3, 1), (2, 2) and having centre on the line x + y − 3 = 0.
questions.explanation: Centre (−g, −f) on the line → g + f = −3; the points give g − f = −1, so g = −2, f = −1, c = 4. Matches the key.

questions.question: Find the equation of the circle through the points (0, −1) and (3, 0) when the line 3x + y − 9 = 0 is tangent to it at (3, 0).
questions.explanation: The centre lies on the normal at (3, 0), i.e. x − 3y − 3 = 0 (slope 1/3), giving g = 3f − 3; with the two point equations f = 1/2, g = −3/2, c = 0. Matches the key.

questions.question: Find the equation of the circle through the origin with x-intercept 2 which is tangent to the line y − 1 = 0.
questions.explanation: Origin → c = 0; point (2, 0) → g = −1; tangency to y = 1: |−f − 1| = √(1 + f²) → f = 0. Centre (1, 0), radius 1. Matches the key.

questions.question: Find the equation of a circle containing the points (1, 2), (2, 3) and having centre on x − y + 1 = 0.
questions.explanation: Centre condition −g + f + 1 = 0 → g = f + 1; the points give g + f = −4, so f = −5/2, g = −3/2, c = 8. Matches the key.

questions.question: Find the equation of the circumcircle of the triangle with vertices (1, −2), (−5, 2) and (3, 4).
questions.explanation: The three point equations give g = 8/11, f = −21/11, c = −155/11; multiplying by 11 clears fractions. Matches the key.

questions.question: Find the equation of the circle containing the points (1, −2) and (3, −4) and touching the x-axis.
questions.explanation: Touching the x-axis → c = g²; the two points then give g² − 2g − 15 = 0, so g = 5 (f = 10, c = 25) or g = −3 (f = 2, c = 9). Both match the key.

questions.question: Find the equation of the circle containing the point (6, 0) and touching the line x = y at (4, 4).
questions.explanation: Centre on the normal x + y = 8 at (4, 4); (4, 4) on the circle gives c = 32; (6, 0) gives g = −17/3, f = −7/3. Matches the key.

questions.question: Show that the equation of a circle with centre (−g, −f) and (i) touching the x-axis is of the form x² + y² + 2gx + 2fy + g² = 0  (ii) touching the y-axis is of the form x² + y² + 2gx + 2fy + f² = 0
questions.answer:
(i) touching x-axis → r = |f| → g² + f² − c = f² → c = g², giving the stated form
(ii) touching y-axis → r = |g| → c = f², giving the stated form. (Shown)
questions.explanation: The radius equals the modulus of the ordinate (resp. abscissa) of the centre when the circle touches the x-axis (resp. y-axis). Proof question, no key entry.

questions.question: Find the equation of the circle passing through the origin and having intercepts 6 and 8.
questions.explanation: c = 0; x-intercept 2√(g² − c) = 6 → |g| = 3; y-intercept 2√(f² − c) = 8 → |f| = 4; the key takes g = −3, f = −4 (other sign choices give the congruent circles x² + y² ± 6x ± 8y = 0). Matches the key.

questions.question: Find the equation of the circle which passes through the two points (b, 0) and (−b, 0) and whose radius is a units.
questions.answer: x² + y² ± 2√(a² − b²)·y − b² = 0 (exists when a ≥ b)
questions.explanation: The centre lies on the perpendicular bisector of the two points, the y-axis, so g = 0; (b, 0) gives c = −b²; radius √(f² + b²) = a gives f = ±√(a² − b²). No key entry.

questions.question: Find the equation of the circle which passes through the points (5, 0) and (0, −5) and whose radius is 5 units.
questions.explanation: The points give f = −g and c = −25 − 10g; radius² = 2g² − c = 25 leads to 2g² + 10g = 0, so g = 0 (centre (0, 0)) or g = −5 (centre (5, −5)). No key entry.

questions.question: Check whether the following lines are tangent, secant or neither to the circle x² + y² = 25: (i) y = x + 3  (ii) y = √3x + 10  (iii) y = 2x + 15
questions.explanation: Compare the distance from the centre (0, 0) with r = 5: (i) 3/√2 ≈ 2.12 < 5; (ii) 10/2 = 5; (iii) 15/√5 = 3√5 ≈ 6.71 > 5. All match the key.

questions.question: Find the condition of tangency and secancy of the line y = 2x + k with the circle x² + y² + 10x + 20y + c = 0.
questions.explanation: Centre (−5, −10), r = √(125 − c); d = |k|/√5; set d = r (tangent) or d < r (secant). Matches the key.

questions.question: Find the equation of the tangent to x² + y² = 36 with the slope √3.
questions.explanation: y = mx ± r√(1 + m²) with m = √3, r = 6 gives ±6√4 = ±12. Matches the key.

questions.question: Find the equation of tangent and normal: (i) at (1, −4) to the circle x² + y² = 17  (ii) at (4, 1) to the circle x² + y² − 4x + 2y = 3
questions.answer:
(i) tangent: x − 4y = 17; normal: 4x + y = 0
(ii) tangent: x + y = 5; normal: x − y = 3
questions.explanation: Tangent at (x₁, y₁) via xx₁ + yy₁ + g(x + x₁) + f(y + y₁) + c = 0; the normal is the line through the centre and the point of contact. Both match the key.

questions.question: Find the length of the tangent: (i) from (6, 1) to the circle x² + y² = 4  (ii) from (2, 5) to the circle x² + y² + 8x − 5y = 7
questions.explanation: Length = √S₁: (i) √(36 + 1 − 4); (ii) √(4 + 25 + 16 − 25 − 7). Both match the key.

questions.question: Find the condition that the line y = mx + c may be tangent to the circle (x − h)² + (y − k)² = r².
questions.explanation: Distance from (h, k) to mx − y + c = 0 equals r: |mh − k + c|/√(1 + m²) = r. Matches the key.

questions.question: Show that the circles x² + y² − 6x − 6y + 10 = 0 and x² + y² = 2 touch each other and find the point of contact.
questions.answer: They touch externally; point of contact (1, 1)

questions.question: Find the equation(s) of the tangent(s) to the circle x² + y² = 25: (i) at the point whose abscissa is 3  (ii) at the point whose ordinate is −4  (iii) parallel to 3x + 4y + 1 = 0  (iv) perpendicular to 3x + 4y + 1 = 0
questions.explanation: (i) points (3, ±4); (ii) points (±3, −4); (iii) tangents 3x + 4y = ±25; (iv) slope 4/3 through distance 5 from the centre. All match the key.

questions.question: Find the equations of the tangents to x² + y² − 6x − 2y + 9 = 0 through the origin and their respective points of contact.
questions.answer: Tangents: y = 0 and 3x − 4y = 0; points of contact: (3, 0) and (12/5, 9/5)
questions.explanation: Centre (3, 1), r = 1; y = mx tangent when |3m − 1|/√(m² + 1) = 1 → 8m² − 6m = 0. Contact points are the feet of perpendiculars from the centre. Matches the key.

questions.question: Show that the line ax + by + al + bm = 0 is normal to the circle x² + y² + 2lx + 2my + c = 0 for all values of a and b.
questions.answer: The centre (−l, −m) satisfies a(−l) + b(−m) + al + bm = 0 identically, so the line always passes through the centre and is therefore a normal. (Shown)
questions.explanation: Every line through the centre of a circle is a normal to it. Proof question, no key entry.

questions.question: Find (i) the product of abscissae and (ii) the product of ordinates of the points where the line y = mx meets the circle x² + y² + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0.
questions.explanation: Substitute y = mx: (1 + m²)x² + 2(g + fm)x + c = 0, product of roots c/(1 + m²); substitute x = y/m for the ordinates. Both match the key.

questions.question: Prove that the line y = x + k√2 touches the circle x² + y² = k² and find its point of contact.
questions.answer: Distance from (0, 0) to x − y + k√2 = 0 is |k√2|/√2 = |k| = radius, so it touches; point of contact (−k√2/2, k√2/2)
questions.explanation: The contact point is the foot of the perpendicular from the centre onto the line. Matches the key.

questions.question: Find the condition that the line 3x + 4y = c may touch the circle x² + y² = 8x.
questions.explanation: Centre (4, 0), r = 4; |12 − c|/5 = 4 → |12 − c| = 20. Matches the key.

questions.question: Find whether the line x + y = 2 + √2 touches the circle x² + y² − 2x − 2y − 1 = 0.
questions.answer: No — the given line is not a tangent (d = 1 < √3 = r, so it is a secant)
questions.explanation: Centre (1, 1), r = √3; d = |1 + 1 − 2 − √2|/√2 = 1 ≠ √3. Matches the key.

questions.question: Prove that the two circles x² + y² + 2gx + c = 0 and x² + y² + 2fy + c = 0 touch each other if 1/f² + 1/g² = 1/c.
questions.answer: C₁ = (−g, 0), r₁ = √(g² − c); C₂ = (0, −f), r₂ = √(f² − c). Touching: g² + f² = (g² − c) + (f² − c) ± 2√((g² − c)(f² − c)) → (g² − c)(f² − c) = c² → g²f² = c(g² + f²) → 1/f² + 1/g² = 1/c. (Proved)
questions.explanation: Squaring removes the ± so the same condition covers internal and external contact. Proof question, no key entry.

questions.question: Prove analytically: the tangents drawn at the ends of a diameter of a circle are parallel.
questions.answer: For x² + y² = r² with diameter ends P(r cos θ, r sin θ) and Q(−r cos θ, −r sin θ): tangent at P is x cos θ + y sin θ = r and at Q is x cos θ + y sin θ = −r — same normal direction, different constants, hence distinct parallel lines. (Proved)
questions.explanation: Equal normal direction with unequal constants is exactly the condition for parallel distinct lines. Proof question, no key entry.

questions.question: Prove analytically: a normal to a circle passes through the centre of the circle.
questions.answer: The normal at (x₁, y₁) to x² + y² + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0 is (x − x₁)(y₁ + f) − (y − y₁)(x₁ + g) = 0; substituting the centre (−g, −f) gives −(x₁ + g)(y₁ + f) + (y₁ + f)(x₁ + g) = 0, so the centre lies on every normal. (Proved)
questions.explanation: The normal is the line through the point of contact perpendicular to the tangent there. Proof question, no key entry.

questions.question: Prove analytically: the midpoint of the hypotenuse of a right triangle is the centre of the circle circumscribing the triangle.
questions.answer: With the right angle at the origin and legs on the axes, A(a, 0), B(0, b); midpoint M(a/2, b/2) satisfies MA = MB = MC = √(a²/4 + b²/4), so M is equidistant from all three vertices and is the circumcentre. (Proved)
questions.explanation: Equidistance from the three vertices is the defining property of the circumcentre. Proof question, no key entry.

questions.question: Prove analytically: the measure of the central angle of a major arc is double the measure of the inscribed angle of the corresponding minor arc.
questions.answer: On x² + y² = r² take minor arc AB of central measure θ = |b − a| and Q on that minor arc. Sum-to-product gives A − Q ∝ (−sin s, cos s), B − Q ∝ (−sin t, cos t) with s = (a+q)/2, t = (b+q)/2 and opposite proportionality signs, so ∠AQB = π − |t − s| = π − θ/2, while the central angle of the major arc is 2π − θ = 2∠AQB. (Proved)
questions.explanation: The inscribed-angle theorem in coordinate form: an angle at the circumference is half the central angle standing on the same arc. Proof question, no key entry.

questions.question: Prove analytically: the parallelogram circumscribing a circle is a rhombus.
questions.answer: Every side is tangent, so the distance from the centre to each side is r; opposite sides are parallel at distance 2r. Area = AB·2r = BC·2r → AB = BC, and a parallelogram with equal adjacent sides is a rhombus. (Proved)
questions.explanation: Computing the same area against the two pairs of parallel sides forces the adjacent sides equal. Proof question, no key entry.

questions.question: Tick the correct option: (i) If a plane cuts one nappe of a right circular cone perpendicularly the conic is  (a) parabola  (b) circle  (c) ellipse  (d) hyperbola.  (ii) The centre of (x + 3)² + (y − 5)² = 36 is  (a) (3, −5)  (b) (−3, −5)  (c) (−3, 5)  (d) (3, 5).  (iii) The centre of x² + y² + 10x − 8y + 1 = 0 is  (a) (−5, 8)  (b) (−10, 8)  (c) (5, −4)  (d) (−5, 4).  (iv) The radius of x² + y² + 4x + 6y + 1 = 0 is  (a) √13  (b) √12  (c) √10  (d) √71.  (v) Which is a degenerate conic  (a) circle  (b) ellipse  (c) line  (d) parabola.  (vi) The circle with centre at origin and diameter 10 units is  (a) x² + y² = 100  (b) x² + y² + 100 = 0  (c) x² + y² = 50  (d) x² + y² = 25.  (vii) For what k is the radius of x² + y² + 6x − 4y + k = 0 equal to 5  (a) 11  (b) −12  (c) 10  (d) 12.  (viii) The centre of x² + y² + 6x + 8 = 0 is  (a) on x-axis  (b) on y-axis  (c) in 1st quadrant  (d) at origin.  (ix) The circle x² + y² + 6x + 10y + 9 = 0  (a) touches x-axis  (b) touches y-axis  (c) passes through origin  (d) cuts x-axis.  (x) The circle x² + y² + 20x − 8y + 16 = 0  (a) touches x-axis  (b) touches y-axis  (c) passes through origin  (d) cuts y-axis.  (xi) y = 2x + c is tangent to x² + y² = 25 if  (a) c² = 25  (b) c² = 625  (c) c² = 50  (d) c² = 125.  (xii) For what k is y = 2x + 3 tangent to x² + y² = k²  (a) ±5/√3  (b) ±3/√5  (c) ±√(3/5)  (d) ±√5/3.  (xiii) For what k is 2x + 3y + k = 0 normal to x² + y² + 2x + 9 = 0  (a) −2  (b) 2  (c) 3  (d) −3.  (xiv) The tangent to x² + y² = 25 at (3, 4) is  (a) 3x + 4y = 0  (b) 4x + 3y = 25  (c) 3x + 4y = 25  (d) 3x + 4y = 5.  (xv) The normal to x² + y² = 36 at (2, 4√2) is  (a) 2x + 4√2y = 0  (b) 4√2x + 2y = 0  (c) 2x − 4√2y = 0  (d) 4√2x − 2y = 0.  (xvi) The tangent to x² + y² = 100 with slope √15 is  (a) y = √15x ± 40  (b) y = −√15x ± 40  (c) y = √15x ± 40y  (d) y = −√15x ± 40y.  (xvii) The length of the tangent to x² + y² + 2y − 1 = 0 from (5, 2) is  (a) √24  (b) √33  (c) √32  (d) √31 units.  (xviii) Congruent chords of a circle are equidistant from its  (a) diameter  (b) centre  (c) arc  (d) segment.  (xix) Angle in a semi-circle is  (a) acute  (b) obtuse  (c) right  (d) straight angle.  (xx) The point (3, 3) is ______ the circle x² + y² = 64  (a) outside  (b) inside  (c) on  (d) cannot be determined
questions.explanation: (iv) √(4 + 9 − 1) = √12. (vii) 13 − k = 25. (ix) r = 5 = |y-coordinate of centre|. (x) r = 10 = |x-coordinate of centre|. (xi) c² = r²(1 + m²) = 125. (xii) |k| = 3/√5. (xvii) √S₁ = √32. (xx) 18 < 64. All match the key.

questions.question: Find the equation of the circle passing through (2, 3), (4, 6) and having (i) centre on the x-axis  (ii) centre on the y-axis.
questions.explanation: (i) f = 0 gives 13 + 4g + c = 0 and 52 + 8g + c = 0 → g = −39/4, c = 26 (doubled to clear fractions). (ii) g = 0 gives f = −13/2, c = 26. Both match the key.

questions.question: y = √3x + 10 is the equation of a tangent to the circle with centre at the origin. Find the equation of the normal to the circle at the point of tangency.
questions.explanation: Radius = distance from the origin to the line = 10/2 = 5, so the circle is x² + y² = 25; the point of contact is the foot of the perpendicular (−5√3/2, 5/2); the normal joins it to the centre, slope −1/√3. Matches the key.

questions.question: Find the condition of tangency, secancy and normality of the line x + y + k = 0 to the circle x² + y² + 2x − 3 = 0.
questions.explanation: Centre (−1, 0), r = 2, d = |k − 1|/√2. Tangent: (k − 1)² = 8; secant: (k − 1)² < 8; normal: the line passes through the centre. Flag: the key prints the secant condition as k² − 2k − 7 = 0 (the boundary equation); the secant region is the strict inequality.

questions.question: Draw the following parabolas: (i) y² = 10x  (ii) x² = −12y  (iii) y² − x − 2y − 1 = 0  (iv) x² − 6x − 2y + 5 = 0
questions.answer:
(i) opens right, vertex (0, 0), focus (5/2, 0)
(ii) opens down, vertex (0, 0), focus (0, −3)
(iii) (y − 1)² = x + 2: opens right, vertex (−2, 1), focus (−7/4, 1)
(iv) (x − 3)² = 2(y + 2): opens up, vertex (3, −2), focus (3, −3/2)
questions.explanation: Complete the square to put each equation in a shifted standard form, then sketch the usual parabola shape at that vertex opening in that direction. Sketch task, no key entry.

questions.question: Determine the vertex, focus, latus rectum and equation of the directrix of the following, and find the equation of the axis of symmetry: (i) y² = −8x  (ii) x² = −16y  (iii) (y + 3)² = 12(x − 2)  (iv) (x + 5)² = 8(y − 3)  (v) x² + 4x − y + 5 = 0  (vi) y² − 6y + 8x − 23 = 0
questions.answer:
(i) vertex (0, 0); focus (−2, 0); LR 8; directrix x − 2 = 0; axis y = 0
(ii) vertex (0, 0); focus (0, −4); LR 16; directrix y − 4 = 0; axis x = 0
(iii) vertex (2, −3); focus (5, −3); LR 12; directrix x + 1 = 0; axis y + 3 = 0
(iv) vertex (−5, 3); focus (−5, 5); LR 8; directrix y − 1 = 0; axis x + 5 = 0
(v) vertex (−2, 1); focus (−2, 5/4); LR 1; directrix 4y − 3 = 0; axis x + 2 = 0
(vi) vertex (4, 3); focus (2, 3); LR 8; directrix x − 6 = 0; axis y − 3 = 0
questions.explanation: Read 4a from the standard (or completed-square) form; the focus lies a units from the vertex along the axis, the directrix a units behind it. (v) is (x + 2)² = y − 1 and (vi) is (y − 3)² = −8(x − 4). All match the key.

questions.question: Find the equation of the parabola whose focus is F(1, −2) and directrix is 3x − 5 = 0.
questions.explanation: Locus condition (x − 1)² + (y + 2)² = (x − 5/3)² simplifies to (y + 2)² = −(4/3)(x − 4/3). Matches the key.

questions.question: Find the equation of the parabola whose focus is (3, 4) and the directrix is the line x + y − 1 = 0.
questions.explanation: 2[(x − 3)² + (y − 4)²] = (x + y − 1)² since the distance to the oblique directrix carries a factor 1/√2. Matches the key.

questions.question: Find the equation of the parabolas whose focus and vertex are as under: (i) vertex (0, 0), focus (5, 0)  (ii) vertex (0, 0), focus (0, −2)  (iii) vertex (1, −3), focus (1, 2)  (iv) vertex (2, 4), focus (3, 4)
questions.explanation: a = distance vertex-to-focus; the opening direction follows from focus minus vertex. Matches the key (the key’s (ii) “x² = −8x” is a misprint for x² = −8y).

questions.question: Find the equation of the parabola whose focus and directrix are given: (i) focus (3, 0), directrix x − 5 = 0  (ii) focus (0, 4), directrix y + 6 = 0  (iii) focus (−4, 3), directrix y = 6
questions.explanation: The vertex is the midpoint of focus and foot of directrix on the axis; a = half the focus-directrix distance; opening is away from the directrix. All match the key.

questions.question: Find the equation of the parabola whose vertex and directrix are as under: (i) vertex (0, 0), directrix x = −6  (ii) vertex (0, 0), directrix y = 5  (iii) vertex (3, 4), directrix x = 5
questions.explanation: a = distance from vertex to directrix; the parabola opens away from the directrix. All match the key.

questions.question: Find the equation of the parabola whose vertex and point are given: (i) vertex (0, 0), point (3, 4)  (ii) vertex (5, 0), point (4, 6)
questions.explanation: Two orientations fit each point: substitute into y² = 4ax and into x² = 4by (shifted forms in (ii)) and solve for the parameter. Both match the key.

questions.question: Find the standard equation of the parabola whose latus rectum and vertex are the diameter and centre of the circle x² + y² − 4x − 8y − 5 = 0 respectively.
questions.explanation: Circle centre (2, 4), radius √25 = 5, so diameter 10 = latus rectum (4a = 10) and the vertex is (2, 4); either axis orientation is admitted. Matches the key.

questions.question: Find the equation of the circle whose centre is at the focus and whose diameter is the latus rectum of the parabola x² = 12y.
questions.explanation: 4a = 12 gives focus (0, 3) and latus rectum 12, so radius 6: x² + (y − 3)² = 36. Matches the key (the key’s “− 6y²” is a misprint for − 6y).

questions.question: For what point of the parabola y² = 10x is the abscissa equal to three times its ordinate?
questions.explanation: x = 3y substituted gives y² = 30y, so y = 0 or 30. Matches the key.

questions.question: Find the condition when the line y = mx + c is tangent to the parabola x² = 4ay. Also find the point of contact and the equation of the tangent.
questions.answer: Condition: c = −am²; point of contact (2am, am²); tangent y = mx − am²
questions.explanation: Substituting gives x² − 4amx − 4ac = 0; equal roots require 16a²m² + 16ac = 0. Matches the key.

questions.question: Find the condition of tangency and the point of tangency for the following lines and parabolas, and the equation of the tangent in each case: (i) 2x + y = c with y² = 10x  (ii) 3x + 4y = p with x² = 12y  (iii) y = cx with y² = 8(x − 1)
questions.answer:
(i) c = −5/4; contact (5/8, −5/2); tangent y = −2x − 5/4
(ii) p = −27/4; contact (−9/2, 27/16); tangent y = −(3/4)x − 27/16
(iii) c = ±√2; contact (2, ±2√2); tangent y = ±√2·x
questions.explanation: (i) c = a/m with a = 5/2, m = −2. (ii) p/4 = −am² with a = 3, m = −3/4. (iii) c²x² − 8x + 8 = 0 has equal roots when 64 − 32c² = 0. Flag: the key misprints (iii)’s contact as (2, ±√2) and its tangents as 4x ± √2y − 6 = 0; those lines miss both the origin and the contact point.

questions.question: Find the equation of tangent and normal to the following parabolas at the given points: (i) y² = 8x at (2, 4)  (ii) x² = 4y at (−6, 9)  (iii) (y − 1)² = 9(x − 2) at (3, 4)
questions.answer:
(i) tangent x − y + 2 = 0; normal x + y − 6 = 0
(ii) tangent 3x + y + 9 = 0; normal x − 3y + 33 = 0
(iii) tangent 3x − 2y − 1 = 0; normal 2x + 3y − 18 = 0
questions.explanation: Tangent by yy₁ = 4a(x + x₁) (or the shifted form); normal perpendicular at the same point. All match the key.

questions.question: Find the equation of tangent and normal at P(x₁, y₁) to the parabola x² = 4ay.
questions.explanation: Differentiating x² = 4ay gives slope x/(2a) at P; the normal slope is its negative reciprocal. Matches the key.

questions.question: A light house uses a parabolic reflector that is 1 m in diameter. How deep should the reflector be if the light source is placed halfway between the vertex and the plane of the rim to produce a parallel beam of light along the axis of the parabola?
questions.explanation: The source must be at the focus a, and a = d/2 with depth d; the rim point (1/2, d) gives 1/4 = 4a·d = 2d². Matches the key.

questions.question: A parabolic reflector of 12 cm in diameter is used in a vehicle and is 8 cm deep. Where should the light source be placed to produce a parallel beam of light?
questions.answer: At the focus, 9/8 cm (1.125 cm) from the vertex on the axis
questions.explanation: Rim point (6, 8): 36 = 4a·8 → a = 9/8; a parallel beam needs the source at the focus. Matches the key (the key’s unit “m” is a misprint for cm).

questions.question: The main cable of a suspension bridge hangs as a parabola between two towers 100 m apart and 30 m high from the roadway. The cable is 5 m above the roadway at the centre. Find the equation of the parabola and the distance from the centre of a 10 m high suspended cable.
questions.explanation: Vertex (0, 5); tower top (50, 30) gives 4a = 100; at y = 10, x² = 500. Matches the key.

questions.question: The main cable of a suspension bridge is a parabola; the towers are 600 feet apart and 60 feet high from the roadway, and the cable touches the roadway midway between the towers. What is the height of the suspender cable 150 feet from the centre of the bridge?
questions.explanation: Vertex (0, 0); (300, 60) gives 4a = 1500; at x = 150, y = 22500/1500 = 15. Matches the key.

questions.question: Find the semi-axes, eccentricity, foci, vertices, covertices, latus rectum and equations of the directrices of the following ellipses, and draw their graphs: (i) x²/9 + y²/25 = 1  (ii) x²/16 + y²/10 = 1  (iii) (x − 3)²/25 + (y + 4)²/16 = 1  (iv) (x + 1)²/9 + (y − 2)²/16 = 1  (v) 9x² + 25y² = 225  (vi) 4x² − 16x + 25y² + 200y − 316 = 0
questions.answer:
(i) a = 5, b = 3, e = 4/5; foci (0, ±4); vertices (0, ±5); covertices (±3, 0); LR 18/5; directrices y = ±25/4
(ii) a = 4, b = √10, e = √6/4; foci (±√6, 0); vertices (±4, 0); covertices (0, ±√10); LR 5; directrices x = ±16/√6
(iii) a = 5, b = 4, e = 3/5; foci (6, −4), (0, −4); vertices (8, −4), (−2, −4); covertices (3, 0), (3, −8); LR 32/5; directrices 3x − 34 = 0, 3x + 16 = 0
(iv) a = 4, b = 3, e = √7/4; foci (−1, 2 ± √7); vertices (−1, 6), (−1, −2); covertices (2, 2), (−4, 2); LR 9/2; directrices y − 2 = ±16/√7
(v) a = 5, b = 3, e = 4/5; foci (±4, 0); vertices (±5, 0); covertices (0, ±3); LR 18/5; directrices x = ±25/4
(vi) a = 5, b = 2, e = √21/5; foci (2 ± √21, −4); vertices (−3, −4), (7, −4); covertices (2, −6), (2, −2); LR 8/5; directrices x − 2 = ±25/√21
questions.explanation: c² = a² − b² with a the semi-major axis; LR = 2b²/a; directrices ±a/e along the major axis. Flag: in (vi) the printed constant −316 is a book misprint (it would give 4(x − 2)² + 25(y + 4)² = 732); with +316 the ellipse is (x − 2)²/25 + (y + 4)²/4 = 1 and all key entries follow. All match the key.

questions.question: Find the equations of ellipses centred at the origin with axes along the coordinate axes satisfying: (i) major and minor axes 12 and 8, minor axis along y-axis  (ii) major axis along y-axis, passing through (1, √(3/2)) and (2/√3, 1)  (iii) foci (±3, 0), vertices (±5, 0)  (iv) foci (0, ±4) and latus rectum 18/5  (v) foci (±5, 0) and minor axis 12 along y-axis  (vi) minor axis along x-axis of length 8 and latus rectum 6 along y-axis  (vii) covertices (0, ±3) and distance between foci 10  (viii) directrix y = 25/3 and latus rectum 32/5
questions.explanation: (ii) solve 1/b² + (3/2)/a² = 1 with (4/3)/b² + 1/a² = 1 → b² = 2, a² = 3. (iv) 2b²/a = 18/5 with a² − b² = 16 → a = 5. (vi) 2b²/a = 6 with b = 4 → a = 16/3. (viii) a/e = 25/3 with 2b²/a = 32/5 → a = 5, e = 3/5. All match the key.

questions.question: Find the equation of the auxiliary circle to 5x² + 7y² = 11.
questions.explanation: The auxiliary circle has the major axis as diameter; here a² = 11/5. Matches the key.

questions.question: Is the point (4, 5) inside, on, or outside the ellipse 2x² + 3y² = 6?
questions.explanation: 2·16 + 3·25 = 107 > 6. Matches the key.

questions.question: Find the equation of the ellipse with centre at (5, −3), one vertex at (10, −3) and one focus at (9, −3).
questions.explanation: Horizontal major axis with a = 5, c = 4, so b² = 9. Matches the key.

questions.question: For the ellipse 9x² + 13y² = 117 find: (i) the distance between foci  (ii) the distance between vertices  (iii) the distance between covertices.
questions.explanation: x²/13 + y²/9 = 1 gives a = √13, b = 3, c = 2. All match the key.

questions.question: Find the eccentricity of an ellipse if: (i) its axes are 32 and 24  (ii) its latus rectum is equal to half of its major axis.
questions.explanation: (i) a = 16, b = 12, c = 4√7. (ii) 2b²/a = a → c² = a²/2. Both match the key.

questions.question: Find the equation of the circle passing through the focus of the parabola y² + 8x = 0 and the foci of the ellipse 25x² + 16y² = 400.
questions.explanation: The three points are (−2, 0) and (0, ±3); symmetry puts the centre at (5/4, 0) with r² = 169/16. Matches the key.

questions.question: Find the length of, and the equations of, the focal radii drawn to the point (4√3, 5) of the ellipse 25x² + 16y² = 1600.
questions.explanation: x²/64 + y²/100 = 1 has a = 10, e = 3/5, foci (0, ±6); focal radii a ± e·y₁ = 10 ± 3; the lines join each focus to the point. Matches the key.

questions.question: Find the equation of the ellipse with centre at (0, 1) and major axis parallel to the y-axis, passing through (2, 1) and (0, 4).
questions.explanation: x²/b² + (y − 1)²/a² = 1 with (2, 1) giving b² = 4 and (0, 4) giving a² = 9. Matches the key.

questions.question: Find the values of c for which the line y = √5 x + c is a tangent to the ellipse 4x² + 9y² = 36.
questions.explanation: Divide by 36: x²/9 + y²/4 = 1, so a² = 9, b² = 4, m = √5. Tangency c² = a²m² + b² = 45 + 4 = 49, so c = ±7. Matches the key.

questions.question: Show that the line x = 2y + 4 touches the ellipse x²/4 + y²/3 = 1, and find the point of contact.
questions.explanation: Substituting x = 2y + 4 gives (2y+4)²/4 + y²/3 = 1 ⇒ 4y² + 12y + 9 = 0 ⇒ (2y + 3)² = 0, a double root, so the line touches. Then y = −3/2 and x = 2(−3/2) + 4 = 1. Point of contact (1, −3/2). Matches the key.

questions.question: Find the condition that the line y = mx + c may be a tangent to the ellipse x²/b² + y²/a² = 1.
questions.explanation: For the vertical-major ellipse, substituting y = mx + c and setting the discriminant to zero gives c² = a² + b²m². Matches the key.

questions.question: Find the condition that the following lines may touch the ellipse x²/a² + y²/b² = 1: (i) x/p + y/q = 1   (ii) x cos α + y sin α = p   (iii) lx + my + n = 0
questions.answer: (i) a²/p² + b²/q² = 1   (ii) p² = a²cos²α + b²sin²α   (iii) a²l² + b²m² = n²
questions.explanation: Write each line in slope form y = m x + c and impose c² = a²m² + b². (i) m = −q/p, c = q ⇒ q² = a²q²/p² + b² ⇒ a²/p² + b²/q² = 1. (ii) m = −cot α, c = p/sin α ⇒ p² = a²cos²α + b²sin²α. (iii) m = −l/m, c = −n/m ⇒ a²l² + b²m² = n². All match the key.

questions.question: Find the equation of the tangent to the ellipse x²/5 + y²/4 = 1 which has slope 3.
questions.explanation: a² = 5, b² = 4, m = 3, so c = ±√(a²m² + b²) = ±√49 = ±7. Tangents y = 3x + 7 and y = 3x − 7. The key prints only y = 3x + 7, but both values of c satisfy the tangency condition.

questions.question: Find the equations of the tangent and the normal to the ellipse at the given point: (i) 9x² + 25y² = 225 at (3, 12/5)   (ii) 49x² + 64y² = 64·49 at (8 cos α, 7 sin α)
questions.answer: (i) tangent 9x + 20y − 75 = 0, normal 100x − 45y − 192 = 0   (ii) tangent 7x cos α + 8y sin α = 56, normal 8x sin α − 7y cos α − 15 sin α cos α = 0
questions.explanation: (i) x²/25 + y²/9 = 1; tangent 3x/25 + 4y/15 = 1 (≡ 9x + 20y − 75 = 0); normal 25x/3 − 9y/(12/5) = 16 ⇒ 100x − 45y − 192 = 0. Matches the key. (ii) x²/64 + y²/49 = 1; tangent x cos α/8 + y sin α/7 = 1 (≡ 7x cos α + 8y sin α = 56, matches key); normal 8x/cos α − 7y/sin α = 15 ⇒ 8x sin α − 7y cos α = 15 sin α cos α. The key's normal "16x sin α − 14y cos α = 15 sin α" does not pass through the contact point — key misprint (RHS should be 30 sin α cos α).

questions.question: Find the equations of the tangents and normals to the ellipse x²/3 + y²/2 = 1 at the ends of the latus rectum whose abscissa is positive.
questions.answer: Tangents x + √3 y − 3 = 0 and x − √3 y − 3 = 0; normals 3x − √3 y − 1 = 0 and 3x + √3 y − 1 = 0
questions.explanation: a² = 3, b² = 2, c² = 1, e = 1/√3; LR abscissa x = ae = 1 gives y² = 2(1 − 1/3) = 4/3, so ends (1, ±2/√3). Tangent x/3 ± y/√3 = 1 ⇒ x ± √3 y − 3 = 0. Normal 3x − 2y/(±2/√3) = 1 ⇒ 3x −/+ √3 y − 1 = 0. Matches the key.

questions.question: Find the equations of the tangents to the ellipse x²/5 + 9y²/20 = 1 at the points whose abscissa is 1.
questions.explanation: x = 1 gives 9y²/20 = 4/5 ⇒ y = ±4/3. Tangent xx₁/5 + 9yy₁/20 = 1: at (1, 4/3) ⇒ x/5 + 3y/5 = 1 ⇒ x + 3y − 5 = 0; at (1, −4/3) ⇒ x − 3y − 5 = 0. The key's second tangent "x − 3y + 3 = 0" is a misprint — it does not pass through (1, −4/3).

questions.question: Find the equation of the hyperbola with centre at the origin satisfying: (i) transverse and conjugate axes 16 and 12, transverse axis along y-axis; (ii) passes through (3√17/4, 1) and (3, 0), transverse axis along x-axis; (iii) transverse axis of length 8 along y-axis with eccentricity √5; (iv) transverse axis along x-axis with latus rectum 10 and eccentricity 3/2; (v) focus (5, 0), directrix x = 2; (vi) eccentricity 3 and focus (8, 0); (vii) eccentricity 2 and vertex (0, 4).
questions.answer: (i) y²/64 − x²/36 = 1   (ii) 16x² − 9y² = 144   (iii) y²/16 − x²/64 = 1   (iv) x²/16 − y²/20 = 1   (v) x²/10 − y²/15 = 1   (vi) 9x²/64 − 9y²/512 = 1   (vii) y²/16 − x²/48 = 1
questions.explanation: (i) a = 8, b = 6 along y. (ii) (3,0) gives a² = 9; (3√17/4, 1) gives 17/16 − 1 = 1/b² ⇒ b² = 16. (iii) a = 4, c = ae = 4√5 ⇒ b² = 80 − 16 = 64. (iv) 2b²/a = 10 and c² = 9a²/4 = a² + b² ⇒ a = 4, b² = 20. (v) ae = 5, a/e = 2 ⇒ a² = 10, b² = 15. (vi) a = 8/3, b² = 64 − 64/9 = 512/9. (vii) a = 4, c = 8, b² = 48 with transverse axis along y. All match the key.

questions.question: Find equation of the hyperbola with centre (1, 3) satisfying: (i) focus (2, 3), eccentricity √3, transverse axis parallel to x-axis; (ii) focus (4, 5), directrix y = 1, transverse axis parallel to y-axis.
questions.explanation: (i) c = 1, a = c/e = 1/√3 ⇒ a² = 1/3, b² = 2/3 ⇒ 3(x−1)² − (3/2)(y−3)² = 1 ≡ 6(x−1)² − 3(y−3)² = 2. (ii) As printed the data is impossible (the focus must lie on x = 1); using the key's intended focus (1, 5) and directrix y = 2: c = 2, a/e = a²/c = 1 ⇒ a² = 2, b² = 2, giving (y−3)²/2 − (x−1)²/2 = 1. Matches the key; book misprint flagged.

questions.question: Find eccentricity, foci, vertices and latus rectum of each (and sketch the graph): (i) x²/9 − y²/16 = 1   (ii) y²/5 − x²/4 = 1   (iii) 9x² − y² + 1 = 0   (iv) x²/4 − y²/9 = 1
questions.answer: (i) e = 5/3, foci (±5, 0), vertices (±3, 0), LR 32/3   (ii) e = 3/√5, foci (0, ±3), vertices (0, ±√5), LR 8/√5   (iii) e = √10/3, foci (0, ±√10/3), vertices (0, ±1), LR 2/9   (iv) e = √13/2, foci (±√13, 0), vertices (±2, 0), LR 9
questions.explanation: (i) a = 3, b = 4, c = 5. (ii) a² = 5, b² = 4, c = 3 (transverse along y). (iii) Rewrite as y²/1 − x²/(1/9) = 1: c² = 10/9. (iv) a = 2, b = 3, c = √13. Graphs: branches through the vertices inside the semi-axis rectangle with asymptotes y = ±(b/a)x (or ±(a/b)x when the transverse axis is vertical). All match the key.

questions.question: Find centre, foci, eccentricity, vertices and equations of directrices (and sketch the graph): (i) (x−5)²/9 − (y+3)²/16 = 1   (ii) (y−4)²/36 − (x+5)²/64 = 1   (iii) 9x² − 4y² + 36x + 8y − 4 = 0   (iv) 25x² − 150x − 9y² + 72y + 306 = 0
questions.answer: (i) centre (5, −3), foci (10, −3), (0, −3), e = 5/3, vertices (8, −3), (2, −3), directrices x = 16/5, 34/5   (ii) centre (−5, 4), foci (−5, 14), (−5, −6), e = 5/3, vertices (−5, 10), (−5, −2), directrices y = 38/5, 2/5   (iii) centre (−2, 1), foci (−2 ± √13, 1), e = √13/2, vertices (0, 1), (−4, 1), directrices x = −2 ± 4/√13   (iv) centre (3, 4), foci (3, 4 ± √34), e = √34/5, vertices (3, 9), (3, −1), directrices y = 4 ± 25/√34
questions.explanation: (i) a = 3, b = 4, c = 5. (ii) a = 6, b = 8, c = 10 (transverse vertical). (iii) Completing squares: 9(x+2)² − 4(y−1)² = 36 ⇒ (x+2)²/4 − (y−1)²/9 = 1, so a = 2, b = 3, c = √13 (the key's foci "( −2, ±√13, 1)" is a typeslip for (−2 ± √13, 1)). (iv) 25(x−3)² − 9(y−4)² = −225 ⇒ (y−4)²/25 − (x−3)²/9 = 1, so a = 5, b = 3, c = √34; the key omits the vertices and directrices given here.

questions.question: Find equation of rectangular hyperbola with centre at origin whose vertices are (±4, 0) and find equation of its conjugate hyperbola. Also, find equations of asymptotes of the rectangular hyperbola.
questions.answer: x² − y² = 16; conjugate y² − x² = 16; asymptotes y = ±x
questions.explanation: Rectangular hyperbola with vertices (±4, 0) has a = b = 4: x²/16 − y²/16 = 1 ⇒ x² − y² = 16. Its conjugate is x²/16 − y²/16 = −1, i.e. y² − x² = 16. Asymptotes of x² − y² = 16 are y = ±x.

questions.question: Find the eccentricity of a hyperbola whose latus rectum is double the transverse axis.
questions.explanation: 2b²/a = 2(2a) ⇒ b² = 2a² ⇒ c² = a² + b² = 3a² ⇒ e = c/a = √3.

questions.question: Show that the eccentricities e₁ and e₂ of the two conjugate hyperbolas satisfy the relation e₁² + e₂² = e₁² e₂².
questions.explanation: For x²/a² − y²/b² = 1, e₁² = (a²+b²)/a²; for its conjugate y²/b² − x²/a² = 1, e₂² = (a²+b²)/b². Hence 1/e₁² + 1/e₂² = a²/(a²+b²) + b²/(a²+b²) = 1; multiplying by e₁² e₂² gives e₁² + e₂² = e₁² e₂².

questions.question: For what value of k, the line y = 2kx will be tangent to 2x² − 5y² = 10.
questions.explanation: x²/5 − y²/2 = 1 with m = 2k, c = 0; tangency c² = a²m² − b² gives 20k² = 2, so k = ±1/√10. Matches the key.

questions.question: Find the condition when the line y = mx + c is tangent to y²/a² − x²/b² = 1.
