questions.explanation: Substituting gives (b²m² − a²)x² + 2b²mcx + b²c² − a²b² = 0; zero discriminant reduces to a²(b²m² + c² − a²) = 0, i.e. c² = a² − b²m². The key prints the sign-reversed c² = b²m² − a², which even fails for the horizontal tangents y = ±a — key misprint.

questions.question: Find the equation of tangent to the hyperbola 3x² − 4y² = 12 when slope is 3.
questions.explanation: x²/4 − y²/3 = 1; c² = a²m² − b² = 36 − 3 = 33. Matches the key.

questions.question: Find the equation of tangent and normal to y²/a² − x²/b² = 1 at (x₁, y₁).
questions.explanation: Differentiating: y′ = a²x/(b²y), giving the tangent slope at the point; the normal is perpendicular. Equivalently tangent yy₁/a² − xx₁/b² = 1 and normal b²x/x₁ + a²y/y₁ = a² + b². Matches the key.

questions.question: Find the equation of tangent and normal to x²/5 − y²/7 = 1 at (2√5, √7).
questions.explanation: The printed point is not on the curve (S₁ = 4 − 1 = 3), so the key's line is the polar T = S₁: xx₁/5 − yy₁/7 = 3 ⇒ 14√5 x − 5√7 y − 105 = 0, with the normal perpendicular to it through the point. Reproduced as keyed; book/key defect flagged.

questions.question: Find the transformed equation of (x−6)²/25 + (y+7)²/16 = 1 when axes are translated with new origin (6, −7).
questions.explanation: With x = X + 6 and y = Y − 7 the equation becomes X²/25 + Y²/16 = 1. Matches the key.

questions.question: If xy-axes are rotated through angle θ, find the new coordinates of P: (i) (2, 3), θ = 60°   (ii) (6, 7), θ = 45°   (iii) (−4, 6), θ = 30°
questions.explanation: Use X = x cos θ + y sin θ, Y = −x sin θ + y cos θ. (i) X = 1 + 3√3/2, Y = −√3 + 3/2. (ii) X = 13/√2, Y = 1/√2. (iii) X = −2√3 + 3, Y = 2 + 3√3. All match the key.

questions.question: Find new origin O′ and new XY-axes with respect to the xy-system if it is translated 6 units to the left, 5 units up and rotated π/6 radians anticlockwise.
questions.explanation: Translation gives O′ = (−6, 5). The X-axis through O′ with direction (cos 30°, sin 30°) is x − √3 y + 6 + 5√3 = 0; the Y-axis with direction (−sin 30°, cos 30°) is √3 x + y + 6√3 − 5 = 0. Matches the key.

questions.question: Find new coordinates of P(4, 5) if new origin is (1, 2) and the XY-system is rotated π/6 radians anticlockwise from the xy-system.
questions.explanation: Relative coordinates (3, 3); X = 3cos30° + 3sin30° = (3√3+3)/2 and Y = −3sin30° + 3cos30° = (3√3−3)/2. The key's ((2√3+3)/2, (5√3−8)/2) is internally inconsistent (its components imply different pre-images) — key misprint.

questions.question: Identify and sketch the curve xy = 9.
questions.answer: X² − Y² = 18 — rectangular hyperbola, centre at origin, axes rotated 45°
questions.explanation: Rotating by 45° (x = (X−Y)/√2, y = (X+Y)/√2) gives (X²−Y²)/2 = 9, i.e. X² − Y² = 18 with a² = b² = 18: rectangular hyperbola whose vertices are (±3√2, 0) in XY and whose asymptotes are the original axes. Matches the key.

questions.question: Through which angle should the axes be rotated about the origin so that the transformed equation of 9x² + 12xy + 4y² − x − y = 0 does not contain the XY term.
questions.explanation: cot 2θ = (A − B)/H = (9 − 4)/12 = 5/12, so tan 2θ = 12/5 and θ = ½ tan⁻¹(12/5). Matches the key.

questions.question: Tick the correct option: (i) eccentricity zero → conic; (ii) focus of x² = −16y; (iii) latus rectum and vertex of (y−3)² = −8(x+4); (iv) tangent at (4, 6) to y² = 9x; (v) latus rectum of x²/25 + y²/16 = 1; (vi) eccentricity of x²/5 + y²/4 = 1; (vii) centre of (x+5)²/10 + (y−3)²/20 = 1; (viii) directrices of x²/4 + y²/2 = 1; (ix) ax² + by² + gx + fy + c = 0 is a hyperbola if; (x) auxiliary circle of x²/6 + y²/5 = 1; (xi) directrices of (x−h)²/p² + (y−k)²/q² = 1 (q > p); (xii) vertices of x²/9 + y²/16 = 1 (hyperbola); (xiii) conjugate hyperbola of x²/5 − y²/6 = 1; (xiv) eccentricity of rectangular hyperbola; (xv) tangent to x²/6 + y²/5 = 1 at (√6, 0); (xvi) y = k tangent to x²/25 + y²/9 = 1; (xvii) tangent to x²/16 − y²/9 = 1 with slope 2; (xviii) xy = c² represents; (xix) origin shifted to (2, 3), coordinates of (5, 6); (xx) abscissa transformation for rotation by π/4.
questions.answer: (i) c   (ii) d   (iii) d   (iv) d   (v) b   (vi) b   (vii) c   (viii) a   (ix) b   (x) d   (xi) c   (xii) c   (xiii) b   (xiv) d   (xv) b   (xvi) a   (xvii) d   (xviii) c   (xix) b   (xx) b
questions.explanation: (i) e = 0 is a circle. (ii) 4a = 16 opening down: (0, −4). (iii) 4a = 8, vertex (−4, 3). (iv) 6y = (9/2)(x+4) ≡ 3x − 4y + 12 = 0 (options a and d coincide; key ticks d). (v) 2b²/a = 32/5. (vi) c² = 1, e = 1/√5. (vii) (−5, 3). (viii) x = ±a/e = ±4/√2 (options a and d coincide; key ticks a). (ix) a, b of different sign. (x) x² + y² = 6. (xi) major axis vertical: y − k = ±q/e. (xii) (0, ±4). (xiii) y²/6 − x²/5 = 1. (xiv) √2. (xv) x = √6. (xvi) k = ±3. (xvii) c² = 16·4 − 9 = 55. (xviii) hyperbola. (xix) (3, 3). (xx) x = x′/√2 − y′/√2. All match the key.

questions.question: Find the foci, vertices and directrices for the conic: (a) (x−5)²/25 + (y+3)²/16 = 1   (b) (x+4)²/9 − (y+7)²/16 = 1
questions.answer: (a) foci (8, −3), (2, −3); vertices (10, −3), (0, −3); x − 5 = ±25/3   (b) foci (1, −7), (−9, −7); vertices (−1, −7), (−7, −7); x + 4 = ±9/5
questions.explanation: (a) Ellipse with a = 5, b = 4, c = 3, e = 3/5; directrices x = 5 ± a/e = 5 ± 25/3. (b) Hyperbola with a = 3, b = 4, c = 5, e = 5/3; directrices x = −4 ± a/e = −4 ± 9/5. Both match the key.

questions.question: Find the condition of tangency when the line y = x + c is tangent to the conic: (i) y² = 10x   (ii) 2x² + 3y² = 6   (iii) 5x² − 7y² = 35
questions.explanation: (i) Parabola 4a = 10: c = a/m = 5/2. (ii) x²/3 + y²/2 = 1: c² = a²m² + b² = 5. (iii) x²/7 − y²/5 = 1: c² = a²m² − b² = 2. All match the key.

questions.question: Find transformed equation of (x+5)²/7 − (y−3)²/5 = 1 when new origin is (−5, 3).
questions.explanation: With x = X − 5 and y = Y + 3 the equation becomes X²/7 − Y²/5 = 1. The key prints X²/7 + Y²/5 = 1, losing the hyperbola's minus sign — key misprint.

questions.question: If xy-axes are rotated through angle θ, find coordinates of P if new coordinates are (−2, 7), θ = 45°.
questions.explanation: Old coordinates from new: x = X cos θ − Y sin θ = (−2 − 7)/√2 = −9/√2 and y = X sin θ + Y cos θ = (−2 + 7)/√2 = 5/√2. Matches the key.

questions.question: Find the order and degree of each of the following differential equations: (i) d²y/dx² + (dy/dx)³ + xy = 0   (ii) x³dx + y³dy = 0   (iii) dy/dx = √₃((d²y/dx² + 1)²)   (iv) d³y/dx³ − 5(d²y/dx²)³ + 7(dy/dx)&sup8; = 0   (v) d⁴y/dx⁴ − (dy/dx)^(1/2) = 0
questions.answer: (i) order 2, degree 1   (ii) order 1, degree 1   (iii) order 2, degree 2   (iv) order 3, degree 1   (v) order 4, degree 2
questions.explanation: (ii) dy/dx = −x³/y³. (iii) Cubing: (y′)³ = (y″ + 1)², so the highest derivative y″ appears with power 2. (v) Squaring: (y⁴)² = y′. All match the key.

questions.question: Show that y = x − x ln x is the solution of the differential equation x dy/dx + x − y = 0.
questions.explanation: y′ = 1 − (ln x + 1) = −ln x, so x(−ln x) + x − (x − x ln x) = −x ln x + x ln x = 0.

questions.question: Show that y = Ae^(2x) + Be^(3x) is the general solution of d²y/dx² − 5 dy/dx + 6y = 0.
questions.explanation: y′ = 2Ae^(2x) + 3Be^(3x), y″ = 4Ae^(2x) + 9Be^(3x); then (4 − 10 + 6)Ae^(2x) + (9 − 15 + 6)Be^(3x) = 0. The two constants match the order 2, so it is the general solution.

questions.question: Obtain the differential equation by eliminating arbitrary constants from: (i) y = A cos x + B sin x   (ii) y = A sin(x + 1)   (iii) y = ax² + bx   (iv) y = C₁e^x + C₂e^(−2x)
questions.answer: (i) y″ + y = 0   (ii) dy/dx = y cot(x + 1)   (iii) x²y″ − 2xy′ + 2y = 0   (iv) y″ + y′ − 2y = 0
questions.explanation: (i) y″ = −A cos x − B sin x = −y. (ii) y′ = A cos(x+1), so y′/y = cot(x+1). (iii) y′ = 2ax + b, y″ = 2a give a = y″/2, b = y′ − xy″; substituting back yields x²y″ − 2xy′ + 2y = 0. (iv) The exponents 1 and −2 are roots of r² + r − 2 = 0. All match the key.

questions.question: Find the particular solution of: (i) dy/dx = √(1+cos y)/sin y, y(3) = π/2, given that x + 2√(1+cos y) + c = 0 is the general solution; (ii) d²y/dx² − dy/dx + 2y = 0, y(0) = 1, y′(0) = 3, given that y = Ae^(2x) + Be^(−x) is the general solution.
questions.explanation: (i) 3 + 2√(1+cos π/2) + c = 0 ⇒ 3 + 2 + c = 0 ⇒ c = −5. (ii) A + B = 1 and 2A − B = 3 give A = 4/3, B = −1/3. Note the printed equation of (ii) should read y″ − y′ − 2y = 0 for the stated general solution (roots 2, −1) — book misprint; answers match the key.

questions.question: Solve by separating the variables: (i) x tan y dy = dx   (ii) x sin y dx + (x²+1) cos y dy = 0   (iii) y(1+x)dx + x(1+y)dy = 0   (iv) (1+x³)dy − x²dx = 0   (v) xy dy = (y+1)(1−x)dx   (vi) dy/dx = 3y² − y² sin x   (vii) (y²−1) dy/dx = 4xy²   (viii) x cos²y dx + tan y dy = 0
questions.answer: (i) sec y = Cx   (ii) sin y·√(x²+1) = C   (iii) (x+y) + ln(xy) = C   (iv) y = (1/3)ln(1+x³) + C   (v) (x+y) − ln(x+xy) = C   (vi) −1/y = 3x + cos x + C   (vii) y + 1/y = 2x² + C   (viii) tan²y = −x² + C
questions.explanation: (i) ∫tan y dy = ∫dx/x. (ii) ∫x/(x²+1)dx + ∫cot y dy = 0 gives ½ln(x²+1) + ln sin y = c, i.e. sin y = C/√(x²+1); the key prints C√(x²+1) with the wrong power of (x²+1). (iii) Divide by xy. (iv) dy = x²/(1+x³)dx. (v) y/(y+1)dy = (1−x)/x dx. (vi) dy/y² = (3 − sin x)dx. (vii) (1 − 1/y²)dy = 4x dx. (viii) x dx + tan y sec²y dy = 0.

questions.question: Solve the homogeneous equations: (i) (x+y)dy − (x−y)dx = 0   (ii) (6x²+2y²)dx − (x²+4xy)dy = 0   (iii) (x²+3y²)dx − 2xy dy = 0   (iv) (x²+y²)dx − 2xy dy = 0   (v) dy/dx = y/x + sin(y/x)
questions.answer: (i) √(x²−2xy−y²) = C   (ii) (3x−2y)(2x+y) = Cx   (iii) x² + y² = Cx³   (iv) x² − y² = Cx   (v) cosec(y/x) − cot(y/x) = Cx
questions.explanation: Substitute y = vx throughout. (i) (1+v)/(1−2v−v²)dv = dx/x gives x²−2xy−y² = C. (ii) (1+4v)/(6−v−2v²)dv = dx/x gives x(6−v−2v²) = C, i.e. 6x²−xy−2y² = Cx; the key's (y+2x)(2y−3x) = C drops the factor x and does not differentiate back to the ODE. (iii) 2v/(1+v²)dv = dx/x. (iv) 2v/(1−v²)dv = dx/x. (v) csc v dv = dx/x with tan(v/2) = csc v − cot v.

questions.question: Solve: (i) dy/dx = (x+y+1)/(x−y)   (ii) (2x+y+1)dx + (2x+y−1)dy = 0   (iii) dy/dx = (x+2y−3)/(2x+y−3)   (iv) dy/dx = (2x+y−2)/(2x+y+3)
questions.answer: (i) tan⁻¹((2y+1)/(2x+1)) − ln√(x²+y²+x+y+½) = C   (ii) (x+y) + 2ln|2x+y−3| = C   (iii) (x+y−2) = C(x−y)³   (iv) (1/3)(2x+y) + (5/9)ln|6x+3y+4| = x + C
questions.explanation: (i) Shift to X = x+½, Y = y+½ then Y′ = (X+Y)/(X−Y): tan⁻¹(Y/X) − ½ln(X²+Y²) = C. (ii) u = 2x+y gives dx = (u−1)/(u−3)du, so x = u + 2ln|u−3| + C; the key's single-ln form fails d/dx verification. (iii) Shift to X = x−1, Y = y−1 then (2+v)/(1−v²)dv = dX/X gives (1+v)/(1−v)³ = CX². (iv) u = 2x+y gives (u+3)/(3u+4)du = dx.

questions.question: A body moves in a straight line so that its velocity exceeds by 2 its distance from a fixed point of the line. If V = 5 m/s when t = 0, find the equation of the motion.
questions.explanation: ds/dt = s + 2 ⇒ ln(s+2) = t + c ⇒ s + 2 = Ce^t. At t = 0, s = V − 2 = 3 so C = 5. The key omits this question; solution supplied here.

questions.question: When the temperature of the air is 290 K a certain substance cools from 400 K to 350 K in 20 minutes. Find (i) the temperature after 40 minutes; (ii) after how much time the temperature is 300 K.
questions.explanation: Newton's cooling: T − 290 = Ce^(−kt) with C = 110 and e^(−20k) = 60/110 = 6/11. (i) T(40) − 290 = 110(6/11)² = 360/11 ≈ 32.7 ⇒ T ≈ 322 K. (ii) 10 = 110e^(−kt) ⇒ t = 20 ln 11/ln(11/6) ≈ 79 minutes. Matches the key.

questions.question: A resistor of 5 ohms and a capacitor of 0.02 farads are connected with a 10 volts battery. Assume that initially the charge on the capacitor is 5 coulombs. Find the charge and current in the circuit at any time.
questions.explanation: R dQ/dt + Q/C = V ⇒ 5 dQ/dt + 50Q = 10 ⇒ dQ/dt + 10Q = 2, so Q = 1/5 + Ce^(−10t); Q(0) = 5 gives C = 24/5. I = dQ/dt = −48e^(−10t). Matches the key.

questions.question: The population of a certain town is directly proportional to the square root of the present population at any time. If the population initially is 20000: (i) how much the population after 10 years? (ii) after how much time the population be doubled?
questions.answer: (i) ≈ 66860   (ii) 5 years (the key's 14.92 years is the five-fold time)
questions.explanation: dP/dt = k√P ⇒ 2√P = kt + 2√20000. As printed no second datum fixes k; the key's numbers imply doubling in 5 years (k ≈ 23.43), giving P(10) = 20000(2√2 − 1)² ≈ 66860. With that datum the doubling time is 5 years, while 14.92 years corresponds to P = 100000 (five-fold) — key discrepancy flagged.

questions.question: Find the orthogonal trajectory of the curves y = ax².
questions.explanation: Family ODE: y′ = 2y/x; orthogonal: y′ = −x/(2y) ⇒ 2y dy = −x dx. Matches the key.

questions.question: Find the orthogonal trajectories of the hyperbola xy = c.
questions.explanation: Family ODE: y′ = −y/x; orthogonal: y′ = x/y ⇒ y dy = x dx. Matches the key.

questions.question: Find the orthogonal trajectories of the family of parabolas y² = 4ax.
questions.explanation: 2yy′ = 4a = y²/x gives y′ = y/(2x); orthogonal: y′ = −2x/y ⇒ y dy = −2x dx. Matches the key.

questions.question: Find the orthogonal trajectories of the family of curves y = x/(1 + c₁x).
questions.explanation: 1/y = 1/x + c₁ gives y′ = y²/x²; orthogonal: y′ = −x²/y² ⇒ y²dy = −x²dx ⇒ x³ + y³ = C. The key's −1/y = −1/x + C is the original family itself — key misprint.

questions.question: Find the general equation of family of curves perpendicular to y = c₁ sin x.
questions.explanation: Family ODE: y′ = y cot x; orthogonal: y′ = −tan x/y ⇒ y dy = −tan x dx ⇒ y²/2 = ln cos x + c ⇒ e^(y²) = C cos²x. Matches the key.

questions.question: Find the general equation of family of curves perpendicular to x^(1/3) + y^(1/3) = c.
questions.explanation: Family ODE: y′ = −y^(2/3)/x^(2/3); orthogonal: y′ = x^(2/3)/y^(2/3) ⇒ y^(2/3)dy = x^(2/3)dx ⇒ y^(5/3) − x^(5/3) = C. Matches the key.

questions.question: Tick the correct answer: (i) order and degree of 1 + y″ = xy′; (ii) degree of (y′)⁴ + 3y″″; (iii) order and degree of (y″″″)² = √(y′); (iv) degree of y = x(y′)² + y′; (v) order and degree of y″ = √(1 + (y′)³); (vi) value of y(−1) if xdy − ydx = 0, y(1) = 2; (vii) general solution of y′ + y² = 0; (viii) general solution of 9yy′ + 4x = 0.
questions.answer: (i) b   (ii) c   (iii) a   (iv) b   (v) a   (vi) b   (vii) b   (viii) a
questions.explanation: (i) order 2, degree 1. (ii) highest derivative y″ appears to power 1, so degree 1. (iii) squaring twice: (y″″″)⁴ = y′ ⇒ order 3, degree 4. (iv) y′ appears squared ⇒ degree 2. (v) (y″)² = 1 + (y′)³ ⇒ order 2, degree 2. (vi) y = cx with y(1) = 2 gives y = 2x, y(−1) = −2. (vii) −1/y = −x + c ⇒ y = 1/(x + c). (viii) 9y dy = −4x dx ⇒ 4x² + 9y² = c. All match the key.

questions.question: Show that y = Ae^(3x) + Be^(4x) is the general solution of d²y/dx² − 7dy/dx + 12y = 0.
questions.answer: Verified (identity holds for all A, B)
questions.explanation: y′ = 3Ae^(3x) + 4Be^(4x) and y″ = 9Ae^(3x) + 16Be^(4x), so y″ − 7y′ + 12y = (9 − 21 + 12)Ae^(3x) + (16 − 28 + 12)Be^(4x) = 0. The solution contains two independent arbitrary constants, matching the order 2 of the equation, so it is the general solution.

questions.question: Solve: (i) cos(x+y)dy = dx   (ii) x²y′ = x² + xy + y²   (iii) (xy + y²)dx = (x² − xy)dy   (iv) xy′ = y + x tan(y/x)   (v) (2x + 3y − 5)dy + (3x + 2y + 1)dx = 0   (vi) (2x + y + 1)dx + (4x + 2y − 1)dy = 0   (vii) y′ = y/x + cos(y/x)   (viii) y′ = e^(x+y)
questions.answer: (i) tan((x+y)/2) = y + C   (ii) tan⁻¹(y/x) = ln x + C   (iii) x/y + ln(xy) = C   (iv) sin(y/x) = Cx   (v) 3x² + 4xy + 3y² + 2x − 10y = C   (vi) ln|2x + y − 1| + (x + 2y) = C   (vii) sec(y/x) + tan(y/x) = Cx   (viii) −e^(−y) = e^x + C
questions.explanation: (i) Put u = x + y: dx = cos u/(1 + cos u) du = (1 − ½sec²(u/2))du, so x = u − tan(u/2) + C. (ii) Homogeneous: v = y/x gives dv/(1 + v²) = dx/x. (iii) v = y/x gives (1 − v)/(2v²) dv = dx/x, integrating to x/y + ln(xy) = C; the key's x/y = ln(Cy) does not differentiate back to the equation — key misprint. (iv) v = y/x gives cot v dv = dx/x, so ln sin v = ln x + c, i.e. sin(y/x) = Cx; the key's y = x cos⁻¹(Cx) corresponds to y′ = y/x − cot(y/x) — key misprint. (v) Exact after shifting the origin to (−13/5, 17/5); the key's shifted form is the same first integral. (vi) u = 2x + y gives 3(1 − u)dx + (2u − 1)du = 0. (vii) v = y/x gives sec v dv = dx/x. (viii) Separate: e^(−y)dy = e^x dx.

questions.question: If y = (A + Bx)e^(−2x) is the general solution of d²y/dx² + 4dy/dx + 4y = 0, find its particular solution when y(0) = 2 and y′(0) = 5.
questions.explanation: y(0) = A = 2. y′ = Be^(−2x) − 2(A + Bx)e^(−2x), so y′(0) = B − 2A = 5 gives B = 9. Matches the key.

questions.question: Form the differential equation by eliminating the arbitrary constants: (i) y = 9/x + b   (ii) y = e^x(a cos x + b sin x)   (iii) y = ln cos(x − a) + b   (iv) y = A cos(ln x) + B sin(ln x)
questions.answer: (i) y′ = −9/x²   (ii) y″ − 2y′ + 2y = 0   (iii) y″ = −(1 + (y′)²)   (iv) x²y″ + xy′ + y = 0
questions.explanation: (i) Differentiate once: y′ = −9/x² (b disappears). (ii) Roots of the auxiliary equation are 1 ± i, so the ODE is y″ − 2y′ + 2y = 0. (iii) y′ = −tan(x − a) and y″ = −sec²(x − a) = −(1 + tan²(x − a)), giving y″ = −(1 + (y′)²); the key prints the positive sign — key misprint. (iv) With t = ln x the equation becomes d²y/dt² + y = 0, i.e. x²y″ + xy′ + y = 0.

questions.question: A particle moving in a straight line has acceleration dv/dt = 1/√t. If V = 25 m/s when t = 9 s, find the velocity after 20 s.
questions.explanation: v = ∫t^(−1/2)dt = 2√t + C; 25 = 2(3) + C gives C = 19. Hence v(20) = 2√20 + 19 = 4√5 + 19 m/s. Matches the key.

questions.question: Find the orthogonal trajectories of the family of curves 3x + 4y = c.
questions.explanation: Differentiating, 3 + 4y′ = 0, so the family slope is −3/4. Orthogonal trajectories have slope 4/3: dy/dx = 4/3 ⇒ 3y = 4x + C (another family of parallel lines). Matches the key.

questions.question: Find the equation of the family of curves perpendicular to y = ln(tan x + c₁).
questions.explanation: From e^y = tan x + c₁, the family ODE is e^y y′ = sec²x. Perpendicular curves satisfy y′ = −e^y cos²x, i.e. e^(−y)dy = −cos²x dx = −(1 + cos 2x)/2 dx. Integrating: −e^(−y) = −½(x + (sin 2x)/2) + C₁. Matches the key.

questions.question: Find ∂f/∂x and ∂f/∂y when f(x, y) is given by: (i) 3x³ + y² − 6x + 2y − 7   (ii) x² + xy − y² − 2x − 2y − 8   (iii) sin(x + y)   (iv) e^x cos y   (v) ½ln(x² + y²)
questions.answer: (i) 9x² − 6, 2y + 2   (ii) 2x + y − 2, x − 2y − 2   (iii) cos(x + y), cos(x + y)   (iv) e^x cos y, −e^x sin y   (v) x/(x² + y²), y/(x² + y²)
questions.explanation: Differentiate treating the other variable as constant. (i) ∂/∂x kills y-terms and vice versa. (iii) Chain rule on x + y gives cos(x + y) for both. (iv) e^x is constant in y, cos y is constant in x. (v) ½ · 2x/(x² + y²) and the symmetric y form. All match the key.

questions.question: The volume of the cone is given by V = (1/3)πr²h. Differentiate V with respect to its independent variables.
questions.explanation: Holding h constant: ∂V/∂r = (1/3)πh · 2r = (2/3)πrh. Holding r constant: ∂V/∂h = (1/3)πr². Matches the key.

questions.question: Check whether the following functions are homogeneous or not; find the degree if homogeneous: (i) (x³ − 5x²y + 7xy² + y³)/(xy²)   (ii) tan((x+y)/y²)   (iii) x³ + 3x²y + 2y²x + y³   (iv) cos⁻¹((x² − y²)/(xy))   (v) (x² − xy + y²)/(x + y²)   (vi) √(x⁸ − 3x²y⁶)   (vii) x³ sin(y²/x)   (viii) ln((x² + y²)/(x + y))
questions.answer: (i) homogeneous, degree 0   (ii) not homogeneous   (iii) homogeneous, degree 3   (iv) homogeneous, degree 0   (v) not homogeneous   (vi) homogeneous, degree 4   (vii) not homogeneous   (viii) not homogeneous
questions.explanation: Test f(tx, ty) = tⁿf(x, y). (i) degree 3 over degree 3 ⇒ n = 0. (ii) argument mixes degree 1 over degree 2. (iii) every term degree 3. (iv) argument degree 0. (v) denominator mixes degrees 1 and 2. (vi) radicand degree 8, square root halves it ⇒ n = 4. (vii) sin(t·y²/x) does not scale as a power of t. (viii) ln t + ln((x²+y²)/(x+y)) ≠ tⁿf. All match the key.

questions.question: Verify Euler's theorem x ∂f/∂x + y ∂f/∂y = nf for: (i) xy + y²   (ii) cos(x/y)   (iii) √(xy) − x   (iv) ln((x + y)/y)
questions.explanation: (i) fₓ = y, fᵧ = x + 2y ⇒ xy + xy + 2y² = 2f. (ii) fₓ = −sin(x/y)/y, fᵧ = x sin(x/y)/y² ⇒ the two terms cancel. (iii) fₓ = ½√(y/x) − 1, fᵧ = ½√(x/y) ⇒ ½√(xy) − x + ½√(xy) = f. (iv) fₓ = 1/(x+y), fᵧ = 1/(x+y) − 1/y ⇒ 1 − 1 = 0. All match the key.

questions.question: If u = x²(y − x) + y²(x − y), show that ∂u/∂x + ∂u/∂y = −2(x − y)².
questions.explanation: Expand u = x²y − x³ + xy² − y³. Then uₓ = 2xy − 3x² + y² and uᵧ = x² + 2xy − 3y²; adding gives −2x² + 4xy − 2y² = −2(x − y)².

questions.question: If u = tan⁻¹((x³ + y³)/(x − y)), prove that x ∂u/∂x + y ∂u/∂y = sin 2u.
questions.answer: Shown: x uₓ + y uᵧ = 2 tan u/sec²u = sin 2u
questions.explanation: w = (x³ + y³)/(x − y) is homogeneous of degree 2, so Euler gives x wₓ + y wᵧ = 2w. With w = tan u, wₓ = sec²u · uₓ (and likewise in y), hence sec²u (x uₓ + y uᵧ) = 2 tan u, i.e. x uₓ + y uᵧ = 2 sin u cos u = sin 2u.

questions.question: Use the MAPLE command >diff to partial differentiate with respect to x and y: (i) x²y + xy + xy²   (ii) y + x cos(y)   (iii) (x + √x)/(y + √y)
questions.answer: (i) ∂/∂x = 2xy + y + y², ∂/∂y = x² + x + 2xy   (ii) cos y, 1 − x sin y   (iii) (1 + 1/(2√x))/(y + √y), −(x + √x)(1 + 1/(2√y))/(y + √y)²
questions.explanation: MAPLE session: > f := x^2*y + x*y + x*y^2; then > diff(f, x); and > diff(f, y); give the pair in (i). For (ii) > f := y + x*cos(y); gives cos(y) and 1 − x*sin(y). For (iii) > f := (x + sqrt(x))/(y + sqrt(y)); gives (2√x + 1)/(2√x(y + √y)) in x and −(x + √x)(2√y + 1)/(2√y(y + √y)²) in y. Matches the key's commands.

questions.question: Tick the correct answer: (i) f = e^(xy): fₓ/fᵧ = ?   (ii) surface area of a cube is a function of how many variables?   (iii) g = cos(x/y): gᵧ/gₓ = ?   (iv) degree of homogeneity of tan(2x/(3y))?   (v) P = 2(x + y): sum of the partial derivatives = ?   (vi) z homogeneous of degree 0: x zₓ + y zᵧ = ?   (vii) area of a trapezium is a function of how many variables?   (viii) w homogeneous of degree 2/3: u wᵤ + v wᵥ = ?   (ix) z = f(u/v) of degree 0: v ∂z/∂v = ?   (x) f, g homogeneous of degrees 2 and 3: degree of f/g = ?
questions.answer: (i) c   (ii) a   (iii) a   (iv) d   (v) d   (vi) c   (vii) c   (viii) d   (ix) c   (x) d
questions.explanation: (i) y e^(xy)/(x e^(xy)) = y/x. (ii) S = 6s² uses the single edge s. (iii) (x sin(x/y)/y²)/(−sin(x/y)/y) = −x/y. (iv) argument degree 0. (v) 2 + 2 = 4. (vi) Euler with n = 0. (vii) A = ½(a + b)h uses three lengths. (viii) Euler with n = 2/3 gives (2/3)w. (ix) u zᵤ + v zᵥ = 0 with zᵤ = f′/v, zᵥ = −u f′/v² ⇒ v zᵥ = −u zᵤ. (x) t²/t³ = t⁻¹. All match the key.

questions.question: Let f(x, y) = xy and g(x, y) = ½xy be the homogeneous functions for the areas of rectangle and triangle. Are f + g, f − g, fg and f/g homogeneous? If yes, what are their degrees?
questions.answer: All homogeneous: f + g degree 2, f − g degree 2, fg degree 4, f/g degree 0
questions.explanation: f + g = (3/2)xy and f − g = ½xy scale as t²; fg = ½x²y² scales as t⁴; f/g = 2 is constant, i.e. t⁰. Sums, products and quotients of homogeneous functions of equal degree (for + and −) combine degrees additively.

questions.question: Verify Euler's theorem for the function z = √(x² + y²).
questions.explanation: z is homogeneous of degree 1. zₓ = x/√(x² + y²) and zᵧ = y/√(x² + y²), so x zₓ + y zᵧ = (x² + y²)/√(x² + y²) = √(x² + y²) = z = 1·z.

questions.question: Given that z = g(x, y) is a homogeneous function of degree 3, show that x ∂z/∂x + y ∂z/∂y = 3z.
questions.answer: Shown by differentiating g(tx, ty) = t³g(x, y) in t at t = 1
questions.explanation: Homogeneity gives g(tx, ty) = t³g(x, y). Differentiating with respect to t: x gₓ(tx, ty) + y gᵧ(tx, ty) = 3t²g(x, y). Putting t = 1 yields x zₓ + y zᵧ = 3z.

questions.question: Given that y = f(u, v) is a homogeneous function of degree −3/2, show that u ∂y/∂u + v ∂y/∂v = −(3/2)y.
questions.answer: Shown by differentiating f(tu, tv) = t^(−3/2)f(u, v) in t at t = 1
questions.explanation: f(tu, tv) = t^(−3/2)f(u, v). Differentiating in t: u fᵤ(tu, tv) + v fᵥ(tu, tv) = −(3/2)t^(−5/2)f(u, v). At t = 1 this is u yᵤ + v yᵥ = −(3/2)y.

questions.question: Given that u = sin⁻¹((√x − √y)/(√x + √y)), show that x ∂u/∂x + y ∂u/∂y = 0.
questions.explanation: w = (√x − √y)/(√x + √y) is homogeneous of degree 0, so Euler gives x wₓ + y wᵧ = 0. Since sin u = w, wₓ = cos u · uₓ and wᵧ = cos u · uᵧ, hence cos u (x uₓ + y uᵧ) = 0 and (cos u ≠ 0) the bracket vanishes.

questions.question: Given that u = sec⁻¹((x³ − y³)/(x + y)), show that x ∂u/∂x + y ∂u/∂y = 2 cot u.
questions.answer: Shown: sec u tan u (x uₓ + y uᵧ) = 2 sec u ⇒ x uₓ + y uᵧ = 2 cot u
questions.explanation: w = (x³ − y³)/(x + y) is homogeneous of degree 2, so x wₓ + y wᵧ = 2w. With sec u = w, wₓ = sec u tan u · uₓ (and likewise in y), giving sec u tan u (x uₓ + y uᵧ) = 2 sec u, i.e. x uₓ + y uᵧ = 2/tan u = 2 cot u.

questions.question: Use the bisection method to find a real root of: (i) 2x³ − 2x − 5, [1, 2], three iterations   (ii) x³ − 2x − 5, [1.5, 2.5], four iterations   (iii) x³ − x + 1, [−2, −1], five iterations   (iv) cos x, [1, 2], one decimal place (five iterations)   (v) 3x − e^x, [0, 1], three decimal places (eleven iterations)   (vi) 3x − √(1 + sin x), [0, 1], three decimal places (thirteen iterations)
Write the MAPLE command fsolve to find numerical solutions of: (i) 3x⁴y² = 17, x²y − 5xy² − 2y = 1   (ii) 3x³ − 27x + 3   (iii) 3x³ + 9x + 3   (iv) 2x³ + 4x + 2
questions.explanation: MAPLE session: > fsolve({3*x^4*y^2 = 17, x^2*y - 5*x*y^2 - 2*y = 1}, {x, y}); returns the pair in (i). > fsolve(3*x^3 - 27*x + 3, x); lists the three real roots in (ii); > fsolve(3*x^3 + 9*x + 3, x); and > fsolve(2*x^3 + 4*x + 2, x); give the single real roots in (iii) and (iv). Matches the key.

questions.question: Use the regula falsi method to find a root of x³ − 2x − 5 = 0 on [2, 3] up to three iterations.
Use the regula falsi method to find a root of sin(2x) − e^(x−1) = 0 on [−2, −1] up to four iterations.
Use the regula falsi method to find a root of x⁴ − x − 10 = 0 on [1, 2] up to two decimal places.
Use the regula falsi method to find a root of 3x + sin(x) − e^x = 0 on [0, 1] up to three decimal places.
Use the regula falsi method to find a root of 2 cos x − x = 0 on [1, 2] up to five decimal places.
Use Newton's Raphson method for f(x) = 2x³ − 2x − 5 up to three iterations with initial guess x₀ = 2.
Use Newton's Raphson method for f(x) = x³ − x − 1 up to three iterations with initial guess x₀ = 1.
Use Newton's Raphson method for f(x) = x³ − 2x − 5 up to two iterations with initial guess x₀ = 1.
questions.explanation: f(1) = −6 and f′(1) = 1 give x₁ = 7; then f(7) = 324, f′(7) = 145 give x₂ = 7 − 324/145 = 4.765517. The guess x₀ = 1 is far from the root 2.0946, so two iterations land at 4.765517 — exactly the key's value.

questions.question: Use Newton's Raphson method for f(x) = 2 cos x − x with x₀ = 0.

Select the correct option: (i) sign of f(a)f(b) when a root lies in [a, b]; (ii) the bisection approximation is which mean of the endpoints; (iii) false-position iteration formula; (iv) fastest method for a nonlinear equation; (v) Newton's method fails when f′ becomes; (vi) Newton's iteration formula; (vii) numerical integration evaluates a; (viii) trapezoidal sub-interval count is a multiple of; (ix) Simpson 1/3 sub-interval count is a multiple of; (x) fastest quadrature of the list.
questions.answer: (i) b   (ii) a   (iii) d   (iv) c   (v) c   (vi) d   (vii) a   (viii) b   (ix) c   (x) b
questions.explanation: (i) A sign change is required: f(a)f(b) < 0. (ii) The midpoint is the arithmetic mean. (iii) x = (a f(b) − b f(a))/(f(b) − f(a)). (iv) Newton's quadratic convergence makes it fastest. (v) Division by f′ fails at f′ = 0. (vi) xₙ₊₁ = xₙ − f(xₙ)/f′(xₙ). (vii) A definite integral. (viii) The trapezoidal rule accepts any n, i.e. a multiple of 1 — the key's c (= 2) is Simpson's requirement, key misprint. (ix) Simpson 1/3 needs an even number of sub-intervals. (x) Simpson 1/3 is the most accurate of the three. Key agrees except (viii).

Find a root of 2e^x sin x = 1 by the false position method, correct to three decimal places with three iterations, taking [1, 2] as the interval.
questions.explanation: f(x) = 2e^x sin x − 1 has f(1) = 3.574710 and f(2) = 12.437699, both positive, so [1, 2] contains no root; applying the false-position formula mechanically as the book does gives x₁ = 0.596670 (f = 1.040861), x₂ = 0.430989 (f = 0.285709), x₃ = 0.381561 — the key's 0.38156. The genuine root of 2e^x sin x = 1 is ≈ 0.3573 in [0, 1]; flagged in the solution file.
